label: prop:ons-onset
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:ons-onset}
Assume $\beta_2>0$, $\xi'''(0)=0$ and~\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}. Then the following hold.
\begin{thmlist}
\item As $\theta\downarrow0$: $p(\theta)\tof_{\mathrm{eq}}$, $W_1(\zeta_\theta,\zeta_*)\to0$ and
 $q_\theta\to0$.
\item There is $\theta_0\in(0,1)$ such that, for $0<\theta<\theta_0$,
 $\Gamma_\theta(t)=t$ on an interval $[q_\theta,s_\theta]$ with $s_\theta>q_\theta$. In
 particular the first positive contact is marginal:
 \[
  \Gamma_\theta'(q_\theta)
  =\xi''(q_\theta)\,\mathbb{E}\Phi_{\zeta_\theta,xx}(q_\theta,X_{q_\theta})^2=1 .
 \]
\item As $\theta\downarrow0$,
 \[
  \frac{q_\theta}{\theta}\longrightarrow\frac{3\sqrt{a_0}}{D_*}=\frac{3}{2\rho_*},
  \qquad
  \frac{\zeta_\theta(\{q_\theta\})}{\theta}\longrightarrow\frac12 .
 \]
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Marginal onset

label: lem:fifth-area
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:fifth-area}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:local}, as $\theta\downarrow0$,
\[
 p'(\theta)=\frac{a_0D_*}{144}\,q_\theta^4\,(1+o(1)).
\]
head: environment
name: The area of the first plateau

label: eq:fifth-p-prime
title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:fifth-area} and the onset limit $q_\theta/\theta\to3\sqrt{a_0}/D_*$
of item~(a),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fifth-p-prime}
\begin{split}
 p'(\theta)&=\frac{a_0D_*}{144}\,q_\theta^4\,(1+o(1))
 =\frac{a_0D_*}{144}\Bigl(\frac{3\sqrt{a_0}}{D_*}\Bigr)^4\theta^4(1+o(1))\\
 &=\frac{9a_0^3}{16D_*^3}\,\theta^4(1+o(1))
 =5c\,\theta^4(1+o(1)).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Write $p'(s)=5cs^4(1+r(s))$ with $r(s)\to0$ as $s\downarrow0$, and choose
$\theta_1\in(0,\theta_0)$ with $|r|\le1$ on $(0,\theta_1]$. Then $p$ is differentiable
at every point of $(0,\theta_1]$, with $|p'|\le10c\,\theta_1^4$ there. Hence $p$ is
Lipschitz on $(0,\theta_1]$, and $p(\theta)-p(\eta)=\int_\eta^\theta p'(s)\,ds$ for
$0<\eta<\theta\le\theta_1$. As $\eta\downarrow0$ we have $p(\eta)\tof_{\mathrm{eq}}$: the measure
$\eta\delta_0+(1-\eta)\zeta_*$ satisfies the constraint at $\eta$ and lies within
$W_1$-distance $\eta$ of $\zeta_*$, so \eqref{eq:cons-lipschitz} gives
$f_{\mathrm{eq}}\le p(\eta)\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}+\frac12\xi''(1)\eta$. Letting $\eta\downarrow0$,
\[
 \bigl|p(\theta)-f_{\mathrm{eq}}-c\,\theta^5\bigr|\le c\,\theta^5\sup_{0<s\le\theta}|r(s)|,
\]
which is $p(\theta)-f_{\mathrm{eq}}=c\,\theta^5(1+o(1))$. Since $\Lambda(\theta)=\theta p(\theta)$,
\[
 \Lambda(\theta)-\thetaf_{\mathrm{eq}}=\theta\bigl\{p(\theta)-f_{\mathrm{eq}}\bigr\}=c\,\theta^6(1+o(1)),\qquad
 \Lambda'(\theta)-f_{\mathrm{eq}}=\bigl\{p(\theta)-f_{\mathrm{eq}}\bigr\}+\theta p'(\theta)=6c\,\theta^5(1+o(1)).
 \qedhere
\]

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\zeta_*(\{0\})=0$, Corollary~\ref{cor:cons-level} with $m_0=0$ and
Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-variational}(d) give that $\Lambda$ is continuously differentiable and
strictly convex on $(0,1)$, that $\Lambda'$ maps $(0,1)$ homeomorphically onto $(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$,
that $f_{\mathrm{eq}}<f_1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-regular}(d)), and that $\theta_f=(\Lambda')^{-1}(f)$.

Now let $\delta\downarrow0$, and write $\theta_\delta=\theta_{f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta}$ for
$0<\delta<f_1-f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. Continuity of $(\Lambda')^{-1}$ gives $\theta_\delta\to0$, and by
item~(b) $\delta=\Lambda'(\theta_\delta)-f_{\mathrm{eq}}=6c\,\theta_\delta^5(1+o(1))$, so
$\theta_\delta=(\delta/(6c))^{1/5}(1+o(1))$. The infimum that defines $\Sigma(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta)$ is
attained at $\theta_\delta<1$, so
\[
 \Sigma(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta)=\bigl\{\Lambda(\theta_\delta)-\theta_\deltaf_{\mathrm{eq}}\bigr\}-\delta\,\theta_\delta
 =c\,\theta_\delta^6(1+o(1))-6c\,\theta_\delta^6(1+o(1))
 =-5c\Bigl(\frac{\delta}{6c}\Bigr)^{6/5}(1+o(1)),
\]
and $5c(6c)^{-6/5}=\frac56(6c)^{-1/5}$. The leading coefficients $c$ and $6c$ do not
cancel, so the relative errors combine as written. Since $\theta_f\to0$ as
$f\downarrowf_{\mathrm{eq}}$, the asymptotics of $q_f=q_{\theta_f}$ follow from item~(a). Finally,
put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fifth-delta0}
 \bar\delta=\Lambda'(\theta_0)-f_{\mathrm{eq}} .
\end{equation}
Then $0<\bar\delta<f_1-f_{\mathrm{eq}}$, because $\Lambda'$ is strictly increasing and $\theta_0<1$.
If $0<\delta<\bar\delta$, then $\theta_\delta<\theta_0$, and item~(a) applies to
$\zeta_{\theta_\delta}$: the first positive contact at the level $f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta$ is
marginal.

title: Proof
body_md:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:local}, $\zeta_*(\{0\})=0$, so
$\zeta_*\ne\delta_0$. By item~(c), $\Lambda$ is continuously differentiable and strictly
convex on $(0,1)$, and every level $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ has the dual minimizer
$\theta_f=(\Lambda')^{-1}(f)\in(0,1)$. With \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}, Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-gartner-ellis}
therefore gives
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(N^{-1}\logZ_N\ge f\bigr)=\Sigma(f)
 \qquad(f_{\mathrm{eq}}<f<f_1).
\]
Since $f_{\mathrm{eq}}<f_1$, the level $f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta$ lies in $(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ for
$0<\delta<f_1-f_{\mathrm{eq}}$, and then the inner limit in the second display of item~(d) equals
$-\Sigma(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta)$. By item~(c), $\delta^{-6/5}\{-\Sigma(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta)\}\to
\frac56(6c)^{-1/5}$ as $\delta\downarrow0$.

title: Proof
body_md:
The covariance $\xi(t)=\beta^2t^2/2$ is a polynomial with $\beta_2^2=\beta^2/2>0$ and
$\xi'''=\xi''''=0$. Thus $a_0=\beta^2$ and $D_*=\beta^6W_*^2$. Hypothesis~\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\
holds for every $\beta>1$ by Lopatto's theorem \cite[Proposition~5.1]{Lop26a}: his Parisi
equation and functional \cite[(1.2)--(1.3)]{Lop26a} are those of this covariance, with a
functional larger than ours by the constant $\log2$, so his Parisi measure $\mu_\beta$ is
$\zeta_*$. The same statement, for the same equation and functional, has an alternative
computer-assisted proof \cite[Theorem~5.1]{Pei26} (Remark~\ref{rem:fifth-sk-inputs}).

Theorem~\ref{thm:local} therefore applies. Its first assertions show that $\alpha_*$ is
continuously differentiable near zero, with
$\rho_\beta(0)=\alpha_*'(0)=\rho_*=D_*/(2\beta)=\beta^5W_*^2/2$, which is positive because
$W_*<0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-fourth-sign}). The constant of Theorem~\ref{thm:local} is
\[
 c=\frac9{640}\,a_0^{3/2}\rho_*^{-3}=\frac9{640}\,\beta^3\rho_\beta(0)^{-3}=c_\beta
 =\frac{9}{80\,\beta^{12}W_*^6}.
\]
Parts (a) and~(b) of Theorem~\ref{thm:sk} are items (a)--(c) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:local} with $c=c_\beta$ and $3/(2\rho_*)=3/(2\rho_\beta(0))$.

For part~(c), \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ holds for this covariance by Lemma~\ref{lem:A-fm-sk}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:local}(d) gives both limits for $Z_N$. Here $Z_N$ is the partition
function of the field with covariance $N\xi(N^{-1}\sigma\cdot\sigma')$, whose
interaction includes the diagonal terms. Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-original-sk} transfers the
first limit, at every $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$, to $N^{-1}F_{N,\beta}-\log2$. The second limit follows,
because its inner limits are again $-\Sigma(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta)$.

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:fifth-sk-inputs}
Besides the present paper, the proof uses refereed results on the Parisi functional and its
equation \cite{AC15a,AC15b,Che17} and the following inputs.
\begin{steplist}
\item \emph{Condition~\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}.} Lopatto's theorem \cite[Proposition~5.1]{Lop26a} is proved in a
 preprint, and so is the alternative proof \cite[Theorem~5.1]{Pei26}, which uses nothing from
 \cite[Sections~3--5]{Lop26a} and whose single computer-assisted step is one polynomial
 inequality, verified in exact rational arithmetic \cite[Section~5 and Appendix~A.5]{Pei26}.
 No other property of $\zeta_*$ is taken from these papers: the interval of support near
 zero, $U_*=1/\beta$ and the absence of an atom at zero are derived from~\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ in
 Proposition~\ref{prop:ons-equilibrium}. Thus, like the results of \cite{AL26} at every
 $\beta>1$, which use Lopatto's interval-support theorem \cite[Theorem~1.1]{Lop26a}, the
 statement at every $\beta>1$ rests on a preprint.
\item \emph{Condition~\hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}.} It enters only part~(c). For this covariance it is the one-level
 case of the multiscale formula of Contucci and Mingione \cite[Theorem~2.1]{CM19}, a refereed
 result (Lemma~\ref{lem:A-fm-sk}); other sources are Talagrand's argument for even covariances
 \cite[Section~7]{Tal07} and the preprints \cite[Theorem~2.1]{CGKLM} and, quantitatively for
 $\theta\le\frac12$, \cite[Theorem~1.1]{AL26}. Its upper half is Guerra's bound for fractional
 moments \cite[Section~6]{Tal07} (Proposition~\ref{prop:A-guerra}).
\item \emph{Temperatures close to critical.} If $1<\beta^2<1+\varepsilon_*$, with
 $\varepsilon_*$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:nearcrit}(a), then $\xi\in\mathcal{K}(\varepsilon_*)$, because
 $\|\xi-\xi_c\|_{C^4[0,1]}=\beta^2-1$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:nearcrit}(a) proves~\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ within this
 paper, from refereed results only (Proposition~\ref{prop:nc-class}). For $\beta$ close to $1$,
 \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ also follows from Zhou's theorem \cite[Theorem~1]{Zho26}, which is stated for the
 covariance $\beta_Z^2t^2$ with $\frac1{\sqrt2}<\beta_Z\le\frac1{\sqrt2}+\eta$ for some
 $\eta>0$, that is, for $\beta=\sqrt2\beta_Z\in(1,1+\sqrt2\eta]$; we use only its inclusion
 $[0,\upsilon_\beta]\subset\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$. For these $\beta$, Theorem~\ref{thm:sk} rests on
 refereed results and the present paper alone.
\end{steplist}
For this model, Proposition~\ref{prop:ons-equilibrium}(b) is
\cite[Lemmas~6.1 and~6.2]{Lop26a}, and by \cite[Theorem~1.1]{Lop26a} $\zeta_*$ has a smooth
density on $[0,q_\beta)$, where $q_\beta$ is the top of its support, whose value at zero is
therefore $\rho_\beta(0)$; this is not used here. The value and the positivity of $\rho_\beta(0)$, in physics
form \cite[(B9)--(B10)]{PR09} of Crisanti and Rizzo~\cite{CR02}, also follow from
\cite[Theorem~B.1 and (B.4)]{Lop26b}, which uses the interval support of $\zeta_*$, and from
\cite[(7.8), (7.10) and (7.12)]{AL26} on differentiation at zero and
\cite[Lemma~7.1, (7.7), and Lemma~7.2]{AL26} (Section~\ref{sec:intro-results}).

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:fifth-al}
For every fixed $\beta>1$, Aronow and Lopatto prove
$e^{-C_1Nx^{6/5}}\le\mathbb{P}(F_{N,\beta}\ge N(P_\beta+x))\le e^{-C_2Nx^{6/5}}$, where
$P_\beta=f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\log2$, at finite $N\ge N_0(\beta)$ and for $A_\beta N^{-2/3}\le x\le x_\beta$,
with positive constants depending on $\beta$ \cite[Theorem~1.5]{AL26} (uniformly in $\beta\ge2$
for $F_{N,\beta}/\beta$, with a ground-state counterpart \cite[Theorem~1.6 and (1.14)]{AL26}). By
Theorem~\ref{thm:sk}(c), $x^{-6/5}\lim_{N}N^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}(F_{N,\beta}\ge N(P_\beta+x))\to
-\frac56(6c_\beta)^{-1/5}$ as $x\downarrow0$. They also prove that the constrained minimum increases
by an amount of order $\lambda^5$ \cite[Lemma~7.2 and Proposition~7.3]{AL26}; in their rescaled
variables \cite[Section~7]{AL26}, $E_\beta(\lambda)=\beta^{-1}P_\beta(\lambda/\beta)$, where
$P_\beta(s)=p(s)+\log2$, and $u_\beta(q,x)=\beta^{-1}\Phi_{\zeta_*}(q,\beta x)$ up to an additive
constant, so that $u_{\beta,xxxx}(0,0)=\beta^3W_*$; Theorem~\ref{thm:sk}(a) reads
\[
 \lim_{\lambda\downarrow0}\lambda^{-5}\bigl(E_\beta(\lambda)-E_\beta(0)\bigr)
 =c_\beta\,\beta^{-6}=\frac9{80}\,u_{\beta,xxxx}(0,0)^{-6}.
\]
Section~\ref{sec:intro-results} compares the scope of the two results.

label: cor:fifth-plefka
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:fifth-plefka}
Assume the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:local}; by the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:sk}, they hold for $\xi(t)=\beta^2t^2/2$ with $\beta>1$. Let $\bar\delta$
be as in \eqref{eq:fifth-delta0}.
Every level $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\bar\delta)$ is regular, and $\Gamma_{\zeta_f}(t)=t$ on an
interval $[q_f,s_f]$ with $s_f>q_f$. In particular
\[
 1-\xi''(q_f)\,\mathbb{E}\Phi_{\zeta_f,xx}(q_f,X_{q_f})^2=0,
\]
so the strict Plefka condition \cite[(1.8)]{Bou26b} fails at every level in
$(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\bar\delta)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:local}(c), every $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ has the unique dual minimizer
$\theta_f=(\Lambda')^{-1}(f)$, so it is regular. If $f<f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\bar\delta=\Lambda'(\theta_0)$,
then $\theta_f<\theta_0$, because $\Lambda'$ is increasing. Theorem~\ref{thm:local}(a)
at $\theta=\theta_f$ gives $\Gamma_{\zeta_f}=\mathrm{id}$ on $[q_f,s_f]$ with $s_f>q_f$. Hence
$\Gamma'_{\zeta_f}(q_f)=1$, and the It\^o identity
$\Gamma_\zeta'(t)=\xi''(t)\mathbb{E}\Phi_{\zeta,xx}(t,X_t)^2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-ito}) gives the
displayed equality.

label: lem:cons-standard
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:cons-standard}
Let $\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item \emph{Regularity.} For every $j\ge0$ the derivative $\partial_x^j\Phi_\zeta$ exists and
 is continuous on $[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$. The function $\Phi_\zeta(t,\cdot)$ is even, and
 $|\Phi_{\zeta,x}|\le1$, $0<\Phi_{\zeta,xx}\le1$. If $\zeta_n\Rightarrow\zeta$, then
 $\partial_x^j\Phi_{\zeta_n}\to\partial_x^j\Phi_\zeta$ uniformly on $[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$ for every
 $j\ge0$.
\item \emph{The function $\Gamma_\zeta$.} $\Gamma_\zeta$ is continuously differentiable on
 $[0,1]$, with
 \[
  \Gamma_\zeta'(t)=\xi''(t)\,\mathbb{E}\Phi_{\zeta,xx}(t,X_t)^2,\qquad
  \Gamma_\zeta(0)=0,\qquad 0\le\Gamma_\zeta\le1,\qquad \Gamma_\zeta(1)<1 .
 \]
 If $\zeta_n\Rightarrow\zeta$, then $\Gamma_{\zeta_n}\to\Gamma_\zeta$,
 $\Gamma_{\zeta_n}'\to\Gamma_\zeta'$ and $\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_n}\to\mathcal{O}_\zeta$ uniformly on $[0,1]$.
\item \emph{Convexity.} The map $\zeta\mapsto P_\zeta$ is strictly convex on $\mathcal{P}([0,1])$
 and has a unique minimizer $\zeta_*$.
\item \emph{First variation.} For $\nu\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ and $s\in[0,1]$ put
 $\zeta_s=(1-s)\zeta+s\nu$. The function $s\mapsto P_{\zeta_s}$ is convex and continuously
 differentiable on $[0,1]$, with one-sided derivatives at the endpoints, and
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:cons-first-variation}
  \frac{d}{ds}P_{\zeta_s}=\int\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_s}\,d(\nu-\zeta)
  =\frac12\int_0^1\xi''(t)\bigl\{\alpha_\nu(t)-\alpha_\zeta(t)\bigr\}
   \bigl\{\Gamma_{\zeta_s}(t)-t\bigr\}\,dt .
 \end{equation}
\item \emph{Lipschitz bound.} For $\mu,\nu\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$,
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:cons-lipschitz}
  |P_\mu-P_\nu|\le\tfrac12\,\xi''(1)\,W_1(\mu,\nu).
 \end{equation}
 In particular $\zeta\mapsto P_\zeta$ is weakly continuous.
\item \emph{The obstacle.} $\mathcal{O}_\zeta\in C^2[0,1]$, $\mathcal{O}_\zeta(1)=0$, and
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:cons-obstacle}
  \mathcal{O}_\zeta'=-\tfrac12\,\xi''\,(\Gamma_\zeta-\mathrm{id}),\qquad
  \mathcal{O}_\zeta''=-\tfrac12\,\xi'''\,(\Gamma_\zeta-\mathrm{id})-\tfrac12\,\xi''\,(\Gamma_\zeta'-1),
  \qquad \mathcal{O}_\zeta'(1)>0 .
 \end{equation}
 Consequently $1$ is not a minimum point of $\mathcal{O}_\zeta$ on $(0,1]$, and every minimum point
 $t\in(0,1)$ of $\mathcal{O}_\zeta$ on $(0,1]$ satisfies $\Gamma_\zeta(t)=t$ and
 $\Gamma_\zeta'(t)\le1$.
\item \emph{Optimality of $\zeta_*$.} Put $o_*=\int\mathcal{O}_*\,d\zeta_*$. Then
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:cons-optimality}
  \mathcal{O}_*\ge o_*\ \text{ on }[0,1],\qquad \mathcal{O}_*=o_*\ \text{ on }\operatorname{supp}\zeta_* .
 \end{equation}
 Conversely, if $\int\mathcal{O}_\zeta\,d(\nu-\zeta)\ge0$ for every $\nu\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$, then
 $\zeta=\zeta_*$.
\end{thmlist}

label: lem:cons-variational
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:cons-variational}
The following hold.
\begin{thmlist}
\item For every $\theta\in[0,1)$, $P$ has a unique minimizer $\zeta_\theta$ on
 $\mathcal A_\theta$, and $\zeta_\theta=\zeta_*$ if $\theta\le m_0$. The function
 $p(\theta)=P_{\zeta_\theta}$ is continuous and nondecreasing on $[0,1)$, with
 $f_{\mathrm{eq}}\le p(\theta)\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}+\tfrac12\,\xi''(1)\,\theta$, and $\theta\mapsto\zeta_\theta$ is weakly
 continuous on $[0,1)$.
\item $\overline{\Lambda}$ is closed and convex, $\overline{\Lambda}'_+(0)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$,
 $\overline{\Lambda}(1)=\lim_{\theta\uparrow1}\Lambda(\theta)=P_{\delta_0}$, and $f_1<\infty$.
\item \emph{Saturation.} If $m_0<\theta<1$, then $\zeta_\theta(\{0\})=\theta$. The function $p$ is
 strictly increasing on $[m_0,1)$, and $\Lambda$ is strictly convex on $[m_0,1)$.
\item \emph{Dual minimizer.} For every $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$, the function
 $\theta\mapsto\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta f$ has a unique minimizer $\theta_f$ on $[0,1]$, and
 $\theta_f\in(0,1)\cap[m_0,1)$.
\item \emph{First contact.} Let $m_0<\theta<1$, write
 $\zeta_\theta=\theta\delta_0+(1-\theta)\mu_\theta$, and put
 $o_\theta=\int\mathcal{O}_\theta\,d\mu_\theta$. Then $\mathcal{O}_\theta\ge o_\theta$ on $[0,1]$,
 $\mathcal{O}_\theta=o_\theta$ on $\operatorname{supp}\mu_\theta$, and $\mathcal{O}_\theta(0)>o_\theta$. The positive
 contact set
 \[
  C_\theta=\Bigl\{t\in(0,1]:\mathcal{O}_\theta(t)=\min_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}_\theta\Bigr\}
 \]
 is a nonempty compact subset of $(0,1)$ that contains $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_\theta\cap(0,1]$. Its
 smallest point $q_\theta$ satisfies
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:cons-contact}
  \zeta_\theta((0,q_\theta))=0,\qquad \Gamma_\theta(q_\theta)=q_\theta,\qquad
  \Gamma_\theta'(q_\theta)=\xi''(q_\theta)\,
  \mathbb{E}\Phi_{\zeta_\theta,xx}(q_\theta,X_{q_\theta})^2\le1,
 \end{equation}
 where $X$ is the diffusion of $\zeta_\theta$, and $\mathcal{O}_\theta(r)>\mathcal{O}_\theta(q_\theta)$ for
 $0\le r<q_\theta$.
\end{thmlist}

name: The constrained problem

title: Proof
body_md:
For $u\in[0,1)$ and $\mu\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ put $\pi(u,\mu)=P_{u\delta_0+(1-u)\mu}$. Then
$p(u)=\min_\mu\pi(u,\mu)$, with the unique minimizer $\mu_u=(\zeta_u-u\delta_0)/(1-u)$, and
$u\mapsto\mu_u$ is weakly continuous by Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-variational}(a). For fixed $\mu$,
$u\mapsto u\delta_0+(1-u)\mu$ is a segment, and \eqref{eq:cons-first-variation} gives
\[
 \partial_u\pi(u,\mu)=\int\mathcal{O}_{u\delta_0+(1-u)\mu}\,d(\delta_0-\mu)\qquad(0<u<1).
\]
This is jointly continuous in $(u,\mu)$. Indeed, if $u_n\to u$ and $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$, the
corresponding obstacles converge uniformly by Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-standard}(b), and
$\int\mathcal{O}\,d\mu_n\to\int\mathcal{O}\,d\mu$ for every continuous $\mathcal{O}$.

Fix $\theta\in(0,1)$ and a small $h\ne0$. Since $p(\theta)=\pi(\theta,\mu_\theta)
\le\pi(\theta,\mu_{\theta+h})$ and $p(\theta+h)=\pi(\theta+h,\mu_{\theta+h})
\le\pi(\theta+h,\mu_\theta)$,
\[
 \pi(\theta+h,\mu_{\theta+h})-\pi(\theta,\mu_{\theta+h})
 \le p(\theta+h)-p(\theta)
 \le\pi(\theta+h,\mu_\theta)-\pi(\theta,\mu_\theta).
\]
By the mean value theorem the outer terms equal $h\,\partial_u\pi(u',\mu_{\theta+h})$ and
$h\,\partial_u\pi(u'',\mu_\theta)$ for some $u',u''$ between $\theta$ and $\theta+h$. Divide by
$h$; for $h<0$ this reverses both inequalities. As $h\to0$, joint continuity and
$\mu_{\theta+h}\Rightarrow\mu_\theta$ show that both bounds converge to
$\partial_u\pi(\theta,\mu_\theta)$. Hence $p$ is differentiable at $\theta$, and
$p'(\theta)=\partial_u\pi(\theta,\mu_\theta)$, which is \eqref{eq:cons-envelope-general}
because $\theta\delta_0+(1-\theta)\mu_\theta=\zeta_\theta$. The same joint continuity makes
$p'$ continuous.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-variational}(a), $p$ is constant on $[0,m_0]$; since $p$ is
differentiable, $p'=0$ on $(0,1)\cap(0,m_0]$. Let $m_0<\theta<1$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-variational}(e), $\mathcal{O}_\theta$ equals $o_\theta=\mathcal{O}_\theta(q_\theta)$ on
$\operatorname{supp}\mu_\theta$, so $\int\mathcal{O}_\theta\,d\mu_\theta=\mathcal{O}_\theta(q_\theta)$, and
$\mathcal{O}_\theta(0)>\mathcal{O}_\theta(q_\theta)$. The integral form follows from
\eqref{eq:intro-obstacle}. The last assertion follows from $\Lambda(\theta)=\theta p(\theta)$.

label: lem:plat-obstacle
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:plat-obstacle}
Let $\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$, $\Gamma=\Gamma_\zeta$ and $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}_\zeta$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item $\mathcal{O}\in C^2[0,1]$, with $\mathcal{O}'(t)=-\tfrac12a(t)\bigl(\Gamma(t)-t\bigr)$ and
 $\mathcal{O}''(t)=-\tfrac12a'(t)\bigl(\Gamma(t)-t\bigr)-\tfrac12a(t)\bigl(\Gamma'(t)-1\bigr)$.
 Moreover $\mathcal{O}'(1)>0$, so $1$ is not a minimum point of $\mathcal{O}$ on $[0,1]$.
\item At every local minimum point $t\in(0,1)$ of
 $\mathcal{O}$,
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:plat-contact}
  \Gamma(t)=t,\qquad \Gamma'(t)=\xi''(t)\,\mathbb{E}\Phi_{\zeta,xx}(t,X_t)^2\le1 .

head: environment

label: lem:plat-fourth-sign
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:plat-fourth-sign}
Let $\xi(t)=\sum_{p\ge2}\beta_p^2t^p$ be not identically zero, with radius of convergence
greater than one. Put $T_t=\xi'(1)-\xi'(t)$, let $\varphi_T$ be the $\mathcal N(0,T)$
density, and set
\[
 c_1=\min\bigl\{2\tanh y\,\operatorname{sech}^2y:\ 1\le y\le2+\xi'(1)\bigr\},\qquad
 \kappa_t=\frac{c_1\,\varphi_{T_t}(5/2)}{T_t}>0\qquad(0\le t<1).
\]
For every $\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$, $0\le t<1$ and $0\le x\le\frac12$,
\[
 \Phi_{\zeta,xxx}(t,x)\le-\kappa_tx,\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
 \Phi_{\zeta,xxxx}(t,0)\le-\kappa_t<0 .
\]
In particular $W_*\le-\kappa_0$. If $\beta_2>0$, then the constant
$D_*=\xi''''(0)U_*^2+a_0^3W_*^2$ of Section~\ref{sec:intro-constrained} satisfies
$D_*\gea_0^3\kappa_0^2>0$.
head: environment
name: Universal sign

title: Proof
body_md:
First let $\zeta$ have finitely many atoms, and write $u=\Phi_{\zeta,x}$,
$U=\Phi_{\zeta,xx}$, $V=\Phi_{\zeta,xxx}$ and $\alpha=\alpha_\zeta$. On each closed strip
between consecutive atoms, $V$ solves the last equation of \eqref{eq:plat-third-pde}, with
$m$ the height of the strip. Fix $t<1$ and $0<x\le\frac12$. Let $Y$ solve
\[
 dY_s=a(s)\alpha(s)u(s,Y_s)\,ds+\sqrt{a(s)}\,dB_s\qquad(t\le s\le1),\qquad Y_t=x ;
\]
the drift is bounded and Lipschitz in space, since $|u|\le1$ and $0<u_x\le1$. Put
$c(s,y)=3a(s)\alpha(s)U(s,y)\ge0$. By It\^o's formula on each strip,
\[
 M_s=V(s,Y_s)\exp\Bigl\{\int_t^sc(r,Y_r)\,dr\Bigr\}
\]
is a continuous martingale on $[t,1]$, bounded by $B_3e^{3\xi'(1)}$; it is continuous
across atoms because $V$ is continuous in time. Let $\tau=\inf\{s\ge t:Y_s=0\}$. Since $V$
is odd in $x$, $V(s,0)=0$, and optional stopping gives
\[
 V(t,x)=\mathbb{E} M_{\tau\wedge1}
 =\mathbb{E}\Bigl[V(1,Y_1)\,e^{\int_t^1c(r,Y_r)\,dr};\ \tau>1\Bigr].
\]
On $\{\tau>1\}$ we have $Y_1>0$, so $V(1,Y_1)=-2\tanh Y_1\operatorname{sech}^2Y_1<0$, while the
exponential factor is at least one. Therefore $V(t,x)\le\mathbb{E}[V(1,Y_1);A]$ for every event
$A\subset\{\tau>1\}$.

Let $\widetilde Y_s=x+\int_t^s\sqrt{a(r)}\,dB_r$. The function $u(s,\cdot)$ is odd and
increasing, so $u(s,y)\ge0$ for $y\ge0$. Hence, for $t\le s\le\tau\wedge1$,
$0\le Y_s-\widetilde Y_s=\int_t^sa(r)\alpha(r)u(r,Y_r)\,dr\le\xi'(1)$.
If $\widetilde Y$ stays positive on $[t,1]$, then $\tau>1$, for otherwise
$\widetilde Y_\tau\le Y_\tau=0$. Take
$A=\{\widetilde Y_s>0\ \text{for}\ t\le s\le1,\ \widetilde Y_1\in[1,2]\}$.
Then $A\subset\{\tau>1\}$ and $Y_1\in[1,2+\xi'(1)]$ on $A$, so $V(t,x)\le-c_1\mathbb{P}(A)$.
The process $\widetilde Y$ is a Brownian motion started at $x$ and run with the clock
$\xi'(s)-\xi'(t)$, which reaches $T=T_t>0$ at $s=1$ because $\xi''>0$ on $(0,1]$. The
reflection principle gives
$\mathbb{P}(A)=\int_1^2\{\varphi_T(y-x)-\varphi_T(y+x)\}\,dy$. For $y\in[1,2]$ and $0<x\le\frac12$,
\[
 \varphi_T(y-x)-\varphi_T(y+x)=\int_{-x}^x\frac{y+r}T\,\varphi_T(y+r)\,dr
 \ge\frac xT\,\varphi_T(5/2),
\]
because $y+r\in[\frac12,\frac52]$. Hence $V(t,x)\le-\kappa_tx$.

For a general $\zeta$, choose measures $\zeta_n$ with finitely many atoms and
$\zeta_n\to\zeta$ weakly. The constant $\kappa_t$ does not depend on $n$, and
$\Phi_{\zeta_n,xxx}\to\Phi_{\zeta,xxx}$ uniformly~\cite[Proposition~1(i)]{AC15a}, so the
inequality passes to the limit. Finally $V(t,0)=0$ and $V(t,\cdot)$ is continuously
differentiable, so $\Phi_{\zeta,xxxx}(t,0)=\lim_{x\downarrow0}V(t,x)/x\le-\kappa_t$. At
$t=0$ and $\zeta=\zeta_*$ this is $W_*\le-\kappa_0$; since $\xi''''(0)\ge0$, the last
assertion follows.
head: environment

label: rem:plat-sign
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:plat-sign}
The non-strict sign $\Phi_{\zeta,xxx}(t,x)\le0$ for $t,x>0$ and every $\zeta$
is~\cite[(7.6)]{Lop26a} for the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick equation; the time change
$t\mapsto\xi'(t)/\xi'(1)$, which turns the Parisi equation of $\xi$ into that of the
Sherrington--Kirkpatrick covariance with $\beta^2=\xi'(1)$, carries it to every $\xi$. A
Feynman--Kac proof for the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick equation is in~\cite[Lemma~5.4]{Pei26},
a maximum-principle proof for a regularized zero-temperature equation
in~\cite[Lemma~3.4 and Appendix~B.3]{Che26}, and for the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick minimizer
Aronow and Lopatto prove $-\beta^3W_*\ge c_0>0$, uniformly in $\beta\ge\beta_0>1$, by
parabolic comparison~\cite[Lemma~7.1, (7.7)]{AL26}. We use the strict bound at the origin with
an explicit constant, for every covariance: it makes $D_*>0$ automatic in
Theorems~\ref{thm:local} and~\ref{thm:field} (Remark~\ref{rem:fld-nondegeneracy}). Thus
$D_*>0$ comes from $W_*<0$; the term $\xi''''(0)U_*^2$ only adds to it.

label: lem:plat-local-plateau
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:plat-local-plateau}
Assume $\xi'''(0)=0$. There is $C_\Psi$, depending only on $\xi$, such that
\[
 \bigl|\Psi_\zeta(t,m)-D_*-6m^2a_0^3U_*^4\bigr|
 \le C_\Psi\bigl(t^{1/2}+W_1(\zeta,\zeta_*)\bigr)
\]
for all $\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$, $t\in[0,1]$ and $m\in[0,1]$. Consequently there are
$K_{\rm loc}\in(0,1)$ and $r_{\rm loc}>0$ with the following property: if
$W_1(\zeta,\zeta_*)<r_{\rm loc}$ and $(u,v)\subset(0,K_{\rm loc})$ is an open interval with
$\zeta((u,v))=0$, then $\Gamma_\zeta'''\geD_*/2$ on $(u,v)$.
head: environment
name: Local plateau positivity

title: Proof
body_md:
For $k=2,3,4$ put $J_k(t)=\partial_x^k\Phi_\zeta(t,X^\zeta_t)$ and
$j_k=\partial_x^k\Phi_{\zeta_*}(0,0)$, so that $j_3=0$ by parity. By \eqref{eq:plat-origin}
with $\nu=\zeta_*$, $\mathbb{E}|J_k(t)-j_k|\le C(t^{1/2}+W_1(\zeta,\zeta_*))$ for $t\le1$, with $C$
depending only on $\xi$. The quantity $\Psi_\zeta(t,m)$ is a polynomial in $a(t)$, $a'(t)$,
$a''(t)$, $m$ and expectations of monomials of degree at most four in $J_2,J_3,J_4$, all
bounded by the constants $B_k$; the functions $a$, $a'$, $a''$ are Lipschitz on $[0,1]$.
Replacing each $J_k(t)$ by $j_k$ and each $a^{(i)}(t)$ by $a^{(i)}(0)$ therefore changes
$\Psi_\zeta(t,m)$ by at most $C_\Psi(t^{1/2}+W_1(\zeta,\zeta_*))$, uniformly in
$m\in[0,1]$, and the result is
\[
 \xi''''(0)U_*^2+3a_0\xi'''(0)\bigl(0-2mU_*^3\bigr)
 +a_0^3\bigl(W_*^2+6m^2U_*^4\bigr)=D_*+6m^2a_0^3U_*^4,
\]
since $\xi'''(0)=0$. Choose $K_{\rm loc}\in(0,1)$ and $r_{\rm loc}>0$ with
$C_\Psi(K_{\rm loc}^{1/2}+r_{\rm loc})\leD_*/2$. If $\zeta((u,v))=0$, then $(u,v)$ is a
plateau of some height $m\in[0,1]$, and
$\Gamma_\zeta'''=\Psi_\zeta(\cdot,m)\geD_*+6m^2a_0^3U_*^4-D_*/2\geD_*/2$
there.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:plat-local-gap}
Assume $\xi'''(0)=0$, and let $K_{\rm loc},r_{\rm loc}$ be as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-local-plateau}. Let $W_1(\zeta,\zeta_*)<r_{\rm loc}$, and let

name: Gap exclusion

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-obstacle}(b), $\Gamma_\zeta(u)=u$, $\Gamma_\zeta(v)=v$ and
$\Gamma_\zeta'(u),\Gamma_\zeta'(v)\le1$. If $\zeta((u,v))=0$, then
Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-local-plateau} gives $\Gamma_\zeta'''\geD_*/2>0$ on $(u,v)$, so

label: lem:plat-kernel
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Two identities on a plateau

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $g'''$ is bounded, $g''$ is Lipschitz on $(0,q)$ and extends continuously to the
endpoints. Integration by parts gives $\int_0^qtg''(t)\,dt=qg'(q)-g(q)+g(0)=0$, and
inserting $g''(t)=g''(0+)+\int_0^tg'''(s)\,ds$ gives the second form of
\eqref{eq:plat-onset-identity}. For \eqref{eq:plat-kernel}, the conditions $g(q)=g'(q)=0$
give $g(s)=\int_s^q(u-s)g''(u)\,du$, and Fubini's theorem gives
$\int_0^qg=\frac12\int_0^qu^2g''(u)\,du$. Since $\int_0^qug''(u)\,du=0$, we may subtract
$\frac q3$ times it:
\[
 \int_0^qg=\int_0^q\Bigl(\frac{u^2}2-\frac{qu}3\Bigr)g''(u)\,du
 =-\int_0^qJ'(u)\,g''(u)\,du=\int_0^qJ(u)\,g'''(u)\,du,
\]
because $J(0)=J(q)=0$ and $g''$ is bounded. Finally
$\int_0^qJ=\frac16(\frac{q^4}3-\frac{q^4}4)=\frac{q^4}{72}$.
head: environment

label: lem:plat-cubic
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:plat-cubic}
Let $g$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-kernel}, let $D\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $\varepsilon$ satisfy
$\varepsilon\ge\sup_{0<t<q}|g'''(t)-D|$. Then, for $0<t<q$,
\[
 \bigl|g''(t)-h_D''(t)\bigr|\le\frac53\,\varepsilon q,\qquad
 \bigl|g(t)-h_D(t)\bigr|\le\frac56\,\varepsilon q\,(q-t)^2 .
\]
In particular
\[
 \Bigl|g''(0+)+\frac23Dq\Bigr|\le\frac23\,\varepsilon q,\qquad
 \Bigl|g''(q-)-\frac13Dq\Bigr|\le\frac53\,\varepsilon q,\qquad
 \Bigl|\int_0^qg-\frac{Dq^4}{72}\Bigr|\le\frac{\varepsilon q^4}{72}.
\]
head: environment
name: The universal cubic

title: Proof
body_md:
The function $e=g-h_D$ satisfies the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-kernel} with
$|e'''|\le\varepsilon$. By \eqref{eq:plat-onset-identity} applied to $e$,
$|e''(0+)|\le q^{-2}\varepsilon\int_0^q(q^2-s^2)\,ds=\frac23\varepsilon q$. Then
$e''(t)=e''(0+)+\int_0^te'''$ gives $|e''(t)|\le\frac23\varepsilon q+\varepsilon t
\le\frac53\varepsilon q$, and $e(t)=\int_t^q(u-t)e''(u)\,du$ gives
$|e(t)|\le\frac56\varepsilon q(q-t)^2$. The area bound is \eqref{eq:plat-kernel} applied
to $e$, with $J\ge0$.

title: Corollary
head: environment
name: The first plateau

title: Proof
body_md:
On $[0,q)$ we have $\alpha_\zeta=m$, so $(0,q)$ is a plateau of height $m$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-ito}, $g=\Gamma_\zeta-\mathrm{id}$ is in $C^1[0,q]$ and three times
continuously differentiable on $(0,q)$, with $g'''=\Gamma_\zeta'''=\Psi_\zeta(\cdot,m)$
bounded by \eqref{eq:plat-bounds}; thus $\varepsilon<\infty$. Also $g(0)=0$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-ito}(a), and $g(q)=g'(q)=0$ because $\Gamma_\zeta=\mathrm{id}$ on $[q,s]$.
The end values of $g''$ are one-sided derivatives of $\Gamma_\zeta'$, by the mean value
theorem. At zero, $g''(0+)$ is given by \eqref{eq:plat-zero} with $\zeta(\{0\})=m$. At
$q$, the right derivative of $\Gamma_\zeta'$ vanishes because $\Gamma_\zeta'=1$ on
$[q,s]$, so \eqref{eq:plat-jump} gives $g''(q-)=2a(q)^2\zeta(\{q\})\mathbb{E} U_q^3$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-cubic} now gives (a)--(c). The bound on $\varepsilon$ is
Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-local-plateau}, since $t<q$ on the plateau.

label: lem:ons-zero-in-support
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:ons-zero-in-support}
Let $\xi(t)=\sum_{p\ge2}\beta_p^2t^p$ be not identically zero, with radius of convergence
greater than one. Then $0\in\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$ and $1\notin\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$. The obstacle $\mathcal{O}_*$

head: environment
name: Zero lies in the support

label: rem:ons-H-no-atom
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:ons-H-no-atom}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:ons-zero-in-support}, every neighbourhood of zero has positive
$\zeta_*$-mass. Condition~\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ asks for more: zero is not an isolated point of
$\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$, or equivalently $\zeta_*((0,\varepsilon))>0$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. If
$\zeta_*(\{0\})=0$, then~\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ follows from the lemma, because
$\zeta_*((0,\varepsilon))=\zeta_*([0,\varepsilon))>0$. If $\xi'''(0)=0$, the converse also
holds:~\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ implies $\zeta_*(\{0\})=0$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:ons-equilibrium}(b) under
the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:local}, and Theorem~\ref{thm:atom}(b) in general). So
when $\xi'''(0)=0$, condition~\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ says exactly that $\zeta_*$ has no atom at zero. If
$\xi'''(0)>0$, condition~\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ forces an atom at zero, of the size given in
Theorem~\ref{thm:atom}(b), and the two conditions separate: the near-critical mixtures with
a cubic term ($\beta_3>0$) of Theorem~\ref{thm:atom}(c) satisfy~\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ and have
$\zeta_*(\{0\})>0$. Where~\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ is known to hold or fail, with its sources, is recorded in
Section~\ref{sec:intro-constrained}.

name: The condition \textup{(H

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:ons-zero-in-support}, every point of $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*\cap(0,1)$ is an
interior minimum of $\mathcal{O}_*$, at which $\Gamma_*=\mathrm{id}$ and $\Gamma_*'\le1$.

(a) By~\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ there is $s_1\in\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*\cap(0,K_{\rm loc})$. Suppose that some
$t\in(0,s_1)$ is not in $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$. By~\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}, the support has points in $(0,t)$. Put
$u=\max(\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*\cap[0,t])$ and $v=\min(\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*\cap[t,s_1])$. Then $0<u<t<v\le s_1$
and $\zeta_*((u,v))=0$. The points $u,v\in(0,K_{\rm loc})$ are minima of $\mathcal{O}_*$ with
$\Gamma_*(u)=u$, $\Gamma_*(v)=v$, $\Gamma_*'(u)\le1$ and $\Gamma_*'(v)\le1$. Since
$W_1(\zeta_*,\zeta_*)=0<r_{\rm loc}$, this contradicts Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-local-gap}. Hence
$(0,s_1]\subset\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$. The support is closed, so $[0,s_1]\subset\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$; put
$\kappa=s_1$.

(b) By~(a), $\Gamma_*(t)=t$ for $0<t\le\kappa$, and $\Gamma_*(0)=\Phi_{\zeta_*,x}(0,0)^2=0$ by
oddness. Since $\Gamma_*$ is continuously differentiable, $\Gamma_*'\equiv1$ on
$[0,\kappa]$. At $t=0$ we have $X_0=0$, so $1=\Gamma_*'(0)=a_0U_*^2$; since
$U_*>0$, $U_*=a_0^{-1/2}$. The right derivative of $\Gamma_*'$ at zero is
therefore zero. By the right-derivative formula of Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-ito}(b) at $t=0$ it
equals
\[
 \xi'''(0)U_*^2+a_0^2\bigl(\Phi_{\zeta_*,xxx}(0,0)^2-2\zeta_*(\{0\})U_*^3\bigr)
 =-2a_0^2\zeta_*(\{0\})U_*^3,
\]
because $\xi'''(0)=0$ and $\Phi_{\zeta_*,xxx}(0,0)=0$ by oddness. Since $U_*>0$, we get
$\zeta_*(\{0\})=0$.

(c) Put $A_2(t)=\mathbb{E} U_t^2$, $A_3(t)=\mathbb{E} U_t^3$ and $B(t)=\mathbb{E} V_t^2$, so that, in the
notation~\eqref{eq:plat-NS}, $N_{\zeta_*}=a'A_2+a^2B$ and $\sigma_{\zeta_*}=2a^2A_3$. Since
$0<U_t\le1$, Jensen's inequality gives $A_3\ge A_2^{3/2}>0$. For $0\le s\le t\le1$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ons-moments}
\begin{aligned}
 A_2(t)-A_2(s)&=\int_s^ta(\tau)\,\mathbb{E}\bigl(V_\tau^2-2\alpha_*(\tau)U_\tau^3\bigr)\,d\tau,\\
 A_3(t)-A_3(s)&=3\int_s^ta(\tau)\,\mathbb{E}\bigl(U_\tau V_\tau^2-\alpha_*(\tau)U_\tau^4\bigr)\,d\tau,\\
 B(t)-B(s)&=\int_s^ta(\tau)\,\mathbb{E}\bigl(W_\tau^2-6\alpha_*(\tau)U_\tau V_\tau^2\bigr)\,d\tau .
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
For a measure with finitely many atoms these identities follow from It\^o's formula: on an
interval where the distribution function equals a constant $m$, the processes $U$ and $V$
solve the stochastic differential equations stated after~\eqref{eq:plat-third-pde}, and
$U,V,W$ are continuous across atoms. For $\zeta_*$ the identities follow by approximation with
finitely atomic measures, using the jet stability~\eqref{eq:plat-jet-stability} of
Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-jets}(a) and the coupling continuity of Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-coupling}.

By~(a) and~(b), $aA_2=\Gamma_*'\equiv1$ on $[0,\kappa]$. The function $A_2$ is
absolutely continuous, and at almost every $t\in(0,\kappa)$ its derivative is the
integrand in~\eqref{eq:ons-moments}. Differentiating $aA_2\equiv1$ at such $t$ gives
$a'A_2+a^2(B-2\alpha_* A_3)=0$, that is, $\alpha_*(t)=\psi(t)$ with
$\psi=N_{\zeta_*}/\sigma_{\zeta_*}=(a'A_2+a^2B)/(2a^2A_3)$. The functions $A_2,A_3,B$ are
continuous by~\eqref{eq:ons-moments}, and $a>0$ and $A_3>0$, so $\psi$ is continuous on
$[0,\kappa]$. Since $\alpha_*$ is right continuous, approximating
$t\in[0,\kappa)$ from the right through such points gives $\alpha_*(t)=\psi(t)$ for every
$t\in[0,\kappa)$. This is~\eqref{eq:ons-quotient}. Now $\alpha_*$ is continuous on
$[0,\kappa)$, so the integrands in~\eqref{eq:ons-moments} are continuous there. Hence
$A_2,A_3,B$ are continuously differentiable on $[0,\kappa)$, and so is $\alpha_*=\psi$.

At $t=0$, the numerator $N_{\zeta_*}$ vanishes, since $a'(0)=\xi'''(0)=0$ and
$B(0)=\Phi_{\zeta_*,xxx}(0,0)^2=0$. The terms of $N_{\zeta_*}'(0)$ that contain $a'(0)$ vanish,
so
\[
 N_{\zeta_*}'(0)=a''(0)A_2(0)+a_0^2B'(0)=\xi''''(0)U_*^2+a_0^3W_*^2=D_* ,
\]
by~\eqref{eq:ons-moments} with $\alpha_*(0)=0$ and $V_0=0$. The denominator at zero is
$\sigma_{\zeta_*}(0)=2a_0^2A_3(0)=2a_0^2U_*^3=2\sqrt{a_0}$. Since
$N_{\zeta_*}(0)=0$, $\alpha_*'(0)=N_{\zeta_*}'(0)/(2\sqrt{a_0})=D_*/(2\sqrt{a_0})$. This
is positive by Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-fourth-sign}.

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) By Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-variational}(a), $f_{\mathrm{eq}}\le p(\theta)\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}+\frac12\xi''(1)\,\theta$,

$(0,\varepsilon)$ and $(\kappa/2,\kappa)$ meet $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*\supset[0,\kappa]$, so they have

for all small $\theta$. Hence $\zeta_\theta$ has support points in both intervals. These
points lie in $C_\theta$, which is closed and carries $\zeta_\theta|_{(0,1]}$; so
$q_\theta<\varepsilon$ for all small $\theta$.

(b) By~(a), we may choose $\theta_0\in(0,1)$ such that, for $0<\theta<\theta_0$,
$W_1(\zeta_\theta,\zeta_*)<r_{\rm loc}$, $q_\theta<\kappa/2$, and $\zeta_\theta$ has a
support point $s_\theta\in(\kappa/2,\kappa)$. Then $s_\theta\in C_\theta$, and
$s_\theta<\kappa<K_{\rm loc}$. Suppose some $t\in(q_\theta,s_\theta)$ is not in $C_\theta$.
Put $u=\max(C_\theta\cap[q_\theta,t])$ and $v=\min(C_\theta\cap[t,s_\theta])$. Then $u<t<v$
and $(u,v)\cap C_\theta=\emptyset$, so $\zeta_\theta((u,v))=0$. The points
$u,v\in(0,K_{\rm loc})$ are minima of $\mathcal{O}_\theta$, with $\Gamma_\theta=\mathrm{id}$ and
$\Gamma_\theta'\le1$ there. This contradicts Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-local-gap}. Thus
$[q_\theta,s_\theta]\subset C_\theta$, and $\Gamma_\theta=\mathrm{id}$ on $[q_\theta,s_\theta]$.
Since $\Gamma_\theta$ is continuously differentiable, $\Gamma_\theta'(q_\theta)=1$, and
$\Gamma_\theta'=a\,\mathbb{E} U^2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-ito}) gives the displayed form of
marginality.

(c) Fix $0<\theta<\theta_0$, and write $q=q_\theta$ and
$\bar U_\theta=\Phi_{\zeta_\theta,xx}(0,0)$. By~(b) and~\eqref{eq:cons-contact},
$\zeta_\theta((0,q))=0$ and $\Gamma_\theta=\mathrm{id}$ on $[q,s_\theta]$, so
Corollary~\ref{cor:plat-first-plateau} applies to $\zeta_\theta$ with $m=\theta$ and
$D=D_*$. Since $\xi'''(0)=0$, \eqref{eq:plat-zero} reads
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ons-onset-zero}
 \Gamma_\theta''(0+)=-2a_0^2\theta\,\bar U_\theta^3,\qquad
 \bar U_\theta\longrightarrowU_*=a_0^{-1/2},
\end{equation}
where the limit follows from~\eqref{eq:plat-jet-stability} and~(a). The last bound of the
corollary and~(a) give
\[
 \eta_\theta:=\sup_{0<t<q_\theta}\bigl|\Gamma_\theta'''(t)-D_*\bigr|
 \le C_\Psi\bigl(q_\theta^{1/2}+W_1(\zeta_\theta,\zeta_*)\bigr)+6\theta^2a_0^3U_*^4
 \longrightarrow0 .
\]

\emph{The onset.} Part~(a) of the corollary, which rests on the exact
identity~\eqref{eq:plat-onset-identity}, gives
\[
 \Bigl|2a_0^2\theta\,\bar U_\theta^3-\frac23D_* q\Bigr|\le\frac23\,\eta_\theta\,q .
\]
Since $D_*>0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-fourth-sign}),
\[
 \frac{q_\theta}{\theta}=\frac{3a_0^2\bar U_\theta^3}{D_*+O(\eta_\theta)}
 \longrightarrow\frac{3a_0^2U_*^3}{D_*}=\frac{3\sqrt{a_0}}{D_*}
 =\frac{3}{2\rho_*}.
\]

\emph{The atom at the contact.} Part~(b) of the corollary, which rests on the jump
formula~\eqref{eq:plat-jump} and on $\Gamma_\theta'\equiv1$ on $[q,s_\theta]$, gives
$|2a(q)^2\zeta_\theta(\{q\})\mathbb{E} U_q^3-\frac13D_* q|\le\frac53\eta_\theta q$.
By~\eqref{eq:plat-origin} with $k=2$, $\nu=\zeta_*$ and $0<U\le1$,
$a(q_\theta)^2\mathbb{E} U_{q_\theta}^3\toa_0^2U_*^3=\sqrt{a_0}$. Hence
\[
 \frac{\zeta_\theta(\{q_\theta\})}{\theta}
 =\frac{\{\frac13D_*+O(\eta_\theta)\}\,q_\theta/\theta}{2\sqrt{a_0}+o(1)}
 \longrightarrow\frac{D_*}{3}\cdot\frac{3\sqrt{a_0}}{D_*}\cdot
 \frac{1}{2\sqrt{a_0}}=\frac12 .
\qedhere
\]

label: eq:fifth-area
title: Proof
body_md:
In this proof $C$ denotes constants that depend only on $\xi$. Fix $\theta\in(0,\theta_0)$,
with $\theta_0$ as in Proposition~\ref{prop:ons-onset}(b), and write $q=q_\theta$ and
$g=\Gamma_\theta-\mathrm{id}$ on $[0,q]$. As in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:ons-onset}(c),
Corollary~\ref{cor:plat-first-plateau} applies to $\zeta_\theta$ with $m=\theta$ and
$D=D_*$: the measure has no mass in $(0,q)$ by~\eqref{eq:cons-contact}, and
$\Gamma_\theta=\mathrm{id}$ on an interval $[q,s_\theta]$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:ons-onset}(b). Its
error parameter is the quantity $\eta_\theta$ of that proof, which tends to zero as
$\theta\downarrow0$, as shown there, because $q_\theta\to0$, $\zeta_\theta\Rightarrow\zeta_*$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:ons-onset}(a)) and $\theta\to0$. Part~(c) of the corollary, which rests on the kernel
identity~\eqref{eq:plat-kernel}, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fifth-area}
 \Bigl|\int_0^qg(s)\,ds-\frac{D_*}{72}\,q^4\Bigr|\le\frac{\eta_\theta}{72}\,q^4,
 \qquad |g(s)|\le\Bigl(\frac{D_*}6+\frac56\,\eta_\theta\Bigr)q^3\quad(0\le s\le q).
\end{equation}
Since $\xi'''(0)=0$, Taylor's formula gives $|\xi''(s)-a_0|\le Cs^2$ on $[0,1]$. The
envelope identity and the pointwise bound in~\eqref{eq:fifth-area} give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fifth-envelope-error}
 \Bigl|p'(\theta)-\frac{a_0}2\int_0^qg(s)\,ds\Bigr|
 \le\frac12\int_0^q|\xi''(s)-a_0|\,|g(s)|\,ds\le Cq^6
\end{equation}
for small $\theta$. Together with the area bound in~\eqref{eq:fifth-area},
$p'(\theta)=\frac{a_0D_*}{144}\,q^4\{1+O(\eta_\theta)\}+O(q^6)$. Since $D_*>0$,
$\eta_\theta\to0$ and $q_\theta\to0$, this is the claim.

label: lem:fld-continuity
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:fld-continuity}
The map $h\mapsto\zeta_h$ is weakly continuous, and $\zeta_{-h}=\zeta_h$. The function $\mathcal{F}$
is even and continuously differentiable with $\mathcal{F}'=\mathfrak{m}$, and $\mathfrak{m}$ is odd and
continuous.
head: environment
name: Continuity in the field

label: lem:fld-plateau
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:fld-plateau}
As $t\downarrow0$, $h\to0$ and $W_1(\zeta,\zeta_*)\to0$,
\[
 \sup_{0\le m\le1}\bigl|\Psi_{\zeta,h}(t,m)-D_*-6m^2a_0^3U_*^4\bigr|\longrightarrow0 .
\]
Consequently there are $K_{\rm fld}\in(0,1)$, $h_0>0$ and $\varepsilon_{\rm fld}>0$ with the following property.
If $|h|\le h_0$, $W_1(\zeta,\zeta_*)\le\varepsilon_{\rm fld}$ and $\alpha_\zeta$ is constant on an open
interval $I\subset(0,K_{\rm fld})$, then $\Gamma_{\zeta,h}'''\geD_*/2$ on $I$.
head: environment
name: Plateau positivity, uniformly in a small field

label: lem:fld-gap
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:fld-gap}
Let $K_{\rm fld},h_0,\varepsilon_{\rm fld}$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-plateau}, and let $|h|\le h_0$ with
$W_1(\zeta_h,\zeta_*)\le\varepsilon_{\rm fld}$. There are no two points $u<w$ of $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_h$ in
$(0,K_{\rm fld})$ with $(u,w)\cap\operatorname{supp}\zeta_h=\emptyset$.
head: environment
name: No gaps near the origin

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose there are, and write $\Gamma=\Gamma_{\zeta_h,h}$. On $(u,w)$ the distribution function of
$\zeta_h$ is constant, so $\Gamma'''\geD_*/2>0$ there by Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-plateau}. Thus
$\Gamma'$ is strictly convex on $(u,w)$, and it is continuous on $[u,w]$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-ito}(b). Both endpoints are support points in $(0,1)$, so by
Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-diffusion}(c) they satisfy \eqref{eq:fld-sc}: $\Gamma(u)=u$, $\Gamma(w)=w$ and
$\Gamma'(u),\Gamma'(w)\le1$. The trapezoid argument of Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-obstacle}(d), which
uses only these four relations and the strict convexity of $\Gamma'$, gives a contradiction.
head: environment

label: lem:fld-structure
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: The bottom of the support for small fields

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:local} (Proposition~\ref{prop:ons-equilibrium}), there is $\kappa>0$ with
$[0,\kappa]\subset\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$. Let $K_{\rm fld},h_0,\varepsilon_{\rm fld}$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-plateau}.
Fix $\bar\kappa\in(0,\min\{\kappa,K_{\rm fld}\})$ with $\xi'(\bar\kappa)\le1$, and put
$\kappa_1=\bar\kappa/2$. For $\varepsilon\in(0,\kappa_1]$ the open intervals $(0,\varepsilon)$
and $(\kappa_1,\bar\kappa)$ lie in $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$, so they have positive $\zeta_*$-mass. Since
$W_1$ metrizes weak convergence, Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-continuity} and the portmanteau theorem
give $h_1(\varepsilon)\in(0,1]$ such that, for $0<|h|<h_1(\varepsilon)$, both intervals have
positive $\zeta_h$-mass, $|h|\le h_0$ and $W_1(\zeta_h,\zeta_*)\le\varepsilon_{\rm fld}$. For such $h$,
$q_{\min}(h)<\varepsilon$, and some $v\in\operatorname{supp}\zeta_h$ lies in $(\kappa_1,\bar\kappa)$. Letting
$\varepsilon\downarrow0$ proves $q_{\min}(h)\to0$.

Take $h_1=h_1(\kappa_1)$, let $0<|h|<h_1$, and put $q=q_{\min}(h)$, so that $q<\kappa_1$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-diffusion}(c), $q>0$, and $\zeta_h([0,q))=0$ by the definition of $q$. Suppose
that $t\in(q,v)\setminus\operatorname{supp}\zeta_h$, and let $u=\max(\operatorname{supp}\zeta_h\cap[q,t])$ and
$w=\min(\operatorname{supp}\zeta_h\cap[t,v])$. Then $0<q\le u<t<w\le v<K_{\rm fld}$ and $(u,w)$ misses the support, which
contradicts Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-gap}. Hence $[q,\kappa_1]\subset[q,v]\subset\operatorname{supp}\zeta_h$. By
\eqref{eq:fld-sc}, $\Gamma_{\zeta_h,h}(t)=t$ on $[q,v]$. Since $\Gamma_{\zeta_h,h}$ is $C^1$ with
$\Gamma_{\zeta_h,h}'(t)=\xi''(t)\mathbb{E}\Phi_{\zeta_h,xx}(t,X^{\zeta_h,h}_t)^2$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-ito}(b)), this gives $\Gamma_{\zeta_h,h}'(q)=1$, the last identity of
part~(a).

title: Proof
body_md:
Insert \eqref{eq:fld-exact} into \eqref{eq:fld-t3}. The left side becomes
$q-\xi'(q)/\xi''(q)$, and $\sigma^6=\xi'(q)^3=a_0^3q^3+O(q^5)$. By \eqref{eq:fld-xi-exp},
\[
 h^2\bigl(c_1^2+O(q+h^2)\bigr)
 =\frac{q^3}3\Bigl(\frac{\xi''''(0)}{a_0}+a_0^3c_3^2\Bigr)+O(q^4).
\]
By \eqref{eq:fld-jets} and $U_*^2=a_0^{-1}$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:local}), the left side is
$h^2(a_0^{-1}+o(1))$, and the bracket on the right tends to
$\xi''''(0)U_*^2+a_0^3W_*^2=D_*$. Since $D_*>0$ and $q\to0$, this gives
$q^3=3h^2(a_0D_*)^{-1}(1+o(1))$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By part~(a), $\Gamma_{\zeta_h,h}'\equiv1$ on $[q,\kappa_1]$, so the right derivative of
$\Gamma_{\zeta_h,h}'$ at $q$ vanishes. Since $\zeta_h([0,q))=0$, we have
$\alpha_{\zeta_h}(q)=\zeta_h(\{q\})$. Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-ito}(c) at $t=q$, with
$U_q=v'(X^{\zeta_h,h}_q)$, $V_q=v''(X^{\zeta_h,h}_q)$ and the law of $X^{\zeta_h,h}_q$, gives
\[
 \zeta_h(\{q\})=\frac{a'(q)\mathbb{E} v'(X)^2+a(q)^2\mathbb{E} v''(X)^2}{2a(q)^2\mathbb{E} v'(X)^3}.
\]
Here $\mathbb{E} v'(X)^k\toU_*^k>0$ for $k=2,3$, because $|v'(x)-c_1|\le Cx^2$,
$\mathbb{E} X^2=h^2+\sigma^2\to0$ and $c_1\toU_*$ by \eqref{eq:fld-jets}. Since $v''$ is odd with $v'''(0)=c_3$, $|v''(x)-c_3x|\le C|x|^3$, and
therefore
\[
 \mathbb{E} v''(X)^2=c_3^2(h^2+\sigma^2)+O(h^4+\sigma^4)=a_0W_*^2q+o(q),
\]
by the first claim of part~(b), which gives $h^2=O(q^3)$, and by $\sigma^2=a_0 q+O(q^3)$.
Also $a'(q)=\xi''''(0)q+O(q^2)$ and $a(q)=a_0+O(q^2)$, because $\xi'''(0)=0$. Thus
\[
 \zeta_h(\{q\})=\frac{\xi''''(0)U_*^2+a_0^3W_*^2+o(1)}{2a_0^2U_*^3+o(1)}\,q
 =\frac{D_*}{2\sqrta_0}\,q\,(1+o(1))=\rho_* q\,(1+o(1)),
\]
using $U_*=a_0^{-1/2}$. Finally $\zeta_*([0,q])=\rho_* q(1+o(1))$, because, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:local}, $\alpha_*(0)=\zeta_*(\{0\})=0$ and $\alpha_*'(0)=\rho_*>0$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-continuity}, $\mathcal{F}$ is even and continuously differentiable with
$\mathcal{F}'=\mathfrak{m}$. By parts (b) and (c), for $0<s<h_1$,
\[
 \mathfrak{m}(s)=\frac s{\sqrta_0}-\lambda s^{7/3}\bigl(1+\epsilon(s)\bigr),\qquad
 \lambda=\fracD_*{4\sqrta_0}\Bigl(\frac3{a_0D_*}\Bigr)^{2/3},
\]
where $\epsilon$ is continuous on $(0,h_1)$, because $\mathfrak{m}$ is, and $\epsilon(s)\to0$ as
$s\downarrow0$. Hence $\mathfrak{m}(h)/h\toa_0^{-1/2}$; since $\mathcal{F}'(0)=\mathfrak{m}(0)=0$ and
$\mathfrak{m}$ is odd, this limit is $\mathcal{F}''(0)$. Integrating,
\[
 \mathcal{F}(h)-\mathcal{F}(0)=\int_0^h\mathfrak{m}(s)\,ds
 =\frac{h^2}{2\sqrta_0}-\frac3{10}\,\lambda\,h^{10/3}(1+o(1))\qquad(h\downarrow0),
\]
where
\[
 \frac3{10}\,\lambda=\frac3{40}\,3^{2/3}D_*^{1/3}a_0^{-7/6}
 =\frac3{40}\,(9D_*)^{1/3}a_0^{-7/6} .
\]
Evenness gives the same expansion with $|h|$ for $h<0$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ had an expansion $\sum_{j\le4}c_jh^j+o(h^4)$ at zero, comparison with this display
for $h>0$ would force $c_1=c_3=0$ and $c_2=(2\sqrta_0)^{-1}$, and then
$c_4h^4+o(h^4)=-\frac3{10}\lambda h^{10/3}(1+o(1))$, which is impossible since $\lambda>0$.

label: rem:fld-plateau-picture
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:fld-plateau-picture}
The first claim of part~(b) can also be read off the plateau calculus, and this explains why the
constant $D_*$ of the constrained onset appears. Let $0<h<h_1$, $q=q_{\min}(h)$ and
$\Gamma=\Gamma_{\zeta_h,h}$. The distribution function of $\zeta_h$ vanishes on $[0,q)$, so
$\Gamma'''=\Psi_{\zeta_h,h}(\cdot,0)$ on $(0,q)$, and this tends to $D_*$ uniformly on $(0,q)$
as $h\to0$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-plateau}, since $q\to0$ and $W_1(\zeta_h,\zeta_*)\to0$. At the
ends of the gap, $\Gamma(q)=q$ and $\Gamma'(q)=1$ by part~(a), $\Gamma(0)=\mathfrak{m}(h)^2$ because
$X_0=h$, and the right derivative of $\Gamma'$ at zero is
$a_0^2\Phi_{\zeta_h,xxx}(0,h)^2=O(h^2)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-ito}(c), since
$\Phi_{\zeta_h,xxx}(0,\cdot)$ is odd with bounded derivative; since $\Gamma'''$ is bounded on $(0,q)$, $\Gamma''$ extends continuously to $[0,q]$, with this right derivative as its value at zero (as in the first step of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-kernel}, and by the mean value theorem). Integrating by parts,
\[
 \mathfrak{m}(h)^2=\int_0^qt\,\Gamma''(t)\,dt=\frac{D_*}3\,q^3(1+o(1))+O(h^2q^2).
\]
Since $\mathfrak{m}(h)=h\,\Phi_{\zeta_h,xx}(0,y)$ for some $y\in(0,h)$, and
$\Phi_{\zeta_h,xx}(0,y)\toU_*$, this gives again $q^3=3h^2(a_0D_*)^{-1}(1+o(1))$.

body_md:
\label{rem:fld-scope}
This condition enters through Theorem~\ref{thm:local}, through $a'(0)=0$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-plateau} and in Remark~\ref{rem:fld-plateau-picture},
through $a'(q)=\xi''''(0)q+O(q^2)$ in the proof of the atom in part~(b), and through

label: rem:fld-earlier
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:fld-earlier}
For fixed $h>0$, Lopatto proves that the Parisi measure of the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model is
supported on an interval $[q_-,q_+]$, nondegenerate exactly when the measure is not replica
symmetric, and that it then has an atom at $q_-$ \cite[Theorem~1.1]{Lop26b}. For $0<|h|<h_1$,
Theorem~\ref{thm:field}(a) shows that $\zeta_h$ is not replica symmetric, and (b) gives the
small-field asymptotics of $q_-=q_{\min}(h)$ and of the atom $\zeta_h(\{q_-\})$. The proof uses neither
that theorem (near the origin the gap exclusion of Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-gap} suffices) nor
\cite[Theorem~B.1]{Lop26b} (interval support and a smooth positive density for $\zeta_*$ at $h=0$
and $\beta>1$).

name: A fixed field

label: rem:fld-ansatz
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:fld-ansatz}
By parts (a) and (b) of Theorem~\ref{thm:field}, the masses of $[0,q_{\min}(h)]$ under $\zeta_h$ and $\zeta_*$
satisfy $\zeta_h([0,q_{\min}(h)])=\zeta_*([0,q_{\min}(h)])\,(1+o(1))$: to
leading order the field moves the whole zero-field mass of $[0,q_{\min}(h)]$ into the atom at
$q_{\min}(h)$, and the distribution function of $\zeta_h$ rejoins that of $\zeta_*$ at the edge
(Figure~\ref{fig:bottom}(b)). So the plateau of the order parameter $q(x)$ at height $q_{\min}(h)$
ends, asymptotically, at the zero-field value $x=\zeta_*([0,q_{\min}(h)])$, consistently with the
ansatz of \cite[Appendix~B]{PR09} that $q(x)$ is unperturbed above the plateau, which
Theorem~\ref{thm:field} does not prove. Under the constraint of Theorem~\ref{thm:local}(a) the
distribution function also rejoins the equilibrium one at the first positive contact to leading
order, but the atom at zero carries $\theta$ and the one at $q_\theta$ carries $\theta/2$
(Figure~\ref{fig:bottom}(a)).

title: Standing assumption
body_md:
In this section $\xi(t)=\sum_{p\ge2}\beta_p^2t^p$ is not identically zero and has radius of
convergence greater than one ($\beta_2=0$ is allowed), so $\xi',\xi''>0$ on $(0,1]$ and

Proposition~\ref{prop:cons-envelope} proved there, Lemma~\ref{lem:ons-zero-in-support}, the

the positivity of $\xi''$ on $(0,1]$. The notation is that of Sections~\ref{sec:cons}
and~\ref{sec:plat}; $\zeta_*$ is the unique minimizer of $P$ \cite[Theorem~2 and
Corollary~1]{AC15b}. From Lemmas~\ref{lem:cons-variational} and~\ref{lem:cons-regular} we

constraint is active for $m_0<\theta<1$; if $m_0<1$, then $f_{\mathrm{eq}}<f_1<\infty$ and each

label: prop:atom-slope
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Slope at equilibrium

title: Proof
body_md:
The function $\Sigma$ is an infimum of affine functions of $f$, hence concave, and it is
finite because $\overline{\Lambda}$ is finite and lower semicontinuous on $[0,1]$. For $f\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}$ we
have $\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta f=\widehat{\Lambda}(\theta)+\theta(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-f)\ge0$, with equality at
$\theta=0$; so $\Sigma=0$ on $(-\infty,f_{\mathrm{eq}}]$.

Fix $\delta>0$. Then $\Sigma(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta)=\inf_{0\le\theta\le1}\{\widehat{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta\delta\}$.
On $[0,m_0]$ the bracket equals $-\theta\delta$, and its infimum there is $-m_0\delta$,
attained at $\theta=m_0$. On $[m_0,1]$ write $\theta=m_0+s$; the infimum there is
$-m_0\delta-S(\delta)$, and the choice $s=0$ shows $S(\delta)\ge-\widehat{\Lambda}(m_0)=0$. This
proves \eqref{eq:atom-exact}.

If $m_0=1$, then $S\equiv0$. Let $m_0<1$ and $0<\eta\le1-m_0$, and put
$c_\eta:=\widehat{\Lambda}(m_0+\eta)>0$. For $s\ge\eta$, writing $m_0+\eta$ as a convex combination of
$m_0$ and $m_0+s$, convexity and $\widehat{\Lambda}(m_0)=0$ give $\widehat{\Lambda}(m_0+s)\ge c_\eta$. Let
$0<\delta<c_\eta$. If $s\ge\eta$, then $s\delta-\widehat{\Lambda}(m_0+s)\le\delta-c_\eta<0$; if
$s<\eta$, then $s\delta-\widehat{\Lambda}(m_0+s)\le\eta\delta$. Hence $0\le S(\delta)\le\eta\delta$ for
$\delta<c_\eta$. Since $\eta$ is arbitrary, $S(\delta)=o(\delta)$, which gives
\eqref{eq:atom-slope} and the dichotomy.

For the same $\eta$ and $\delta<c_\eta$, every $\theta<m_0$ gives
$\widehat{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta\delta=-\theta\delta>-m_0\delta\ge\Sigma(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta)$, and every
$\theta=m_0+s$ with $s\ge\eta$ gives
$\widehat{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta\delta\ge c_\eta-\delta-m_0\delta>-m_0\delta$. So the dual minimizer
at the level $f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta$ lies in $[m_0,m_0+\eta)$, and $\theta_f\to m_0$. For $\theta>m_0$
the measure $\nu=s\delta_0+(1-s)\zeta_*$ with $s=(\theta-m_0)/(1-m_0)$ satisfies
$\nu(\{0\})=\theta$ and $W_1(\nu,\zeta_*)\le s$, so the Lipschitz bound
\eqref{eq:cons-lipschitz} gives $f_{\mathrm{eq}}\le p(\theta)\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}+\frac12\xi''(1)s$. Hence
$p(\theta_f)\tof_{\mathrm{eq}}$. If $\zeta'$ is a weak subsequential limit of $\zeta_f$, the same bound
gives $P_{\zeta'}=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$, and uniqueness gives $\zeta'=\zeta_*$. By compactness the whole
family converges.

label: rem:atom-earlier
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:atom-earlier}
Boursier \cite[Remark~1.4]{Bou26a} states, for the Parisi measure $\zeta_*$, the identity
$(-\Lambda^*)'(f_{\mathrm{eq}})=-\zeta_*(\{0\})$ without proof, and relates it to an extreme-value
heuristic. Her
dual function uses the equality constraint $\zeta(\{0\})=\theta$ \cite[(1.12)]{Bou26a}, and her
terminal value $\log(2\cosh x)$ shifts $P_\zeta$, $f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and the level by $\log2$, which does
not affect slopes; after this shift her $-\Lambda^*$ agrees with $\Sigma$ above $f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. Indeed,
for $\theta\in[m_0,1]$ the two constraints give the same infimum, since the inequality
constraint is active for $m_0<\theta<1$ and $\zeta_*$, $\delta_0$ are admissible for both at
$\theta=m_0$, $\theta=1$. For $\theta<m_0$ and $f>f_{\mathrm{eq}}$,
\[
 \theta\inf_{\zeta(\{0\})=\theta}P_\zeta-\theta f\ge-\theta(f-f_{\mathrm{eq}})>-m_0(f-f_{\mathrm{eq}})
 =\overline{\Lambda}(m_0)-m_0f,
\]
and also $\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta f=-\theta(f-f_{\mathrm{eq}})>\overline{\Lambda}(m_0)-m_0f$; so both dual functions are the infimum over $[m_0,1]$ of a common bracket. As $\Sigma=0$ on
$(-\infty,f_{\mathrm{eq}}]$, the identity concerns the right derivative, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:atom-slope} proves it in this form, with the exact remainder $S$.

label: prop:atom-atom
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: The atom

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) If $(0,r)\cap\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*=\emptyset$ for some $r>0$, then
$\zeta_*(\{0\})=\zeta_*([0,r))>0$, because $0\in\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$ and $[0,r)$ is a relatively open
neighbourhood of $0$ in $[0,1]$. Suppose $\xi''(0)<1$, and choose $r\in(0,1)$ with $\xi''<1$
on $[0,r]$. If some $u\in(0,r]$ belonged to $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$, Lemma~\ref{lem:ons-zero-in-support}
and $\Gamma_*(0)=0$ would give $\Gamma_*(u)-\Gamma_*(0)=u$, and the mean value theorem would
give $v\in(0,u)$ with $1=\Gamma_*'(v)=\xi''(v)\mathbb{E} U_v^2\le\xi''(v)<1$, since $0<U_v\le1$. Hence
zero is isolated. This is the argument of \cite[Theorem~1(ii)]{AC15a}.

(b) Choose $u_n\in\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$ with $u_n\downarrow0$ strictly. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:ons-zero-in-support} and \eqref{eq:atom-at-zero},
$\xi''(0)U_*^2=\Gamma_*'(0)=\lim_n\Gamma_*(u_n)/u_n=1$. Since $U_*\le1$, this gives
$\xi''(0)\ge1$ and $U_*=\xi''(0)^{-1/2}$. The mean value theorem on $[u_{n+1},u_n]$ gives
$v_n\in(u_{n+1},u_n)$ with
$\Gamma_*'(v_n)=(\Gamma_*(u_n)-\Gamma_*(u_{n+1}))/(u_n-u_{n+1})=1$, so $v_n\downarrow0$.
Evaluating the right derivative of $\Gamma_*'$ at zero along $v_n$, and using
\eqref{eq:atom-at-zero},
\[
 0=\lim_n\frac{\Gamma_*'(v_n)-\Gamma_*'(0)}{v_n}=\Gamma_*''(0+)
  =\xi'''(0)U_*^2-2\xi''(0)^2m_0U_*^3 .
\]
Since $\xi''(0)U_*>0$, it follows that
$m_0=\xi'''(0)/(2\xi''(0)^2U_*)=\xi'''(0)/(2\xi''(0)^{3/2})$. Finally
$\xi''(0)=2\beta_2^2$ and $\xi'''(0)=6\beta_3^2$.

(c) If $m_0=0$, zero is not isolated by (a), and (b) gives $\beta_3=0$. The converse is (b).

label: lem:nc-confinement
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Confinement

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) Suppose not. Then there are an open set $\mathcal U\subset\mathcal W$ containing
$\delta_0$, covariances $\xi_n$ with $\|\xi_n-\xi_c\|_{C^4[0,1]}\to0$, and constraints $\theta_n$
such that $\zeta_n=\zeta_{\xi_n,\theta_n}\notin\mathcal U$. By compactness of
$\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ a subsequence converges weakly to some $\zeta\notin\mathcal U$. The measure
$\delta_0$ is feasible for every constraint, so $P^{\xi_n}_{\zeta_n}\le P^{\xi_n}_{\delta_0}$,
and joint continuity gives $P^{\xi_c}_\zeta\le P^{\xi_c}_{\delta_0}$. Thus $\zeta$ minimizes
$P^{\xi_c}$, and $\zeta=\delta_0$ by uniqueness, a contradiction.

(b) The continuous function $t-\Gamma_c(t)$ has a positive minimum on $[K,1]$. If the claim
failed, there would be covariances $\xi_n\to\xi_c$ in $C^4$, measures
$\zeta_n\Rightarrow\delta_0$ and points $t_n\in[K,1]$ with
$\Gamma^{\xi_n}_{\zeta_n}(t_n)\ge t_n$; by uniform convergence of $\Gamma^{\xi_n}_{\zeta_n}$
to $\Gamma_c$, a limit point $t$ of $(t_n)$ would satisfy $\Gamma_c(t)\ge t$. Given
\eqref{eq:nc-confinement}, $\mathcal{O}'_\zeta(t)=\frac{a(t)}2(t-\Gamma^\xi_\zeta(t))>0$ on $[K,1]$,
so $\mathcal{O}_\zeta$ is strictly increasing there and takes smaller values just to the left of
$K$; no point of $[K,1]$ minimizes it.

label: lem:nc-gap
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: No gaps between contacts below $K$

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) By Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-obstacle}(b), $\Gamma_\zeta(u)=u$, $\Gamma_\zeta(v)=v$ and
$\Gamma_\zeta'(u),\Gamma_\zeta'(v)\le1$. If $\zeta((u,v))=0$, then $(u,v)$ is a plateau of
$\zeta$ inside $(0,K)$, so $\Gamma_\zeta'''\ge2$ there by \eqref{eq:nc-positive-third}, and
$\Gamma_\zeta'$ is strictly convex on $(u,v)$. This contradicts the trapezoid principle,
Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-obstacle}(d): the identity $\Gamma_\zeta(v)-\Gamma_\zeta(u)=v-u$ makes the
mean of $\Gamma_\zeta'$ over $(u,v)$ equal to one, while strict convexity and the endpoint
bounds force it below one.

(b) By Lemma~\ref{lem:ons-zero-in-support}, $0$ and $v$ are support points of $\zeta_*$ with
$\Gamma_*(0)=0$, $\Gamma_*(v)=v$ and $\Gamma_*'(0),\Gamma_*'(v)\le1$. If $\zeta_*((0,v))=0$,
the argument of (a) applies with $u=0$.

label: prop:nc-support
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Interval support near criticality

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) For $0\le r\le1$, all terms of $\xi''(r)$ are nonnegative, so $\xi''(r)\ge\xi''(0)>1$. In
$\xi''(-r)$ only the terms of odd degree are negative, so
\[
 \xi''(-r)\ge2\beta_2^2-\sum_{p\ge3}p(p-1)\beta_p^2=2\xi''(0)-\xi''(1)
 >2-\bigl(1+\|\xi-\xi_c\|_{C^4[0,1]}\bigr),
\]
because $\xi''(0)>1$ and $|\xi''(1)-1|\le\|\xi-\xi_c\|_{C^4[0,1]}$. The lower bound is positive,
since $\varepsilon_1\le\frac14$.

(b) By Lemma~\ref{lem:ons-zero-in-support}, zero lies in $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$, every support point of
$\zeta_*$ is a contact, and $\Gamma_*'(u)\le1$ at every support point $u$. The measure $\zeta_*$
is not $\delta_0$: for $\delta_0$ the Parisi equation has the solution
$\log\cosh x+\frac12(\xi'(1)-\xi'(t))$, so $\Gamma'_{\delta_0}(0)=\xi''(0)>1$. So
$\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$ has a positive point, and by item~\ref{item:nc-confined} of the choice of
constants (with $\theta=0$), every positive support point lies in $(0,K)$. Hence
$v_*=\max\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*\in(0,K)$. Suppose some $w\in(0,v_*)$ is not in the support. Put
$u=\max(\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*\cap[0,w])$ and $v=\min(\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*\cap[w,v_*])$; then $u<w<v$ and
$\zeta_*((u,v))=0$. If $u>0$, then $u$ and $v$ are contacts in $(0,K)$, which contradicts
Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-gap}(a); if $u=0$, this contradicts Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-gap}(b). So
$\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*=[0,v_*]$, and zero is an accumulation point of the support.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:nc-regular}
Let $\xi\in\mathcal{K}(\varepsilon_1)$ and $\theta\in(0,1)$. Then $\zeta_\theta(\{0\})=\theta$, and
the positive contact set of $\zeta_\theta$ is an interval $[q_\theta,v_\theta]\subset(0,K)$,
possibly reduced to the point $q_\theta$, with
$\operatorname{supp}\zeta_\theta=\{0\}\cup[q_\theta,v_\theta]$. If $v_\theta>q_\theta$, then
$\Gamma_\theta(t)=t$ on $[q_\theta,v_\theta]$ and the first positive contact is marginal. If
$v_\theta=q_\theta$, then $\zeta_\theta=\theta\delta_0+(1-\theta)\delta_{q_\theta}$.

name: Shape of the constrained minimizers

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) and the first assertion of (b) are Proposition~\ref{prop:nc-support}, since
$\|\xi-\xi_c\|_{C^4[0,1]}<\varepsilon_1$. Zero is an accumulation point of the support, so

(c) Evaluate \eqref{eq:plat-psi} for $\zeta_*$ at $t=0$ and $m=0$. There $X_0=0$, so
$U_0=U_*$, $W_0=W_*$ and $V_0=0$ by parity, while $a'(0)=\xi'''(0)=0$ and
$a''(0)=\xi''''(0)$. Thus $\Psi^\xi_{\zeta_*}(0,0)=\xi''''(0)U_*^2+a_0^3W_*^2=D_*$.
Since $\zeta_*\in\mathcal W$ by item~\ref{item:nc-confined} of the choice of constants,
item~\ref{item:nc-positive} gives $D_*\ge2$.

$\theta\downarrow0$. If $v_{\theta_n}=q_{\theta_n}$ along a sequence $\theta_n\downarrow0$, then
by Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-regular}
$\zeta_{\theta_n}=\theta_n\delta_0+(1-\theta_n)\delta_{q_{\theta_n}}$, and every weak limit
point of this sequence is a Dirac mass. But $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*=[0,v_*]$ with $v_*>0$. Hence
$v_\theta>q_\theta$ for all small $\theta>0$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-regular} gives the support
and the marginality. The limits \eqref{eq:nc-onset} are Theorem~\ref{thm:local}(a).

name: Scope

label: prop:nc-dat-threshold
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:nc-dat-threshold}
There are absolute constants $K_{\rm rs}\in(0,\frac14]$ and $C$ such that the following holds
for every $\xi\in\mathcal{K}(\varepsilon_*)$, with $\varepsilon_*$ as fixed in
Appendix~\ref{sec:dat-constants}. Put $\tau=\xi''(0)-1\in(0,\varepsilon_*)$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item For each $\theta\in[0,1]$ the equation $q=\mathfrak{T}(\xi'(q),\theta)$ has exactly one
 solution $q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta$ in $(0,K_{\rm rs}]$. It satisfies $q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta\le2\tau$, and
 $\theta\mapstoq^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta$ is continuously differentiable.
\item Put $\mathfrak A(\theta)=\xi''(q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta)\,\mathfrak{S}(\xi'(q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta),\theta)$. There is
 a unique $\theta_c\in(0,1)$ with $\mathfrak A>1$ on $[0,\theta_c)$, $\mathfrak A(\theta_c)=1$
 and $\mathfrak A<1$ on $(\theta_c,1]$.
\item If $0<\theta<\theta_c$, then $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_\theta=\{0\}\cup[q_\theta,v_\theta]$ with
 $0<q_\theta<v_\theta<\frac1{20}$, and the first positive contact is marginal:
 $\xi''(q_\theta)\mathbb{E}\Phi_{\zeta_\theta,xx}(q_\theta,X_{q_\theta})^2=1$.
\item If $\theta_c\le\theta<1$, then $\zeta_\theta=\theta\delta_0+(1-\theta)\delta_{q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta}$,
 its positive contact set is $\{q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta\}$, and with $q=q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta$
 \[
  1-\xi''(q)\,\mathbb{E}\Phi_{\zeta_\theta,xx}(q,X_q)^2=1-\mathfrak A(\theta),
 \]
 which vanishes at $\theta=\theta_c$ and is positive for $\theta>\theta_c$.
\item The threshold satisfies
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:nc-dat-asymptotics}
  \Bigl|\theta_c-\tfrac23\Bigl(1+\tfrac{\xi''''(0)}4\Bigr)\tau\Bigr|\le C\tau^2 .
 \end{equation}
\end{thmlist}

name: The de Almeida--Thouless threshold

label: cor:nc-dat-levels
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:nc-dat-levels}
Let $\xi\in\mathcal{K}(\varepsilon_*)$ and $f_c=\overline{\Lambda}'_+(\theta_c)$. Then $f_{\mathrm{eq}}<f_c<f_1$ and
$\theta_{f_c}=\theta_c$. A level $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ has a marginal first positive contact if and
only if $f\le f_c$. For $f\in(f_c,f_1)$ the measure $\zeta_f$ has exactly two atoms and the
first positive contact satisfies the strict Plefka inequality \cite[(1.8)]{Bou26b}.
Consequently, within $(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$, the strict Plefka hypothesis of \cite[Theorem~1]{Bou26b}
holds exactly on $(f_c,f_1)$ and fails exactly on $(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_c]$.
head: environment
name: The marginal levels

title: Proof
body_md:
The covariance lies in $\mathcal{K}(\varepsilon_1)$, so it satisfies \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ by
Proposition~\ref{prop:nc-class}(b), and Theorem~\ref{thm:local}(c) applies: $\Lambda$ is $C^1$
and strictly convex on $(0,1)$, $\Lambda'$ maps $(0,1)$ increasingly onto $(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$, and
$\theta_f=(\Lambda')^{-1}(f)$ for every $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$. Hence
$f_c=\Lambda'(\theta_c)\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$, $\theta_{f_c}=\theta_c$, and $\theta_f\le\theta_c$ if and
only if $f\le f_c$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:nc-dat-threshold}, the first positive contact of
$\zeta_f=\zeta_{\theta_f}$ is marginal when $\theta_f<\theta_c$, by~(c), and when
$\theta_f=\theta_c$, by~(d) with $\mathfrak A(\theta_c)=1$; when $\theta_f>\theta_c$, the
measure has two atoms and $1-\mathfrak A(\theta_f)>0$. The condition \cite[(1.8)]{Bou26b} is the
strict form of the Plefka inequality \eqref{eq:intro-plefka} at the first positive contact.

label: rem:nc-dat
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:nc-dat}
(1) For the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, Parisi and Rizzo located this threshold by a
replica computation at replica number $n$ \cite[Section~III, (10), and Section~III.C, (22)--(23)]{PR09}. With
$\xi(t)=\beta^2t^2/2$ and $n=\theta$, their equations (10) and (22) are the equation of
Proposition~\ref{prop:nc-dat-threshold}(a) and $\mathfrak A(\theta)=1$, and their expansion
$n_{\rm dAT}=\frac43(1-T)+O((1-T)^2)$ agrees with (e), since
$\tau=\beta^2-1=2(1-T)+O((1-T)^2)$ and $\xi''''(0)=0$; they describe the
replica-symmetry-breaking solution below the line in \cite[Section~IV]{PR09}. For
$1<\beta^2<1+\varepsilon_*$, Proposition~\ref{prop:nc-dat-threshold} is the constrained-Parisi
form, near criticality, of this prediction: the two-atom measure is the constrained minimizer
exactly when $\theta\ge\theta_c$, and below $\theta_c$ the minimizer carries an interval
starting at a marginal first contact. A positive $\xi''''(0)$ multiplies the leading term of
$\theta_c$ by $1+\frac14\xi''''(0)$.

(2) Every admissible $\theta_0$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:local}(a) satisfies
$\theta_0\le\theta_c$, because for $\theta\ge\theta_c$ the measure $\zeta_\theta$ has two
atoms and its only positive contact is $q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta$, by~(d). By~(c) and

title: Proof
body_md:
Parts (a)--(d) are taken from the literature, with two remarks on scope. First, the papers
\cite{AC15a,AC15b,Che17} state their models under a summability condition such as
$\sum_p2^p\beta_p^2<\infty$, which our radius assumption need not imply; there it serves only
to define the Hamiltonian. The cited statements concern the Parisi equation and functional,
which involve only finitely many derivatives of $\xi$ on $[0,1]$ ($\xi'$, $\xi''$ and, in \cite[Proposition~3]{AC15a}, $\xi'''$); these are bounded here, with
$\xi''>0$ on $(0,1]$. Second, the statements of Auffinger and Chen, made along a time-changed
Brownian motion, hold along the diffusion \eqref{eq:intro-diffusion}, and their function
$\Gamma_\zeta$ of \cite[(18)]{AC15a} is ours, by the Girsanov argument recalled in the
paragraph on analytic facts at the beginning of Section~\ref{sec:plat}.

(a) Existence, continuity and uniform convergence of the spatial derivatives are
\cite[Proposition~1(i)]{AC15a}, and the two bounds are \cite[Proposition~2, (15)--(16)]{AC15a}.
For finitely atomic $\zeta$ the Cole--Hopf formulas \cite[(11)--(12)]{AC15a} show that
$\Phi_\zeta(t,\cdot)$ is even, and evenness passes to general $\zeta$ by the uniform
convergence.

(b) Differentiability, continuity of $\Gamma_\zeta'$ and its formula are
\cite[Proposition~3, (20)]{AC15a}. The uniform convergence of $\Gamma_{\zeta_n}$ and
$\Gamma'_{\zeta_n}$ is \cite[Proposition~1(ii)]{AC15a}, applied to the polynomials $y_1^2$ and
$y_2^2$; that of $\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_n}$ follows by integration. Since $X_0=0$ and
$\Phi_{\zeta,x}(0,\cdot)$ is odd, $\Gamma_\zeta(0)=\Phi_{\zeta,x}(0,0)^2=0$. The bounds
$0\le\Gamma_\zeta\le1$ follow from (a), and $\Gamma_\zeta(1)=\mathbb{E}\tanh^2X_1<1$.

(c) This is \cite[Theorem~2 and Corollary~1]{AC15b}.

(d) At $s=0$ the right derivative is the first-variation formula \cite[Theorem~2]{Che17}, which gives the
second expression in \eqref{eq:cons-first-variation}. Applied at the base point $\zeta_s$ in the directions $\nu-\zeta_s=(1-s)(\nu-\zeta)$ and $\zeta-\zeta_s=-s(\nu-\zeta)$, the same formula gives both one-sided derivatives at every $s\in(0,1)$ and the left derivative at $s=1$, and all equal the second expression in \eqref{eq:cons-first-variation}. Write
$\delta\alpha=\alpha_\nu-\alpha_\zeta$. By \eqref{eq:intro-obstacle} the integrand is
$-\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_s}'\,\delta\alpha$, and Fubini's theorem gives
\[
 -\int_0^1\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_s}'(t)\,\delta\alpha(t)\,dt
 =-\int d(\nu-\zeta)(r)\int_r^1\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_s}'(t)\,dt
 =\int\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_s}\,d(\nu-\zeta),
\]
because $\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_s}(1)=0$. As $s\mapsto\zeta_s$ is weakly continuous, (b) shows that the
derivative is continuous in $s$. Convexity follows from (c).

(e) Apply (d) to the segment from $\nu$ to $\mu$. Since $0\le\Gamma\le1$ and $0\le t\le1$, we
have $|\Gamma(t)-t|\le1$, so the derivative in \eqref{eq:cons-first-variation} is at most
$\frac12\xi''(1)\int_0^1|\alpha_\mu-\alpha_\nu|\,dt$ in absolute value. The same estimate,
with $\sup_{[0,1]}\xi''$ in place of $\frac12\xi''(1)$, appears in the proof
of~\cite[Lemma~3.2]{Bou26b}.

(f) Since $\Gamma_\zeta\in C^1[0,1]$, differentiating \eqref{eq:intro-obstacle} gives the first
two identities in \eqref{eq:cons-obstacle} and $\mathcal{O}_\zeta\in C^2[0,1]$. Moreover
$\mathcal{O}_\zeta'(1)=\frac12\xi''(1)\{1-\Gamma_\zeta(1)\}>0$ by (b), so $\mathcal{O}_\zeta(t)<\mathcal{O}_\zeta(1)$
for $t<1$ close to $1$. At a minimum point $t\in(0,1)$ of $\mathcal{O}_\zeta$ on $(0,1]$ we have
$\mathcal{O}_\zeta'(t)=0$ and $\mathcal{O}_\zeta''(t)\ge0$. Since $\xi''(t)>0$, the first gives
$\Gamma_\zeta(t)=t$, and the second then gives $\Gamma_\zeta'(t)\le1$.

(g) By (d), the right derivative at $s=0$ of $s\mapsto P_{(1-s)\zeta_*+s\nu}$ is
$\int\mathcal{O}_*\,d(\nu-\zeta_*)$, and it is nonnegative because $\zeta_*$ minimizes $P$. Taking
$\nu=\delta_t$ gives $\mathcal{O}_*(t)\ge o_*$. So $\mathcal{O}_*-o_*$ is a nonnegative continuous function
with $\zeta_*$-integral zero, and it vanishes on $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$. This is
\cite[Corollary~3.6]{JT17}. Conversely, under the stated condition, convexity of
$s\mapsto P_{(1-s)\zeta+s\nu}$ and (d) give
$P_\nu\ge P_\zeta+\int\mathcal{O}_\zeta\,d(\nu-\zeta)\ge P_\zeta$ for every $\nu$, so $\zeta$
minimizes $P$ and equals $\zeta_*$ by (c).

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) The set $\mathcal A_\theta$ is convex. It is weakly closed, because
$\zeta\mapsto\zeta(\{0\})$ is upper semicontinuous, and hence compact. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-standard}(c),(e), $P$ attains its minimum on $\mathcal A_\theta$ at exactly
one point $\zeta_\theta$. If $\theta\le m_0$, then $\zeta_*\in\mathcal A_\theta$, so
$\zeta_\theta=\zeta_*$ and $p(\theta)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. The sets $\mathcal A_\theta$ decrease in $\theta$,
so $p$ is nondecreasing and $p\ge p(0)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. The measure $\theta\delta_0+(1-\theta)\zeta_*$ lies
in $\mathcal A_\theta$, at $W_1$-distance $\theta\int_0^1(1-\alpha_*)\,dt\le\theta$ from
$\zeta_*$, so \eqref{eq:cons-lipschitz} gives the upper bound on $p(\theta)$.

Let $\theta_n\to\theta$ in $[0,1)$, and put $\lambda_n=(\theta_n-\theta)^+/(1-\theta)$. The
measure $\lambda_n\delta_0+(1-\lambda_n)\zeta_\theta$ lies in $\mathcal A_{\theta_n}$ and within
$W_1$-distance $\lambda_n$ of $\zeta_\theta$, so $\limsup_np(\theta_n)\le p(\theta)$ by
\eqref{eq:cons-lipschitz}. Let $\zeta'$ be the weak limit of a subsequence of
$(\zeta_{\theta_n})$. Since $\{0\}$ is closed,
$\zeta'(\{0\})\ge\limsup_n\zeta_{\theta_n}(\{0\})\ge\theta$, and
$P_{\zeta'}=\lim P_{\zeta_{\theta_n}}\le p(\theta)$ along the subsequence. Thus $\zeta'$
minimizes $P$ on $\mathcal A_\theta$, so $\zeta'=\zeta_\theta$ and $P_{\zeta'}=p(\theta)$. By
compactness, $\zeta_{\theta_n}\Rightarrow\zeta_\theta$ and $p(\theta_n)\to p(\theta)$.

(b) Let $\theta_1,\theta_2\in[0,1)$ and $t\in(0,1)$ with
$\theta=t\theta_1+(1-t)\theta_2>0$. The probability measure
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cons-mixture}
 \nu=\frac{t\theta_1\zeta_{\theta_1}+(1-t)\theta_2\zeta_{\theta_2}}{\theta}
 \quad\text{satisfies}\quad
 \nu(\{0\})\ge\frac{t\theta_1^2+(1-t)\theta_2^2}{\theta}\ge\theta
\end{equation}
(as in \cite[proof of Lemma~3.2]{Bou26b}), so $\nu\in\mathcal A_\theta$, and convexity of $P$ gives
$\Lambda(\theta)\le\theta P_\nu\le t\Lambda(\theta_1)+(1-t)\Lambda(\theta_2)$. Hence $\Lambda$ is
convex on $[0,1)$. By (a), $\Lambda(\theta)/\theta=p(\theta)\tof_{\mathrm{eq}}$ as $\theta\downarrow0$,
and $\Lambda(0)=0$; this gives $\overline{\Lambda}'_+(0)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. If $\mu\in\mathcal A_{1-h}$ with
$0<h\le1$, then $\mu((0,1])\le h$, so $W_1(\mu,\delta_0)=\int_0^1\mu((t,1])\,dt\le h$. Since
$\delta_0\in\mathcal A_{1-h}$, \eqref{eq:cons-lipschitz} gives
\[
 (1-h)\bigl(P_{\delta_0}-\tfrac12\xi''(1)h\bigr)\le\Lambda(1-h)\le(1-h)P_{\delta_0}.
\]
Hence $\Lambda(\theta)\to P_{\delta_0}$ as $\theta\uparrow1$, so $\overline{\Lambda}(1)=P_{\delta_0}$ and
$\overline{\Lambda}$ is continuous on $[0,1]$; with the value $+\infty$ outside $[0,1]$ it is closed and
convex. The same bounds give
$\{\overline{\Lambda}(1)-\overline{\Lambda}(1-h)\}/h\le P_{\delta_0}+\frac12\xi''(1)$. By convexity these quotients
increase to $\overline{\Lambda}'_-(1)$ as $h\downarrow0$, so $f_1<\infty$.

(c) Let $m_0<\theta<1$ and suppose that $\zeta_\theta(\{0\})>\theta$. For every $\nu$, the
measure $(1-s)\zeta_\theta+s\nu$ lies in $\mathcal A_\theta$ for small $s>0$, so
\[
 P_{\zeta_\theta}\le P_{(1-s)\zeta_\theta+s\nu}\le(1-s)P_{\zeta_\theta}+sP_\nu ,
\]
that is, $P_{\zeta_\theta}\le P_\nu$. Then $\zeta_\theta=\zeta_*$, whose mass at zero is
$m_0<\theta$, a contradiction. Hence $\zeta_\theta(\{0\})=\theta$; this also holds at
$\theta=m_0$, where $\zeta_{m_0}=\zeta_*$.

Let $m_0\le\theta_1<\theta_2<1$. If $p(\theta_1)=p(\theta_2)$, then
$\zeta_{\theta_2}\in\mathcal A_{\theta_1}$ attains $p(\theta_1)$, so
$\zeta_{\theta_2}=\zeta_{\theta_1}$. This is impossible, because $\zeta_{\theta_i}(\{0\})=\theta_i$.
So $p$ is strictly increasing on $[m_0,1)$.

Let $\theta_1\ne\theta_2$ in $[m_0,1)$, let $t\in(0,1)$, and put
$\theta=t\theta_1+(1-t)\theta_2$, so that $m_0<\theta<1$. For the measure $\nu$ of
\eqref{eq:cons-mixture}, saturation gives
\[
 \nu(\{0\})=\frac{t\theta_1^2+(1-t)\theta_2^2}{\theta}
 =\theta+\frac{t(1-t)(\theta_1-\theta_2)^2}{\theta}>\theta=\zeta_\theta(\{0\}).
\]
So $\nu\in\mathcal A_\theta$ differs from $\zeta_\theta$, uniqueness gives
$\theta P_\nu>\Lambda(\theta)$, and the convexity inequality of (b) is strict.

(d) Let $f_{\mathrm{eq}}<f<f_1$ and $\varphi(\theta)=\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta f$. By (b), $\varphi$ is closed
and convex, so it attains its minimum on $[0,1]$, and
$\varphi'_+(0)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}-f<0<f_1-f=\varphi'_-(1)$. Hence no minimizer lies at $0$ or at $1$. On
$[0,m_0]$ we have $\varphi(\theta)=\theta(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-f)$ by (a), which is strictly decreasing, so the
minimizers lie in $[m_0,1)$. They form an interval on which $\varphi$ is constant, that is,
on which $\Lambda$ is affine. By (c) this interval is a single point.

(e) Let $m_0<\theta<1$. By (c), $\mu_\theta(\{0\})=0$. For $\nu\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$, the segment
from $\zeta_\theta$ to $\theta\delta_0+(1-\theta)\nu$ stays in $\mathcal A_\theta$. By
minimality and \eqref{eq:cons-first-variation}, its right derivative at $\zeta_\theta$, which is
$(1-\theta)\int\mathcal{O}_\theta\,d(\nu-\mu_\theta)$, is nonnegative. Taking $\nu=\delta_t$ gives
$\mathcal{O}_\theta(t)\ge o_\theta$ for every $t\in[0,1]$. Since
$\int(\mathcal{O}_\theta-o_\theta)\,d\mu_\theta=0$ and $\mathcal{O}_\theta$ is continuous,
$\mathcal{O}_\theta=o_\theta$ on $\operatorname{supp}\mu_\theta$. Suppose that $\mathcal{O}_\theta(0)=o_\theta$. Then for
every $\nu$,
\[
 \int\mathcal{O}_\theta\,d(\nu-\zeta_\theta)
 =\int\mathcal{O}_\theta\,d\nu-\theta\,\mathcal{O}_\theta(0)-(1-\theta)o_\theta
 =\int(\mathcal{O}_\theta-o_\theta)\,d\nu\ge0,
\]
and Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-standard}(g) gives $\zeta_\theta=\zeta_*$, which contradicts
$\zeta_\theta(\{0\})=\theta>m_0$. Hence $\mathcal{O}_\theta(0)>o_\theta$.

Consequently $0\notin\operatorname{supp}\mu_\theta$. So $o_\theta=\min_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}_\theta$, and
$\operatorname{supp}\zeta_\theta\cap(0,1]=\operatorname{supp}\mu_\theta\subset C_\theta$; in particular $C_\theta$ is
nonempty. Since $o_\theta=\min_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}_\theta<\mathcal{O}_\theta(0)$, also $C_\theta=\{t\in[0,1]:\mathcal{O}_\theta(t)=o_\theta\}$; this set is closed and does not
contain $0$. It is therefore compact and bounded away from zero, and by
Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-standard}(f) it does not contain $1$. Thus $C_\theta\subset(0,1)$ and
$q_\theta=\min C_\theta\in(0,1)$. Since $\operatorname{supp}\mu_\theta\subset C_\theta\subset[q_\theta,1)$,
we get $\zeta_\theta((0,q_\theta))=0$. A point $r\in(0,q_\theta)$ is not in $C_\theta$, so
$\mathcal{O}_\theta(r)>o_\theta=\mathcal{O}_\theta(q_\theta)$, and the same holds at $r=0$. Finally,
$q_\theta\in(0,1)$ is a minimum point of $\mathcal{O}_\theta$ on $(0,1]$, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-standard}(f),(b) give the last two relations in \eqref{eq:cons-contact}.
