title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:cons-envelope}, $\Lambda'$ is continuous on $(0,1)$. It is strictly
increasing on $(m_0,1)$, because $\Lambda$ is strictly convex on $[m_0,1)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-variational}(c)). As $\theta\uparrow1$, $\Lambda'(\theta)$ increases to
$\overline{\Lambda}'_-(1)=f_1$, by convexity and the continuity of $\overline{\Lambda}$ at $1$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-variational}(b)). If $m_0>0$, then $\Lambda'(\theta)\to\Lambda'(m_0)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$
as $\theta\downarrow m_0$, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-regular}(d). If $m_0=0$, then
for $0<\theta<\frac12$ convexity gives
\[
 f_{\mathrm{eq}}=\overline{\Lambda}'_+(0)\le\Lambda'(\theta)\le\frac{\Lambda(2\theta)-\Lambda(\theta)}{\theta}
 =2p(2\theta)-p(\theta),
\]
and the right side tends to $f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-variational}(a). Therefore $\Lambda'$
maps $(m_0,1)$ onto $(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$. For $f$ in this interval and $\theta=(\Lambda')^{-1}(f)$,
the convex function $\overline{\Lambda}(\vartheta)-\vartheta f$ has derivative zero at $\vartheta=\theta$, so $\theta$
minimizes it and $\theta=\theta_f$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-variational}(d). Finally,
$\Lambda'=p+\theta p'$ and \eqref{eq:cons-envelope} at $\theta_f\in(m_0,1)$ give
\eqref{eq:cons-level}.

title: Proof
body_md:
(b) First let $\zeta$ and $\tilde\zeta$ have finitely many atoms. On each closed strip
between consecutive atoms of either measure, $u$ solves
\[
 u_t+\tfrac a2u_{xx}+a\alpha uu_x=0,\qquad u(1,x)=\tanh x,
\]
classically, and $\tilde u$ solves the same equation with $\tilde a$, $\tilde\alpha$. For
$k\ge2$, differentiating $k$ times in $x$ gives a linear backward equation for
$\partial_x^ku$, with drift $a\alpha u$, zeroth-order coefficient $(k+1)a\alpha u_x$, and a
forcing that is a polynomial in derivatives of order less than $k$. Since $|u|\le1$ and
$0<u_x\le1$, the maximum principle and induction on $k$ bound $\partial_x^ku$ uniformly
over $\mathfrak F$. The difference $w=u-\tilde u$ has terminal value zero and solves
\[
 w_t+\tfrac a2w_{xx}+a\alpha uw_x+a\alpha\tilde u_xw
 =-\tfrac{a-\tilde a}2\,\tilde u_{xx}-(a\alpha-\tilde a\tilde\alpha)\,\tilde u\tilde u_x ,
\]
whose drift and zeroth-order coefficient are bounded uniformly. The maximum principle
bounds $\|w\|_\infty$ by a constant times the time integral of the supremum of the
right side, which is \eqref{eq:plat-jet-general} for $k=0$. Differentiating this
equation and inducting gives every $k$; at each step the forcing involves only finitely
many of the derivatives already bounded, so the constants stay uniform over $\mathfrak F$
and over all measures. Both statements pass to general measures
by~\cite[Proposition~1(i)]{AC15a}, applied at each of the two covariances, because weak
convergence of measures on $[0,1]$ implies $L^1$ convergence of their distribution
functions.

(a) Take $\mathfrak F=\{\xi\}$ in (b). Then
$\|a(\alpha_\zeta-\alpha_\nu)\|_{L^1}\le\|a\|_\inftyW_1(\zeta,\nu)$, and
\eqref{eq:plat-jet-general} for $u=\Phi_{\zeta,x}$ becomes \eqref{eq:plat-jet-stability}
after the index shift $k\mapsto k-1$.

(c) For a measure with finitely many atoms the Parisi equation holds classically on each
closed strip between consecutive atoms, and there
$\partial_t\partial_x^k\Phi=-\partial_x^{k-1}\{\frac a2\Phi_{xxx}+a\alpha\Phi_x\Phi_{xx}\}$.
This is bounded by a constant $L_k$ that depends only on $\xi$ and $B_1,\dots,B_{k+2}$.
Since $\partial_x^k\Phi$ is continuous in time across atoms~\cite[Proposition~5,
(64)]{AC15a}, \eqref{eq:plat-time-lip} holds for such measures, and it passes to every
$\zeta$ by \eqref{eq:plat-jet-stability}.

(d) The drift of $X$ is bounded by $\|a\|_\infty$, since $\alpha\le1$ and
$|\Phi_{\zeta,x}|\le1$, and the martingale part has variance $\int_0^ta\le\|a\|_\infty t$.

(e) Split the difference at $(t,0)$ and at $(0,0)$. The three pieces are bounded by
$B_{k+1}\mathbb{E}|X_t|$, by $L_kt$ (part (c)) and by $C_k\|a\|_\inftyW_1(\zeta,\nu)$
(part (a)); then use $\mathbb{E}|X_t|\le(\mathbb{E} X_t^2)^{1/2}$ and \eqref{eq:plat-small-time}.

$\Phi_{\zeta_n,x}$, and $b_n=a_n\alpha_nu_n$, $b=a\alpha u$ for the drifts. Since

\[
 |b_n(s,y)-b(s,x)|\le|a_n\alpha_n-a\alpha|(s)+\|a\|_\infty\|u_n-u\|_\infty
 +\|a\|_\infty|y-x| .
\]

has expectation at most $4\int_0^1|\sqrt{a_n}-\sqrt a|^2$ by Doob's inequality. Gronwall's
inequality applied to $\Delta_n(t)=\mathbb{E}\sup_{s\le t}|X^n_s-X_s|^2$ gives
\[
 \Delta_n(1)\le3e^{3\|a\|_\infty^2}\Bigl\{\bigl(\|a_n\alpha_n-a\alpha\|_{L^1}
 +\|a\|_\infty\|u_n-u\|_\infty\bigr)^2+4\int_0^1|\sqrt{a_n}-\sqrt a|^2\Bigr\},
\]
which tends to zero by \eqref{eq:plat-jet-general} with $k=0$ and because
$\|a_n\alpha_n-a\alpha\|_{L^1}\le\|a_n-a\|_\infty+\|a\|_\inftyW_1(\zeta_n,\zeta)$. Since

 |\Gamma_n(t)-\Gamma(t)|\le2\|u_n-u\|_\infty+2\mathbb{E}|X^n_t-X_t|,

\[
 |\Gamma_n'(t)-\Gamma'(t)|\le\|a_n-a\|_\infty
 +2\|a\|_\infty\bigl(\|\partial_x(u_n-u)\|_\infty+B_3\,\mathbb{E}|X^n_t-X_t|\bigr).
\]

body_md:
On $[s,t)$ we have $\alpha_\zeta=m$. If $m=0$, the drift of $X$ vanishes there and the
claim is the Gaussian transition law. If $m>0$, put $g=e^{m\Phi_\zeta}$. For $s<r<t'<t$, $\Phi_\zeta(r,\cdot)$ is the Cole--Hopf transform of $\Phi_\zeta(t',\cdot)$ (as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-ito}(c)); since $\Phi_\zeta$ is continuous on $[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$ with $|\Phi_{\zeta,x}|\le1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-standard}(a)), letting $t'\uparrow t$ and $r\downarrow s$ shows that $g(r,\cdot)$ is the Gaussian average of $g(t,\cdot)$ with variance $\xi'(t)-\xi'(r)$ for $s\le r\le t$. Hence $g_r+\frac a2g_{xx}=0$ on $[s,t)\times\mathbb{R}$, and $g$ is continuous on $[s,t]\times\mathbb{R}$. Let $M_r=x+\int_s^r\sqrt{a}\,dB$.
Then $g(r,M_r)/g(s,x)$, $s\le r\le t$, is a positive martingale with mean one. Under the
probability measure that it defines at time $t$, Girsanov's theorem gives $M$ the drift
$a\,\partial_x\log g=am\Phi_{\zeta,x}$, which is the drift of $X$ on $[s,t)$. The drift is
Lipschitz in space, so the law of $X$ on $[s,t]$ started from $x$ is the law of $M$ under
the new measure. The density of $X_t$ is therefore $g(t,y)/g(s,x)$ times the
$\mathcal N(x,\xi'(t)-\xi'(s))$ density of $M_t$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-standard}(g), with $o_*=\int\mathcal{O}_*\,d\zeta_*$, we have
$o_*=\min_{[0,1]}\mathcal{O}_*$, and the minimum is attained at every support point. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-standard}(f), $\mathcal{O}_*$ is twice continuously differentiable, with
$\mathcal{O}_*'(t)=-\frac12\xi''(t)\{\Gamma_*(t)-t\}$, and $1$ is not a minimum point of $\mathcal{O}_*$
on $(0,1]$; so $\mathcal{O}_*(1)>o_*$ and $1\notin\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$.

\emph{Positive support points.} A point $u\in\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*\cap(0,1)$ is an interior minimum
of $\mathcal{O}_*$, and~\eqref{eq:plat-contact} gives $\Gamma_*(u)=u$ and $\Gamma_*'(u)\le1$.

\emph{Zero lies in the support.} Suppose that $t_0:=\min\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*>0$. By the two
preceding steps, $t_0<1$ and $\Gamma_*(t_0)=t_0$. The distribution function $\alpha_*$
vanishes on $[0,t_0)$. Hence the drift of $X$ vanishes there, and for $0<t<t_0$ the variable
$X_t=\int_0^t\sqrt{\xi''(s)}\,dB_s$ is centered Gaussian with variance $\xi'(t)>0$. The
interval $(0,t_0)$ is a plateau of height $m=0$, and~\eqref{eq:plat-second} gives
\[
 \Gamma_*''(t)=\xi'''(t)\,\mathbb{E} U_t^2+\xi''(t)^2\,\mathbb{E} V_t^2\qquad(0<t<t_0).
\]
Here $\xi'''(t)\ge0$ and $\xi''(t)>0$. Moreover $\mathbb{E} V_t^2>0$. Indeed, the continuous
function $\Phi_{\zeta_*,xxx}(t,\cdot)$ is not identically zero. Otherwise
$\Phi_{\zeta_*,xx}(t,\cdot)$ would be the positive constant $\Phi_{\zeta_*,xx}(t,0)$, and by
oddness $\Phi_{\zeta_*,x}(t,x)=x\,\Phi_{\zeta_*,xx}(t,0)$ would be unbounded, which
contradicts $|\Phi_{\zeta_*,x}|\le1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-standard}(a)). So $\Phi_{\zeta_*,xxx}(t,\cdot)$ is nonzero on a nonempty
open set, which has positive probability under the Gaussian law of $X_t$. Hence
$\Gamma_*''>0$ on $(0,t_0)$. The function $h=\Gamma_*-\mathrm{id}$ is therefore continuous and
strictly convex on $[0,t_0]$, with $h(t_0)=0$ and $h(0)=\Phi_{\zeta_*,x}(0,0)^2=0$ by
oddness. Thus $h<0$ on $(0,t_0)$, so $\mathcal{O}_*'=-\frac12\xi''h>0$ there and
$\mathcal{O}_*(0)<\mathcal{O}_*(t_0)=o_*$. This contradicts $\mathcal{O}_*\ge o_*$, so $0\in\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$.

\emph{The point zero.} By oddness $\Gamma_*(0)=0$, and $\mathcal{O}_*(0)=o_*$ because
$0\in\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*$. If $\xi''(0)>0$, the endpoint inequality,
Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-obstacle}(c), gives $\Gamma_*'(0)\le1$: the difference
$\mathcal{O}_*(t)-\mathcal{O}_*(0)=-\frac14\xi''(0)\{\Gamma_*'(0)-1\}t^2+o(t^2)$ is nonnegative. If
$\xi''(0)=0$, then $\Gamma_*'(0)=\xi''(0)U_*^2=0$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\|\xi-\xi_c\|_{C^4[0,1]}<\frac14$, let $\zeta$ be a probability measure, and let
$k\in\{2,3,4\}$. The derivative $\partial_x^k\Phi_c(t,x)=(\log\cosh)^{(k)}(x)$ does not depend
on $t$, and $(\log\cosh)^{(k+1)}$ is bounded by an absolute constant $L$. Hence
\[
 \bigl|\partial_x^k\Phi^\xi_\zeta(t,X_t)-\partial_x^k\Phi_c(0,0)\bigr|
 \le\|\partial_x^k(\Phi^\xi_\zeta-\Phi_c)\|_\infty+L|X_t| .
\]
We apply the estimate \eqref{eq:plat-jet-general} to the pairs $(\xi,\zeta)$ and $(\xi_c,\delta_0)$, for
which $(\tilde a,\tilde\alpha)=(1,1)$. Since
$\|a\alpha_\zeta-1\|_{L^1}\le\|a-1\|_{L^1}+\frac54\int_0^1(1-\alpha_\zeta)\,dt$ and
$\int_0^1(1-\alpha_\zeta)\,dt=\int s\,\zeta(ds)=W_1(\zeta,\delta_0)$, the first term is at most
$C(\|\xi-\xi_c\|_{C^4[0,1]}+W_1(\zeta,\delta_0))$. By \eqref{eq:plat-small-time},
$\mathbb{E}|X_t|\le(2\|a\|_\infty t+2\|a\|_\infty^2t^2)^{1/2}\le3\sqrt t$. Now $\Psi^\xi_\zeta(t,m)$ is a
polynomial in $a(t),a'(t),a''(t),m$ and in expectations of monomials of degree at most four in
$(U_t,V_t,W_t)$, all of which are bounded uniformly; at the reference values $(1,0,0)$ and
$(1,0,-2)$ it equals $4+6m^2$. Therefore
\[
 \bigl|\Psi^\xi_\zeta(t,m)-4-6m^2\bigr|
 \le C'\bigl(\|\xi-\xi_c\|_{C^4[0,1]}+W_1(\zeta,\delta_0)+\sqrt t\bigr)
 \qquad(0\le t\le1,\ 0\le m\le1),
\]
with an absolute constant $C'$. Choose $K_P$ with $C'\sqrt{K_P}\le\frac23$, and then
$\varepsilon_P$ and $\mathcal W_P$ so that the other two terms contribute at most $\frac43$.
Then $\Psi^\xi_\zeta\ge2$ on $[0,K_P]\times[0,1]$, and \eqref{eq:nc-positive-third} follows from
Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-ito}(c).

title: Proof
body_md:
The last sentence is Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-regular}(d). Let $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$, so that
$\zeta_*\ne\delta_0$ and Corollary~\ref{cor:cons-level} applies.

\emph{Upper bound.} For $\theta\in(0,1)$, Markov's inequality gives
$\mathbb{P}(N^{-1}\logZ_N\ge f)\le e^{-N\theta f}\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta$, so
$\limsup_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}(N^{-1}\logZ_N\ge f)\le\Lambda(\theta)-\theta f$. At
$\theta=\theta_f$ the right side is $\Sigma(f)$.

\emph{Lower bound.} Let $\varepsilon>0$ with $f'=f+2\varepsilon<f_1$, and put
$\theta=\theta_{f'}\in(m_0,1)$, so that $\Lambda'(\theta)=f'$ by
Corollary~\ref{cor:cons-level}. Tilt by $Z_N^\theta$: for events $E$ put
$\mathbb Q_N(E)=\mathbb{E}[Z_N^\theta\mathbf{1}_E]/\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta$. For $0<\lambda<\min\{\theta,1-\theta\}$,
Markov's inequality under $\mathbb Q_N$ and \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ give
\begin{align*}
 \limsup_N\frac1N\log\mathbb Q_N\bigl(N^{-1}\logZ_N\ge f'+\varepsilon\bigr)
  &\le\Lambda(\theta+\lambda)-\Lambda(\theta)-\lambda(f'+\varepsilon),\\
 \limsup_N\frac1N\log\mathbb Q_N\bigl(N^{-1}\logZ_N\le f'-\varepsilon\bigr)
  &\le\Lambda(\theta-\lambda)-\Lambda(\theta)+\lambda(f'-\varepsilon).
\end{align*}
Since $\Lambda'(\theta)=f'$, both right sides equal $-\lambda\varepsilon+o(\lambda)$ as
$\lambda\downarrow0$. Fix $\lambda$ so that both are negative. Then $\mathbb Q_N(A_N)\to1$ for
$A_N=\{|N^{-1}\logZ_N-f'|<\varepsilon\}$. On $A_N$ we have
$Z_N^\theta\le e^{N\theta(f'+\varepsilon)}$ and $N^{-1}\logZ_N>f+\varepsilon$. Hence
$\mathbb{P}(N^{-1}\logZ_N\ge f)\ge\mathbb{P}(A_N)
\ge\mathbb Q_N(A_N)\,\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\,e^{-N\theta(f'+\varepsilon)}$, and \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ gives
$\liminf_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}(N^{-1}\logZ_N\ge f)\ge\Lambda(\theta)-\theta f'-\theta\varepsilon
\ge\Sigma(f')-\varepsilon$. The function $\Sigma$ is an infimum of affine functions, and it is
finite because $\overline{\Lambda}$ is lower semicontinuous and finite on $[0,1]$; so $\Sigma$ is concave
and continuous on $\mathbb{R}$. Letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ gives the lower bound $\Sigma(f)$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $D_N$ be a centered Gaussian variable with variance $\frac12$, independent of
$(g_{ij})_{i<j}$, and put
$H_N(\sigma)=\beta N^{-1/2}\sum_{i<j}g_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j+\beta D_N$. For
$\sigma,\sigma'\in\{-1,1\}^N$ with $R=N^{-1}\sigma\cdot\sigma'$,
$\mathbb{E} H_N(\sigma)H_N(\sigma')
=\frac{\beta^2}N\sum_{i<j}\sigma_i\sigma'_i\sigma_j\sigma'_j+\frac{\beta^2}2
=\frac{\beta^2}{2N}(N^2R^2-N)+\frac{\beta^2}2=N\xi(R)$.
So $H_N$ is a field as in \eqref{eq:intro-covariance}, and
$Z_N=2^{-N}\sum_\sigma e^{H_N(\sigma)}$ has the law of the partition function. On this
probability space $N^{-1}\logZ_N=N^{-1}F_{N,\beta}-\log2+\beta D_N/N$ identically. If
$N^{-1}F_{N,\beta}-\log2\ge f$ and $N^{-1}\logZ_N<f-\eta$, then $\beta D_N<-\eta N$; if
$N^{-1}\logZ_N\ge f+\eta$ and $N^{-1}F_{N,\beta}-\log2<f$, then $\beta D_N>\eta N$. Since $\beta D_N$
is centered Gaussian with variance $\beta^2/2$, each of these events has probability at most
$e^{-\eta^2N^2/\beta^2}$, and \eqref{eq:cons-sk-sandwich} follows.

For the consequence, let $f\in I$ and let $\eta>0$ be small enough that $f\pm\eta\in I$. The
function $\Sigma$ is finite and continuous on $\mathbb{R}$ (proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-gartner-ellis}), and the error terms in \eqref{eq:cons-sk-sandwich} decay
faster than every exponential. The first inequality therefore gives
$\limsup_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}(N^{-1}F_{N,\beta}-\log2\ge f)\le\Sigma(f-\eta)$, and the second gives
$\liminf_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}(N^{-1}F_{N,\beta}-\log2\ge f)\ge\Sigma(f+\eta)$. Let $\eta\downarrow0$.

\label{rem:mo-fm}
\begin{steplist}
\item \emph{The upper bound.} The upper bound in the proof of
 Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-gartner-ellis} uses only
 $\limsup_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\le\Lambda(\theta)$ at $\theta_f$, which for $\xi$ convex on
 $[-1,1]$ is Proposition~\ref{prop:A-guerra}. For such $\xi$,

 gives, again without \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}},
 \[
  \liminf_{\delta\downarrow0}\delta^{-6/5}\liminf_{N\to\infty}
  \Bigl(-\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(N^{-1}\logZ_N\gef_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta\bigr)\Bigr)
  \ge\frac56\,(6c)^{-1/5}.
 \]
\item \emph{The lower bound.} It uses \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ at $\theta_{f+2\varepsilon}$ and
 $\theta_{f+2\varepsilon}\pm\lambda$, which lie
 in any prescribed neighbourhood of $\theta_f$ once $\varepsilon$ and $\lambda$ are small, by
 continuity of $(\Lambda')^{-1}$. So \eqref{eq:cons-ldp} holds at $f$ once \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ holds near
 $\theta_f$, and since $\theta_f\downarrow m_0$ as $f\downarrowf_{\mathrm{eq}}$
 (Corollary~\ref{cor:cons-level}), limits as $f\downarrowf_{\mathrm{eq}}$, such as the second display of
 Theorem~\ref{thm:local}(d), need \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ only on $(m_0,\theta_1)$ for some $\theta_1>m_0$. For
 the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick covariance with $\beta>1$, where \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ holds
 \cite[Proposition~5.1]{Lop26a} (an alternative proof is \cite[Theorem~5.1]{Pei26}) and hence
 $m_0=0$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:local}, \cite[Theorem~1.1]{AL26} for $\theta\le\frac12$ suffices
 for these limits.
\item \emph{Sources.} The upper half of \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ is Guerra's bound \cite[Section~6]{Tal07},
 proved for $\xi$ convex on $[-1,1]$ in Proposition~\ref{prop:A-guerra}, and
 \cite[Section~7]{Tal07} explains how the proof of the
 Parisi formula is modified to give the lower half for even $\xi$. By the preprint
 \cite[Theorem~2.1 and its proof]{CGKLM}, \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ holds for every $\xi$ finite on $\mathbb{R}$, with the
 Guerra-type upper bound written out for convex $\xi$ and sketched otherwise, and the lower half
 \cite[Lemma~2.6]{CGKLM} written as modifications of the Aizenman--Sims--Starr scheme; this is
 the only source we know for covariances with a term of odd degree, such as the pure $p$-spin
 models with odd $p$ and the mixtures of Theorem~\ref{thm:atom}(c). For the
 Sherrington--Kirkpatrick covariance, \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ is the one-level case of \cite[Theorem~2.1]{CM19}
 (Lemma~\ref{lem:A-fm-sk}), and the preprint \cite[Theorem~1.1]{AL26} gives a quantitative
 version for $0<\theta\le\frac12$.
\item \emph{A cubic term.} The covariances of Theorem~\ref{thm:atom}(c) are convex on $[-1,1]$
 (Proposition~\ref{prop:nc-support}(a), as $\varepsilon_3=\varepsilon_1$), so by (i) the bound
 $\limsup_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}(N^{-1}\logZ_N\gef_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta)\le\Sigma(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta)$,
 $0<\delta<f_1-f_{\mathrm{eq}}$, holds for them without \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}; when $\xi$ is finite on $\mathbb{R}$, \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\
 from \cite[Theorem~2.1]{CGKLM} and Theorem~\ref{thm:atom}(d) turn \eqref{eq:atom-odd-rate} into
 the exponent of $\mathbb{P}(N^{-1}\logZ_N\gef_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta)$.
\item \emph{Even $p$.} For the pure $p$-spin models with even $p$, $\xi$ is convex on $[-1,1]$,
 $m_0>0$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:pure-p}) and $P_{\zeta_*}=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. Taking $\zeta=\zeta_*$ in
 \eqref{eq:A-guerra}, Markov's inequality gives
 $\mathbb{P}(N^{-1}\logZ_N\gef_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta)\le e^{-N\theta\delta}$ for all $N$ and

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:A-approx}
Let $0<\theta<1$, and let $\mathcal D_\theta$ be the set of finitely supported
$\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ with $\zeta(\{0\})\ge\theta$ and $\zeta([0,t])<1$ for every $t<1$.
Every $\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ with $\zeta(\{0\})\ge\theta$ is the limit in $W_1$ of a
sequence in $\mathcal D_\theta$. Consequently
$p(\theta)=\inf\{P_\zeta:\zeta\in\mathcal D_\theta\}$.
head: environment
name: Approximation by finitely supported measures

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\alpha(t)=\zeta([0,t])$. For an integer $n$ with $1-1/n\ge\theta$, define $\alpha_n(1)=1$
and $\alpha_n(t)=\min\{\alpha(k/n),1-1/n\}$ for $t\in[k/n,(k+1)/n)$, $0\le k\le n-1$. Then
$\alpha_n$ is nondecreasing and right-continuous, so it is the distribution function of a
measure $\zeta_n$ supported in $\{0,1/n,\dots,1\}$. Moreover
$\zeta_n(\{0\})=\min\{\alpha(0),1-1/n\}\ge\theta$ and $\alpha_n\le1-1/n$ on $[0,1)$, so
$\zeta_n\in\mathcal D_\theta$. For $t\in[k/n,(k+1)/n)$,
$0\le\alpha(t)-\alpha_n(t)\le\alpha(\frac{k+1}n)-\alpha(\frac kn)+\frac1n$,
and integration gives $W_1(\zeta_n,\zeta)\le2/n$. Since $\mathcal D_\theta$ lies in the
constraint set $\{\zeta(\{0\})\ge\theta\}$, the last assertion follows from the Lipschitz bound
\eqref{eq:cons-lipschitz}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $\theta\in(0,1)$. We use \cite{CM19} with one scale: in their notation $r=1$, $\zeta_0=\theta$,
$\gamma_0=0$ and $\gamma_1=\beta/\sqrt2$ \cite[(6), (8)]{CM19}.

\emph{The pressure is a fractional moment.} With one scale the auxiliary index $\alpha$ ranges
over $\mathbb{N}$, and two distinct indices meet at level $0$, where $\gamma_0=0$ \cite[(7),
(9)]{CM19}. The Hamiltonian \cite[(10)]{CM19} is therefore
$H_N(\sigma,\alpha)=N^{-1/2}\sum_{i,j=1}^Ng_{ij}(\alpha)\sigma_i\sigma_j$, where the families
$(g_{ij}(\alpha))_{i,j\le N}$, $\alpha\in\mathbb{N}$, are independent and consist of independent centered
Gaussian variables with variance $\gamma_1^2$. For each $\alpha$ the field
$\sigma\mapsto H_N(\sigma,\alpha)$ is centered Gaussian with covariance
$\gamma_1^2N^{-1}(\sigma\cdot\sigma')^2=N\xi(N^{-1}\sigma\cdot\sigma')$, exactly as in
\eqref{eq:intro-covariance}; the diagonal terms $i=j$ are included. The weights of
\cite[(15)]{CM19} are the Poisson--Dirichlet weights with parameter $\theta$, independent of the
Hamiltonian. Put $Z_\alpha=2^{-N}\sum_\sigma e^{H_N(\sigma,\alpha)}$; these are independent copies
of $Z_N$, and $\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\le(\mathbb{E}Z_N)^\theta<\infty$. By \eqref{eq:A-pd}, the pressure
\cite[(14)]{CM19} is
$p_N=N^{-1}\mathbb{E}\log\sum_{\alpha\ge1}\nu_\alpha\,2^NZ_\alpha=\log2+(N\theta)^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta$.

\emph{The trial functional is the Parisi functional.} A point of the trial set of
\cite[Definition~2.2]{CM19} consists of an integer $k\ge1$, numbers
$0=x_{-1}<x_0<x_1<\dots<x_k=1$, one of which, say $x_{m'}$ with $0\le m'<k$, equals $\theta$, and
numbers $0=q_0\le q_1\le\dots\le q_k=1$ \cite[(20), (21), (27)]{CM19}; we write $x_j$ for their
$\xi_j$. The coupling levels \cite[(25)--(26)]{CM19} are $\tilde\gamma_j=0$ for $j\le m'$ and
$\tilde\gamma_j=\gamma_1$ for $j>m'$. We read off three facts from the functional
\cite[(28)--(30)]{CM19}. First, the Gaussian increments with index $j\le m'$ vanish; the
increment with index $m'+1$ has variance $2\gamma_1^2q_{m'+1}=\xi'(q_{m'+1})$, and for $j>m'+1$ the
increment with index $j$ has variance $2\gamma_1^2(q_j-q_{j-1})=\xi'(q_j)-\xi'(q_{j-1})$.
Second, the recursion \cite[(29)]{CM19} integrates out the increment with index $j$ with the
exponent $x_{j-1}$, for $j=k,k-1,\dots,1$ (we read $J_p$ in \cite[(28)]{CM19} as $J_j$, and
the range of \cite[(29)]{CM19} as $1\le j\le k$); in particular the increment from $0$ to $q_{m'+1}$
carries the exponent $x_{m'}=\theta$. Third, the terminal function is $\log2+\log\cosh$, and the
deterministic term of \cite[(30)]{CM19} is
$\frac12\bigl\{\theta\gamma_1^2q_{m'+1}^2+\sum_{j=m'+1}^{k-1}x_j\gamma_1^2(q_{j+1}^2-q_j^2)\bigr\}$.

Let $\mu$ be the probability measure on $[0,1]$ whose distribution function equals $\theta$ on
$[0,q_{m'+1})$, equals $x_j$ on $[q_j,q_{j+1})$ for $m'<j<k$, and equals $1$ at $1$. Integrating
out a Gaussian variable of variance zero changes nothing, so the first two facts show that the
recursion of \cite[(28)--(29)]{CM19} is the recursion \eqref{eq:A-cole-hopf} for $\mu$, shifted
by $\log2$; hence its value is $\log2+\Phi_\mu(0,0)$. Since
$\gamma_1^2(b^2-a^2)=\int_a^bt\xi''(t)\,dt$, the deterministic term equals
$\frac12\int_0^1t\xi''(t)\mu([0,t])\,dt$. So the functional of \cite[(30)]{CM19} at this point
equals $\log2+P_\mu$. The measure $\mu$ is finitely supported, $\mu(\{0\})\ge\theta$, and
$\mu([0,t])\le x_{k-1}<1$ for $t<1$; that is, $\mu\in\mathcal D_\theta$.

Conversely, every $\mu\in\mathcal D_\theta$ arises in this way. Let $v_0<v_1<\dots<v_n$ be the
values of $\mu([0,t])$ for $t\in[0,1)$, so that $v_0=\mu(\{0\})\ge\theta$ and $v_n<1$, and let
$0=s_0<s_1<\dots<s_n<s_{n+1}=1$ be such that $\mu([0,t])=v_i$ for $t\in[s_i,s_{i+1})$. If
$v_0=\theta$, take $k=n+1$, $x_j=v_j$ for $j\le n$, and $q_j=s_j$ for $1\le j\le k$. If
$v_0>\theta$, take $k=n+2$, $x_0=\theta$, $x_j=v_{j-1}$ for $1\le j\le n+1$, $q_1=0$, and
$q_j=s_{j-1}$ for $2\le j\le k$. In both cases $m'=0$, and the construction of the previous
paragraph returns $\mu$.

\emph{Conclusion.} The infimum of the trial functional is therefore
$\log2+\inf\{P_\mu:\mu\in\mathcal D_\theta\}=\log2+p(\theta)$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:A-approx}.
By \cite[Theorem~2.1]{CM19}, $p_N$ converges to this infimum, so
$(N\theta)^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\to p(\theta)$. Multiplying by $\theta$ gives \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let first $\zeta$ be finitely supported. By \eqref{eq:A-exponents} every coefficient
$y_{l+1}-y_l$ in \eqref{eq:A-derivative} is nonnegative. Each $\Delta_l(r)$ is the gap between
$\xi$ and its tangent line at $q_l\in[0,1]$, so it is nonnegative for $r\in[-1,1]$ because $\xi$
is convex there; and $R(\sigma,\tau)\in[-1,1]$. Hence
$\varphi'(u)\le-\frac12\sum_jy_j\{\psi(q_j)-\psi(q_{j-1})\}$ for $u\in(0,1)$, and the mean value
theorem gives \eqref{eq:A-reduced}, that is, \eqref{eq:A-guerra}. For a general $\zeta$ with
$\zeta(\{0\})\ge\theta$, Lemma~\ref{lem:A-approx} gives finitely supported $\zeta_n$ with
$\zeta_n(\{0\})\ge\theta$ and $W_1(\zeta_n,\zeta)\to0$; apply \eqref{eq:A-guerra} to $\zeta_n$
and let $n\to\infty$, using \eqref{eq:cons-lipschitz}. Taking the infimum over $\zeta$ gives
$(N\theta)^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\le p(\theta)$, and multiplying by $\theta$ gives the last
assertion.

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $H_u=\sum_{\ell=0}^LX_\ell$ with $X_0=\sqrt u\,H_N$ and
$X_\ell(\sigma)=\sqrt{1-u}\,z^\ell\cdot\sigma$ for $\ell\ge1$; the process $X_\ell$ is a function
of level $\ell$, and these processes are independent.

\emph{Regularity.} Put $M=\max_\sigma|H_N(\sigma)|+\sum_{j,i}|z^j_i|$, which has exponential
moments of every order. Then $|H_u(\sigma)|\le M$ for all $u$ and $\sigma$, so
$e^{-M}\le Y_L\le e^M$. A power mean with exponent in $(0,1]$ lies between the geometric and
the arithmetic mean, so by induction
$\exp(-\mathbb{E}_{j+1}\cdots\mathbb{E}_LM)\le Y_j\le\mathbb{E}_{j+1}\cdots\mathbb{E}_Le^M$ for every $j$ and $u$. Hence every
quantity below, and its derivative in $u$ on a compact subset of $(0,1)$, is bounded by
$Ce^{CM}$ for a constant $C$. Dominated convergence therefore justifies the differentiations
under the expectations and the Gaussian integrations by parts below, and it gives continuity of
$\varphi$ on $[0,1]$.

\emph{Weights.} For $0\le j\le L$ put $V_j=Y_j^{y_j}/\mathbb{E}_jY_j^{y_j}$; it depends on the levels
$0,\dots,j$, and $\mathbb{E}_jV_j=1$. Let $\pi(\sigma)=2^{-N}e^{H_u(\sigma)}/Y_L$ be the Gibbs weights.
For a function $F$ of all levels put $\mathcal A_LF=F$ and
$\mathcal A_{j-1}F=\mathbb{E}_j[V_j\,\mathcal A_jF]$ for $j=L,\dots,1$; thus $\mathcal A_jF$ depends on
the levels $0,\dots,j$, and $\mathcal A_j1=1$. Since the levels are independent, with
$V=V_0V_1\cdots V_L$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A-tower}
 \mathbb{E}[VF]=\mathbb{E}\bigl[V_0\cdots V_j\,\mathcal A_jF\bigr]\qquad(0\le j\le L).
\end{equation}
For $0\le l\le L$ define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A-pair-measures}
 \mu_{u,l}(\sigma,\tau)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[V_0\cdots V_l\;\mathcal A_l\pi(\sigma)\;\mathcal A_l\pi(\tau)\bigr].
\end{equation}
These numbers are nonnegative and sum to $\mathbb{E}[V_0\cdots V_l]=1$.

\emph{The derivative.} Differentiating the recursion gives
\begin{gather*}
 \partial_u\log Y_L=\sum_\sigma\pi(\sigma)\,\partial_uH_u(\sigma),\qquad
 \partial_u\log Y_{j-1}=\mathbb{E}_j\bigl[V_j\,\partial_u\log Y_j\bigr]\quad(1\le j\le L),\\
 \partial_u\log\mathbb{E}_0Y_0^\theta=\theta\,\mathbb{E}_0\bigl[V_0\,\partial_u\log Y_0\bigr].
\end{gather*}
By \eqref{eq:A-tower} with $j=0$,
\[
 N\varphi'(u)=\sum_{\ell=0}^L\mathbb{E}\Bigl[V\sum_\sigma\pi(\sigma)G_\ell(\sigma)\Bigr],\qquad
 G_0=\frac{H_N}{2\sqrt u},\quad G_\ell(\sigma)=-\frac{z^\ell\cdot\sigma}{2\sqrt{1-u}}\ (\ell\ge1).
\]

\emph{Integration by parts at level $\ell$.} Fix $\ell$ and condition on the other levels. The
pair $(G_\ell,X_\ell)$ is a centered Gaussian process, and the integrand depends on level $\ell$
only through the values $X_\ell(\tau)$, $\tau\in\{-1,1\}^N$. Gaussian integration by parts gives
\[
 \mathbb{E}\Bigl[V\sum_\sigma\pi(\sigma)G_\ell(\sigma)\Bigr]
 =\sum_{\sigma,\tau}c_\ell(\sigma,\tau)\,
 \mathbb{E}\Bigl[\frac{\partial(V\pi(\sigma))}{\partial X_\ell(\tau)}\Bigr],
 \qquad c_\ell(\sigma,\tau)=\mathbb{E}\,G_\ell(\sigma)X_\ell(\tau).
\]
To compute the derivative, note that $Y_j$ does not depend on level $\ell$ when $j<\ell$. For
$j\ge\ell$, induction from $j=L$, where $\partial\log Y_L/\partial X_\ell(\tau)=\pi(\tau)$, gives
$\partial\log Y_j/\partial X_\ell(\tau)=\mathcal A_j\pi(\tau)$, because $\mathbb{E}_j$ does not
integrate level $\ell$ when $j>\ell$. Consequently $\partial\log V_j/\partial X_\ell(\tau)$ is
$0$ for $j<\ell$; it is $y_\ell\,\mathcal A_\ell\pi(\tau)$ for $j=\ell$, since the normalization
$\mathbb{E}_\ell Y_\ell^{y_\ell}$ does not depend on level $\ell$; and it is
$y_j\{\mathcal A_j\pi(\tau)-\mathcal A_{j-1}\pi(\tau)\}$ for $j>\ell$. Together with
$\partial\log\pi(\sigma)/\partial X_\ell(\tau)=\mathbf{1}_{\sigma=\tau}-\pi(\tau)$, and after
regrouping with $y_{L+1}=1$ and $\mathcal A_L\pi=\pi$,
\[
 \frac{\partial(V\pi(\sigma))}{\partial X_\ell(\tau)}
 =V\pi(\sigma)\Bigl[\mathbf{1}_{\sigma=\tau}-\sum_{l=\ell}^L(y_{l+1}-y_l)\,\mathcal A_l\pi(\tau)\Bigr].
\]
Since $\mathcal A_l\pi(\tau)$ depends on the levels $0,\dots,l$ only, \eqref{eq:A-tower} gives
$\mathbb{E}[V\pi(\sigma)\,\mathcal A_l\pi(\tau)]=\mu_{u,l}(\sigma,\tau)$. The diagonal value
$\bar c_\ell=c_\ell(\sigma,\sigma)$ does not depend on $\sigma$ (see below), and
$\sum_\sigma\mathbb{E}[V\pi(\sigma)]=1$. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A-ibp}
 \mathbb{E}\Bigl[V\sum_\sigma\pi(\sigma)G_\ell(\sigma)\Bigr]
 =\bar c_\ell-\sum_{l=\ell}^L(y_{l+1}-y_l)\sum_{\sigma,\tau}\mu_{u,l}(\sigma,\tau)\,
 c_\ell(\sigma,\tau).
\end{equation}

\emph{Covariances.} With $R=R(\sigma,\tau)$,
\[
 c_0(\sigma,\tau)=\tfrac12\mathbb{E} H_N(\sigma)H_N(\tau)=\tfrac N2\,\xi(R),\qquad
 c_\ell(\sigma,\tau)=-\tfrac N2\bigl\{\xi'(q_\ell)-\xi'(q_{\ell-1})\bigr\}R\quad(\ell\ge1),
\]
and $R(\sigma,\sigma)=1$; so $\bar c_0=\frac N2\xi(1)$, and
$\bar c_\ell=-\frac N2\{\xi'(q_\ell)-\xi'(q_{\ell-1})\}$ for $\ell\ge1$. Write
$\mu_{u,l}[F]=\sum_{\sigma,\tau}\mu_{u,l}(\sigma,\tau)\,F(R(\sigma,\tau))$. Summing
\eqref{eq:A-ibp} over $\ell$, the diagonal values add up to
$\frac N2\{\xi(1)-\xi'(1)\}=-\frac N2\psi(1)$, because $\xi'(q_0)=0$. In the remaining terms
with $\ell\ge1$ we exchange the sums over $\ell$ and $l$; since
$\sum_{\ell=1}^l\{\xi'(q_\ell)-\xi'(q_{\ell-1})\}=\xi'(q_l)$, which vanishes for $l=0$,
\[
 \varphi'(u)=-\frac12\psi(1)
 -\frac12\sum_{l=0}^L(y_{l+1}-y_l)\,\mu_{u,l}\bigl[\xi(R)-\xi'(q_l)R\bigr].
\]
Finally, $\xi(r)-\xi'(q_l)r=\Delta_l(r)-\psi(q_l)$, and summation by parts with $\psi(q_0)=0$,
$q_L=1$ and $y_{L+1}=1$ gives
$\sum_{l=0}^L(y_{l+1}-y_l)\psi(q_l)=\psi(1)-\sum_{j=1}^Ly_j\{\psi(q_j)-\psi(q_{j-1})\}$. Since
each $\mu_{u,l}$ is a probability measure, \eqref{eq:A-derivative} follows.

label: rem:A-normalizations
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:A-normalizations}
\begin{steplist}
\item \emph{Terminal value.} Our terminal value $\log\cosh x$ in \eqref{eq:intro-pde} and our
 partition function $Z_N=2^{-N}\sum_\sigma e^{H_N(\sigma)}$ are those of \cite[(1.2)--(1.4)]{Bou26b} and, with the
 uniform reference measure on spins, of \cite[(2.2), (2.4)]{CGKLM}. With $\log(2\cosh x)$, as in
 \cite{CPS23}, \cite[(1.4)--(1.5)]{Bou26a}, \cite[(1.2)]{AL26} and \cite[(28)]{CM19}, or with
 $\log2$ added to the functional, as in \cite[(1.3)]{Lop26a}, the Parisi functional, $f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and
 $p(\theta)$ exceed ours by $\log2$. This matches the passage from $Z_N$ to
 $\sum_\sigma e^{H_N(\sigma)}=2^NZ_N$: $\Lambda(\theta)$ becomes $\Lambda(\theta)+\theta\log2$,
 and $\Sigma$ is unchanged once $f$ is shifted by $\log2$. Thus the constrained minimum of
 Aronow and Lopatto is $P_\beta(s)=p(s)+\log2$, with $s$ in the role of $\theta$
 \cite[(1.2)]{AL26}.
\item \emph{The Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Hamiltonian.} For $\xi(t)=\beta^2t^2/2$, a field with
 covariance exactly $N\xi(N^{-1}\sigma\cdot\sigma')$ is obtained by summing over all ordered
 pairs, the diagonal included, for instance $\beta(2N)^{-1/2}\sum_{i,j=1}^Ng_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j$ with independent standard
 Gaussian $g_{ij}$ \cite[(1.1)]{Lop26a}, or the
 one-scale Hamiltonian of \cite[(10)]{CM19} with $\gamma_1=\beta/\sqrt2$. The original model
 $F_{N,\beta}$ sums over $i<j$ only; its completion $F_{N,\beta}+\beta D_N$ \cite[Section~1.1]{AL26}, with $D_N$
 centered Gaussian of variance $\frac12$ and independent of $F_{N,\beta}$ (as in the proof of
 Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-original-sk}), has the law of $\logZ_N+N\log2$. Hence, for $0<\theta<1$,
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:A-original-moments}
  \mathbb{E} e^{\thetaF_{N,\beta}}=e^{-\theta^2\beta^2/4}\,2^{\theta N}\,\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta ,
 \end{equation}
 and Lemma~\ref{lem:A-fm-sk} holds for $F_{N,\beta}$ with $\Lambda(\theta)$ replaced by
 $\Lambda(\theta)+\theta\log2$.
\end{steplist}

label: rem:B-kondor
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:B-kondor}
Near the critical temperature, Kondor \cite{Kon83} found that $\Phi(n)$ starts at order $n^5$
\cite[(3)]{PR09}, with $\Phi(n)=\Phi(0)-\frac9{5120}n^5$ for the truncated model, as reported in
\cite[Section~IV]{PR09}; in \cite[Figure~3]{PR09}, $c_5^{\mathrm{PR}}\beta^{-5}=-\frac9{5120}$ at $T=1$,
consistent with (33) and the leading term $\dot q(0)=\frac12$ of their series (B6) at $T=1$. Here it
is the limit $c_\beta\to\frac9{5120}$, equivalently $\rho_\beta(0)\to2$, as $\beta\downarrow1$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:nearcrit}(a); Proposition~\ref{prop:nc-kondor}: $W_*\to-2$, $D_*\to4$),
and only a limit: at $\beta=1$, $\zeta_*=\delta_0$ (Section~\ref{sec:nc-reference}), \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ fails, the constraint is inactive
($\zeta_\theta=\delta_0$, $p(\theta)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ for every $\theta$) and the coefficient of $\theta^5$ is
zero; correspondingly, Parisi and Rizzo find that on the line $T=1$ the replica free energy is
$f_{\rm RS}$, the value of the solution $q=0$, for $n<2$ \cite[Section~III]{PR09}. The $o(1)$
terms of Theorem~\ref{thm:sk} are not uniform in $\beta$, nor those of Theorem~\ref{thm:local} in $\xi$; on
$\mathcal{K}(\varepsilon_*)$ the marginal regime ends at $\theta_c$ of order $a_0-1$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:nearcrit}(b), Remark~\ref{rem:nc-dat}).

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) Put $M_t=\int_0^t\sqrt{a(s)}\,dB_s$ and $\mathsf b(t,x)=a(t)\alpha_\zeta(t)\Phi_{\zeta,x}(t,x)$.
By the facts of Section~\ref{sec:fld-setting}, $\mathsf b$ is Borel, $|\mathsf b|\le\|a\|_\infty$ and
$|\mathsf b(t,x)-\mathsf b(t,y)|\le\|a\|_\infty|x-y|$. For each continuous path $M$, the integral
equation $Y_t=h+\int_0^t\mathsf b(s,Y_s+M_s)\,ds$ has a unique continuous solution (Picard
iteration, and Gronwall's inequality for uniqueness), and the solutions of \eqref{eq:fld-sde} are
exactly the processes $X=Y+M$. Thus $X^{\zeta,h}=\Pi_h(M)$ for a measurable map $\Pi_h$. Since
$\Phi_{\zeta,x}(t,\cdot)$ is odd, $\mathsf b(t,-x)=-\mathsf b(t,x)$, so $-\Pi_h(M)$ solves the
equation with data $(-h,-M)$, that is, $-\Pi_h(M)=\Pi_{-h}(-M)$. As $-M$ has the law of $M$,
$X^{\zeta,-h}$ has the law of $-X^{\zeta,h}$. The functions $\Phi_{\zeta,x}^2$ and
$\Phi_{\zeta,xx}^2$ are even in $x$, which gives the two identities of expectations. Evenness of
$\Phi_\zeta(0,\cdot)$ gives $P^{-h}_\zeta=P^h_\zeta$, and uniqueness of the minimizer gives
$\zeta_{-h}=\zeta_h$.

(b) Let $\mathcal G_n=\{k/n:0\le k\le n\}\cup\{q\}=\{s_0<s_1<\dots<s_{N_n}\}$, and move the mass of
$\zeta$ on each $(s_{i-1},s_i]$ to $s_i$:
$\zeta_n=\sum_{i=1}^{N_n}\zeta((s_{i-1},s_i])\,\delta_{s_i}$. This is a probability measure because
$\zeta(\{0\})=0$. Every atom moves by at most $1/n$, so $\zeta_n\to\zeta$ weakly. If $s_i<q$, then
$(s_{i-1},s_i]\subset(0,q)$ carries no mass, so $\zeta_n$ has no atom in $[0,q)$; let $t_1\ge q$
be its first atom. The Cole--Hopf form with $m=0$ on $[0,t_1)$ and the semigroup property of
Gaussian convolution give \eqref{eq:fld-heat} for $\zeta_n$, and it passes to $\zeta$ by the
uniform convergence of $\Phi_{\zeta_n}$ to $\Phi_\zeta$. On $[0,q)$ the drift in
\eqref{eq:fld-sde} vanishes because $\alpha_\zeta=0$ there, so
$X^{\zeta,h}_q=h+M_q\sim\mathcal N(h,\xi'(q))$, as $\xi'(0)=0$.

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) The derivatives $\partial_x^j\Phi_\zeta$, $j\ge1$, are continuous and bounded on
$[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$, and $X$ has continuous paths; apply dominated convergence.

\emph{Step 1: finitely atomic measures.} Let $\zeta$ have finitely many atoms, and let
$[t_l,t_{l+1})$ be an interval on which $\alpha_\zeta=m_l$. Put $\varphi=\Phi_\zeta(t_{l+1},\cdot)$;
it is smooth, its derivatives of positive order are bounded, and $|\varphi(y)|\le|\varphi(0)|+|y|$.
For $\tau>0$ the Gaussian convolution of $e^{m_l\varphi}$ (of $\varphi$ if $m_l=0$) with variance
$\tau$ is $C^\infty$ in $(\tau,x)$, positive, and solves the heat equation. Since
$\xi'(t_{l+1})-\xi'(s)$ is analytic and positive for $s<t_{l+1}$, the Cole--Hopf form shows that
$\Phi_\zeta$ is $C^\infty$ on $[t_l,t_{l+1})\times\mathbb{R}$ and solves the Parisi equation there
classically, with $\alpha_\zeta=m_l$. Hence $u=\Phi_{\zeta,x}$ satisfies
$u_t+\frac a2u_{xx}+am_luu_x=0$ there, and the generator of $X$ on this interval is
$\frac a2\partial_{xx}+am_lu\,\partial_x$. It\^o's formula on $[s_1,s_2]\subset[t_l,t_{l+1})$,
together with the equations obtained by differentiating the equation for $u$ in $x$, gives
\[
 du(t,X_t)=\sqrt a\,U_t\,dB_t,\qquad
 dU_t=-m_laU_t^2\,dt+\sqrt a\,V_t\,dB_t,\qquad
 dV_t=-3m_laU_tV_t\,dt+\sqrt a\,W_t\,dB_t .
\]
These use only the equation, not the starting point. All stochastic integrands are bounded, so
the martingale parts have mean zero, and
\begin{align}
 \mathbb{E} u(s_2,X_{s_2})^2-\mathbb{E} u(s_1,X_{s_1})^2&=\int_{s_1}^{s_2}a\,\mathbb{E} U_s^2\,ds,\label{eq:fld-I1}\\
 \mathbb{E} U_{s_2}^2-\mathbb{E} U_{s_1}^2&=\int_{s_1}^{s_2}a\,\mathbb{E}\bigl(V_s^2-2m_lU_s^3\bigr)\,ds,\label{eq:fld-I2}\\
 \mathbb{E}\bigl(V^2-2m_lU^3\bigr)_{s_2}-\mathbb{E}\bigl(V^2-2m_lU^3\bigr)_{s_1}
 &=\int_{s_1}^{s_2}a\,\mathbb{E}\bigl(W_s^2-12m_lU_sV_s^2+6m_l^2U_s^4\bigr)\,ds.\label{eq:fld-I3}
\end{align}
By part~(a), \eqref{eq:fld-I1} and \eqref{eq:fld-I2} extend to $s_2=t_{l+1}$. Summing over the
intervals, \eqref{eq:fld-I1} holds for all $0\le s_1\le s_2\le1$, and so does \eqref{eq:fld-I2}
with $m_l$ replaced by $\alpha_\zeta(s)$ inside the integral.

\emph{Step 2: general measures.} Let $S\subset(0,1)$ be finite, let
$\mathcal G_n=\{k/n:0\le k\le n\}\cup S$, and define a finitely atomic measure $\zeta_n$ by its
distribution function $\alpha_n(s)=\alpha_\zeta(\max\{g\in\mathcal G_n:g\le s\})$ for $s<1$ and
$\alpha_n(1)=1$. Since $\alpha_\zeta(s-1/n)\le\alpha_n(s)\le\alpha_\zeta(s)$, $\alpha_n\to\alpha_\zeta$ at
every continuity point of $\alpha_\zeta$; hence $\zeta_n\to\zeta$ weakly and
$W_1(\zeta_n,\zeta)\to0$. If $\alpha_\zeta=m$ on an open interval $I$ and $s_1<s_2$ are points of
$S\cap I$, then $\alpha_n=m$ on $[s_1,s_2]$. Let $X^n$ solve \eqref{eq:fld-sde} for $\zeta_n$ with
the same Brownian motion and $X^n_0=h$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-diffusion}(a)), and put
$u_n=\Phi_{\zeta_n,x}$ and $u=\Phi_{\zeta,x}$. The martingale parts cancel, and since
$\alpha_n\le1$, $|u|\le1$ and $|u_x|\le1$,
\[
 |X^n_t-X_t|\le\|a\|_\infty\Bigl(\|u_n-u\|_\infty+W_1(\zeta_n,\zeta)
 +\int_0^t|X^n_s-X_s|\,ds\Bigr).
\]
Gronwall's inequality gives, on every path,
$\sup_t|X^n_t-X_t|\le\|a\|_\infty e^{\|a\|_\infty}\bigl(\|u_n-u\|_\infty+W_1(\zeta_n,\zeta)\bigr)$,
which tends to zero. Then, for $j\ge1$,
\[
 \sup_t\bigl|\partial_x^j\Phi_{\zeta_n}(t,X^n_t)-\partial_x^j\Phi_\zeta(t,X_t)\bigr|
 \le\|\partial_x^j(\Phi_{\zeta_n}-\Phi_\zeta)\|_\infty+B_{j+1}\sup_t|X^n_t-X_t|\longrightarrow0 .
\]
All these quantities are bounded by the constants $B_j$, so expectations of polynomials in them
converge uniformly in $t$; also $\alpha_n\to\alpha_\zeta$ almost everywhere. By dominated
convergence in the time integrals, \eqref{eq:fld-I1} and \eqref{eq:fld-I2} (with
$\alpha_\zeta(s)$ in the integrand) hold for $\zeta$ and all $0\le s_1\le s_2\le1$, and
\eqref{eq:fld-I3} holds for $\zeta$ on $[s_1,s_2]$ whenever $\alpha_\zeta=m$ on an open interval
containing $[s_1,s_2]$ (take $S=\{s_1,s_2\}$ and $m_l=m$).

\emph{Step 3: conclusions.} (b) By \eqref{eq:fld-I1} and part~(a),
$\Gamma(s_2)-\Gamma(s_1)=\int_{s_1}^{s_2}a\,\mathbb{E} U_s^2\,ds$ with a continuous integrand. (c) Let
$A(t)=\mathbb{E} U_t^2$. By part~(a) and right continuity of $\alpha_\zeta$, the integrand
$a(s)\mathbb{E}(V_s^2-2\alpha_\zeta(s)U_s^3)$ in \eqref{eq:fld-I2} is right continuous, so $A$ has the right
derivative $a(t)\mathbb{E}(V_t^2-2\alpha_\zeta(t)U_t^3)$ at every $t\in[0,1)$. Since $\Gamma'=aA$ and
$a\in C^1$, part~(c) follows. (d) On $I$ both integrands in \eqref{eq:fld-I2} and
\eqref{eq:fld-I3} are continuous by part~(a). Hence $A$ and $R(t)=\mathbb{E}(V_t^2-2mU_t^3)$ are $C^1$ on
$I$, with $A'=aR$ and $R'=a\mathbb{E}(W^2-12mUV^2+6m^2U^4)$. Differentiating $\Gamma'=aA$ twice gives
\eqref{eq:fld-second} and \eqref{eq:fld-third}.

title: Proof
body_md:
We use \cite[Proposition~1.1]{JT17}, applied with $\beta=1$ and $\xi_0=\xi$; its hypothesis
$\xi_0(1+\epsilon)<\infty$ holds because the radius of convergence exceeds one. In \cite{JT17}
the functional and the diffusion are built from the unique weak solution $u_\zeta$ of the Parisi
equation in the class of continuous functions on $[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$ with essentially bounded weak
derivative $\partial_xu_\zeta$ \cite[Section~8.1 and Proposition~8.1]{JT17}. We first check that
$u_\zeta=\Phi_\zeta$. Let $\zeta$ be finitely atomic. Then $\Phi_\zeta$ is continuous on
$[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$ with $|\Phi_{\zeta,x}|\le1$, and by Step~1 of the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-ito} it is $C^\infty$ on each strip $[t_l,t_{l+1})\times\mathbb{R}$ and solves the
Parisi equation classically there. Hence
$0\le-\partial_t\Phi_\zeta=\frac a2(\Phi_{\zeta,xx}+m_l\Phi_{\zeta,x}^2)\le\|a\|_\infty$ on each
strip, and $\Phi_\zeta(\cdot,x)$ is Lipschitz on $[0,1]$. Let
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty((0,1]\times\mathbb{R})$. Integrating by parts once in $t$ over $[0,1]$ and twice in
$x$, and using $\Phi_\zeta(1,x)=\log\cosh x$ and $\varphi=0$ near $t=0$, we can write the weak
formulation of \cite[Section~8.1]{JT17} as
\[
 \int_0^1\!\!\int_\mathbb{R}\Bigl(\partial_t\Phi_\zeta+\frac a2\bigl\{
 \Phi_{\zeta,xx}+\alpha_\zeta\Phi_{\zeta,x}^2\bigr\}\Bigr)\varphi\,dx\,dt=0,
\]
which holds because the integrand vanishes off the finitely many atom times. Thus $\Phi_\zeta$ is
a weak solution, and $\Phi_\zeta=u_\zeta$ by uniqueness. For general $\zeta$, take finitely atomic
$\zeta_n$ with $W_1(\zeta_n,\zeta)\to0$, as in Step~2 of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-ito}.
Then $\Phi_{\zeta_n}\to\Phi_\zeta$ uniformly, and $u_{\zeta_n}\to u_\zeta$ uniformly by
\cite[Proposition~8.2]{JT17}, which is stated for the same metric. Hence $u_\zeta=\Phi_\zeta$.
Consequently the Parisi functional of \cite{JT17} at field $h$ is $P^h_\zeta$, its minimizer is
$\zeta_h$, its diffusion is \eqref{eq:fld-sde}, and its function $G_\mu$
\cite[(1.1.1)]{JT17} is $\mathcal{O}_{\zeta,h}$.

Let $h\ge0$. By \cite[Proposition~1.1]{JT17} (see also \cite[Corollary~3.6]{JT17}; these results were obtained independently in \cite{Che17}, see \cite[Remark~1.3]{JT17}), $\zeta_h$ gives
full mass to the closed set of minimizers of $\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_h,h}$ over $[0,1]$, so $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_h$
is contained in that set. The same proposition also states \eqref{eq:fld-sc} at every support
point, but its inequality is derived \cite[Corollary~3.10]{JT17} from derivative formulas whose
proofs are omitted there \cite[Lemma~8.4]{JT17}. At points of $(0,1)$ we derive
\eqref{eq:fld-sc} from the support statement instead. By Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-ito}(b),
$\Gamma=\Gamma_{\zeta_h,h}$ is $C^1$, so $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_h,h}$ is $C^2$ on $[0,1]$ with
$\mathcal{O}'=-\frac a2(\Gamma-t)$ and $\mathcal{O}''=-\frac{a'}2(\Gamma-t)-\frac a2(\Gamma'-1)$. At an interior
minimum, $\mathcal{O}'=0\le\mathcal{O}''$; since $a>0$, this gives \eqref{eq:fld-sc}, as in
Section~\ref{sec:plat-obstacle}.

For $h<0$, part~(a) gives $\zeta_h=\zeta_{-h}$ and $\Gamma_{\zeta_h,h}=\Gamma_{\zeta_{-h},-h}$, hence
$\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_h,h}=\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_{-h},-h}$, and the expectation in \eqref{eq:fld-sc} is the same for
$h$ and $-h$; so the statements for $-h>0$ transfer.

If $h\ne0$, then $\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_h,h}$ is $C^1$ with
$\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_h,h}'(0)=-\fraca_02\Gamma_{\zeta_h,h}(0)=-\fraca_02\Phi_{\zeta_h,x}(0,h)^2<0$,
because $X_0=h$ and $\Phi_{\zeta_h,x}(0,\cdot)$ is odd and strictly increasing. So zero is not a
minimizer of $\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_h,h}$ and does not lie in $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_h$; for $h>0$ this is also
\cite[Lemma~3.9]{JT17}.

title: Proof
body_md:
If $h_n\to h$ and $\zeta_n\to\zeta$ weakly, then $P^{h_n}_{\zeta_n}\to P^h_\zeta$: indeed
$|\Phi_{\zeta_n}(0,h_n)-\Phi_\zeta(0,h)|\le\|\Phi_{\zeta_n}-\Phi_\zeta\|_\infty+|h_n-h|$, which tends
to zero, and $\alpha_{\zeta_n}\to\alpha_\zeta$ in $L^1$. Let $h_n\to h$, and let $\zeta'$ be a weak
limit point of $(\zeta_{h_n})$; the space of probability measures on $[0,1]$ is compact. Along the
corresponding subsequence, for every $\nu$,
$P^h_{\zeta'}=\lim P^{h_n}_{\zeta_{h_n}}\le\lim P^{h_n}_\nu=P^h_\nu$, so $\zeta'=\zeta_h$ by
uniqueness. Hence $h\mapsto\zeta_h$ is weakly continuous. By Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-diffusion}(a),
$\zeta_{-h}=\zeta_h$ and $\mathcal{F}$ is even; since $\Phi_{\zeta_h,x}(0,\cdot)$ is odd,
$\mathfrak{m}(-h)=-\mathfrak{m}(h)$.

Fix $h$ and $k\ne0$. Comparing each minimizer in the other problem,
\[
 \Phi_{\zeta_{h+k}}(0,h+k)-\Phi_{\zeta_{h+k}}(0,h)
 \le\mathcal{F}(h+k)-\mathcal{F}(h)
 \le\Phi_{\zeta_h}(0,h+k)-\Phi_{\zeta_h}(0,h).
\]
By the mean value theorem both bounds equal $k\,\Phi_{\zeta,x}(0,y)$, with
$\zeta\in\{\zeta_h,\zeta_{h+k}\}$ and $y$ between $h$ and $h+k$. Since $\Phi_{\zeta,xx}\le1$,
$|\Phi_{\zeta,x}(0,y)-\Phi_{\zeta_h,x}(0,h)|\le\|\Phi_{\zeta,x}-\Phi_{\zeta_h,x}\|_\infty+|y-h|$,
which tends to zero as $k\to0$ by jet stability and the continuity just proved. Dividing by $k$
(the two bounds have the same limit for either sign of $k$) gives $\mathcal{F}'(h)=\mathfrak{m}(h)$, and
the same estimate shows that $\mathfrak{m}$ is continuous.

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $X=X^{\zeta,h}$ and, for $k=2,3,4$, $j_k=\partial_x^k\Phi_{\zeta_*}(0,0)$. Thus $j_2=U_*$,
$j_4=W_*$, and $j_3=0$ because $\Phi_{\zeta_*}(0,\cdot)$ is even. Let $Q_m(t,x;\zeta)$ be the
expression defining $\Psi_{\zeta,h}(t,m)$, the right side of \eqref{eq:plat-psi}, with the
expectations removed and $U,V,W$ replaced by $\partial_x^k\Phi_\zeta(t,x)$, $k=2,3,4$; thus
$\Psi_{\zeta,h}(t,m)=\mathbb{E} Q_m(t,X_t;\zeta)$. Since $a'(0)=\xi'''(0)=0$ and $a''(0)=\xi''''(0)$, its
value at the reference point is
\[
 Q_m^*:=\xi''''(0)j_2^2+a_0^3\bigl(j_4^2+6m^2j_2^4\bigr)=D_*+6m^2a_0^3U_*^4 .
\]
The function $Q_m$ is a polynomial in $(a,a',a'',m)$ and in the three jets, which range over a
fixed compact set by the uniform bounds of Section~\ref{sec:fld-setting}. Hence
$|Q_m|\le Q_{\max}$ and, with a constant $L$ uniform in $m\in[0,1]$,
\[
 |Q_m(t,x;\zeta)-Q_m^*|\le L\Bigl(\delta(t)+\sum_{k=2}^4|\partial_x^k\Phi_\zeta(t,x)-j_k|\Bigr),
 \qquad \delta(t)=|a(t)-a_0|+|a'(t)|+|a''(t)-a''(0)| ,
\]
where $\delta(t)\to0$ as $t\to0$. Put
$\varepsilon(\zeta)=\max_{2\le k\le4}\|\partial_x^k(\Phi_\zeta-\Phi_{\zeta_*})\|_\infty$, which is at
most $C'W_1(\zeta,\zeta_*)$ by jet stability, with $C'=\max_{2\le k\le4}C_k\|a\|_\infty$, and
\[
 \omega(r)=\max_{2\le k\le4}\ \sup_{0\le t\le r,\ |x|\le r}
 \bigl|\partial_x^k\Phi_{\zeta_*}(t,x)-j_k\bigr|,
\]
which tends to zero as $r\to0$ by continuity of the jets. The drift in \eqref{eq:fld-sde} is
bounded by $\|a\|_\infty$, so, as in \eqref{eq:plat-small-time},
$\mathbb{E}|X_t-h|^2\le2\|a\|_\infty t+2\|a\|_\infty^2t^2$. Let $0<r\le1$, $t\le r$ and $|h|\le r/2$.
Chebyshev's inequality gives
$\mathbb{P}(|X_t|>r)\le\mathbb{P}(|X_t-h|>r/2)\le8(\|a\|_\infty t+\|a\|_\infty^2t^2)/r^2$, and on the event
$\{|X_t|\le r\}$ each jet differs from $j_k$ by at most $\varepsilon(\zeta)+\omega(r)$. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fld-plateau-error}
 \sup_{0\le m\le1}\bigl|\Psi_{\zeta,h}(t,m)-Q_m^*\bigr|
 \le L\bigl(\delta(t)+3\varepsilon(\zeta)+3\omega(r)\bigr)
 +\frac{16Q_{\max}}{r^2}\bigl(\|a\|_\infty t+\|a\|_\infty^2t^2\bigr).
\end{equation}
Given $\eta>0$, choose $r\in(0,1]$ with $3L\omega(r)\le\eta/4$, and then $t_0\in(0,r]$ such that
the terms in $\delta(t)$ and in $t$ are each at most $\eta/4$ for $t\le t_0$. The left side of
\eqref{eq:fld-plateau-error} is then at most $\eta$ whenever $t\le t_0$, $|h|\le r/2$ and
$3LC'W_1(\zeta,\zeta_*)\le\eta/4$. This proves the first claim. For the second, take
$\eta=D_*/2$, which is positive by Remark~\ref{rem:fld-nondegeneracy}, and put
$K_{\rm fld}=\min\{t_0,1/2\}$, $h_0=r/2$ and $\varepsilon_{\rm fld}=\eta/(12LC')$. If $\alpha_\zeta=m$ on an open
interval $I\subset(0,K_{\rm fld})$, then, by Lemma~\ref{lem:fld-ito}(d), $\Gamma_{\zeta,h}'''=\Psi_{\zeta,h}(\cdot,m)\ge Q_m^*-D_*/2\geD_*/2$
on $I$.

body_md:
Let $T_{k-1}g$ denote the Taylor polynomial of degree $k-1$ at zero of a function $g$. If
$\|g^{(k)}\|_\infty\le C''$, Taylor's theorem gives $|g(x)-T_{k-1}g(x)|\le C''|x|^k/k!$ on
$\mathbb{R}$. We use $\mathbb{E} X^2=h^2+\sigma^2$, $\mathbb{E} X^4=h^4+6h^2\sigma^2+3\sigma^4$,
$\mathbb{E} X^6=h^6+15h^4\sigma^2+45h^2\sigma^4+15\sigma^6$ and $\mathbb{E}|X|^k\le C_k''(h^k+\sigma^k)$; since
$h,\sigma\le1$, higher powers are absorbed into lower ones.

For \eqref{eq:fld-t1}, write $v=p+r$ with $p(x)=c_1x+c_3x^3/6+c_5x^5/120$. The remainder $r$ is
odd and $|r'(x)|\le C|x|^6/6!$. Since $Z$ and $-Z$ have the same law,
$\mathbb{E} r(h+\sigma Z)=\frac12\mathbb{E}[r(\sigma Z+h)-r(\sigma Z-h)]$, which is at most
$h\,\mathbb{E}\sup_{|s|\le h}|r'(\sigma Z+s)|=O(h(\sigma^6+h^6))$ in absolute value. Also
$\mathbb{E} p(X)=c_1h+\frac{c_3}6(h^3+3h\sigma^2)+\frac{c_5}{120}(h^5+10h^3\sigma^2+15h\sigma^4)$.

For \eqref{eq:fld-t2}, $v'^2$ is even, with
$T_5(v'^2)(x)=c_1^2+c_1c_3x^2+(\frac14c_3^2+\frac1{12}c_1c_5)x^4$ and remainder bounded by a
constant times $x^6$.

For \eqref{eq:fld-t3}, $v^2$ is even, with
$T_7(v^2)(x)=c_1^2x^2+\frac13c_1c_3x^4+(\frac1{36}c_3^2+\frac1{60}c_1c_5)x^6$ and remainder bounded
by a constant times $x^8$; here $|v|\le1$ is used. Take expectations and subtract $\sigma^2$
times the expansion of $\mathbb{E} v'(X)^2$ before truncation. The terms of order $\sigma^2$ and
$\sigma^4$ cancel, and the coefficient of $\sigma^6$ is
\[
 15\Bigl(\frac1{36}c_3^2+\frac1{60}c_1c_5\Bigr)-3\Bigl(\frac14c_3^2+\frac1{12}c_1c_5\Bigr)
 =-\frac13c_3^2 .
\]
Every remaining polynomial term contains $h^2\sigma^2$ or $h^4$, and the truncation errors are
$O(h^8+\sigma^8+\sigma^2h^6)$.

label: prop:atom-odd-structure
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:atom-odd-structure}
Every $\xi\in\mathcal{K}_3(\varepsilon_3)$, where $\varepsilon_3=\varepsilon_1\in(0,\frac14]$, has
the following properties.
\begin{thmlist}
\item $\xi''\ge1-\varepsilon_3$ on $[-1,1]$; in particular $\xi$ is strictly convex on
 $[-1,1]$.
\item $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_*=[0,v_*]$ for some $v_*\in(0,K)$. Moreover $U_*=a_0^{-1/2}$,
 \[
  m_0=\frac{\xi'''(0)}{2\xi''(0)^{3/2}}=\frac{3\beta_3^2}{(2\beta_2^2)^{3/2}}\in(0,1),
  \qquad
  D_*=\frac{\xi''''(0)}{a_0}-\frac{3\xi'''(0)^2}{2a_0^2}+a_0^3W_*^2 .
 \]
\item For $0\le\theta\le m_0$, $\zeta_\theta=\zeta_*$ and $p(\theta)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. For
 $m_0<\theta<1$, $\zeta_\theta(\{0\})=\theta$ and $p(\theta)>f_{\mathrm{eq}}$, the first positive
 contact $q_\theta$ of $\zeta_\theta$ exists and satisfies $\zeta_\theta((0,q_\theta))=0$,
 $\Gamma_\theta(q_\theta)=q_\theta$ and $\Gamma_\theta'(q_\theta)\le1$, and $p$ is
 differentiable at $\theta$ with
 $p'(\theta)=\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_\theta}(0)-\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_\theta}(q_\theta)$. Also $f_{\mathrm{eq}}<f_1$, and
 every $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ has $\theta_f\in(m_0,1)$.
\item As $\theta\downarrow m_0$, $p(\theta)\tof_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and $\zeta_\theta\Rightarrow\zeta_*$.
 There is $\theta_3\in(m_0,1)$ such that, for $m_0<\theta<\theta_3$,
 \[
  \operatorname{supp}\zeta_\theta=\{0\}\cup[q_\theta,v_\theta],\qquad 0<q_\theta<v_\theta<K,\qquad
  \Gamma_\theta'(q_\theta)=\xi''(q_\theta)\mathbb{E} U_{q_\theta}^2=1 .
 \]
 With $f_3=p(\theta_3)>f_{\mathrm{eq}}$, every $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_3)$ has $\theta_f\in(m_0,\theta_3)$, so
 its first positive contact is marginal.
\end{thmlist}

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\xi\in\mathcal{K}_3(\varepsilon_3)$. Since $\xi''(0)>1$ and
$\|\xi-\xi_c\|_{C^4[0,1]}<\varepsilon_3=\varepsilon_1$, the comparison with the critical
reference applies to $\xi$, whatever $\beta_3$: Proposition~\ref{prop:nc-support} and
items~\ref{item:nc-positive} and~\ref{item:nc-confined} of the choice of constants in
Section~\ref{sec:nc-reference}.

(a) By Proposition~\ref{prop:nc-support}(a),
$\xi''>1-\|\xi-\xi_c\|_{C^4[0,1]}>1-\varepsilon_3\ge\frac34$ on $[-1,1]$.

(b) The first assertion is Proposition~\ref{prop:nc-support}(b). Zero is therefore an
accumulation point of the support, and Proposition~\ref{prop:atom-atom}(b) gives
$U_*=a_0^{-1/2}$ and the formula for $m_0$, which is positive since $\beta_3>0$. Also
$m_0<1$, because the open set $(0,v_*)$ meets the support and so has positive mass.
Inserting $U_*=a_0^{-1/2}$ and $\xi'''(0)=2a_0^{3/2}m_0$ into \eqref{eq:atom-odd-D}
gives $6a_0\xi'''(0)m_0U_*^3=3\xi'''(0)^2/a_0^2$ and
$6a_0^3m_0^2U_*^4=\frac32\xi'''(0)^2/a_0^2$, which is the closed form of $D_*$.

(c) For $\theta\le m_0$ the measure $\zeta_*$ is admissible, so $p(\theta)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$, and
uniqueness gives $\zeta_\theta=\zeta_*$. For $m_0<\theta<1$, the activity of the constraint
and $p(\theta)>f_{\mathrm{eq}}$, that is $\widehat{\Lambda}(\theta)>0$, are part of Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-regular},
and so are $f_{\mathrm{eq}}<f_1$ and $\theta_f\in(m_0,1)$, since $m_0<1$ by (b). Let
$\theta\in(m_0,1)$. By Corollary~\ref{cor:cons-level}, which applies since $m_0<1$,
$f=\Lambda'(\theta)$ lies in $(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ and $\theta=\theta_f$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-variational}(e) applies at $\theta$ and gives the first contact
$q_\theta$ with the stated properties, and Proposition~\ref{prop:cons-envelope} gives the
derivative of $p$.

(d) For $\theta>m_0$ the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:atom-slope} gives
$f_{\mathrm{eq}}\le p(\theta)\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}+\frac12\xi''(1)(\theta-m_0)/(1-m_0)$, so $p(\theta)\tof_{\mathrm{eq}}$, and every weak
subsequential limit of $\zeta_\theta$ is $\zeta_*$ by uniqueness; hence
$\zeta_\theta\Rightarrow\zeta_*$.

For $\theta$ close to $m_0$, the positive support of $\zeta_\theta$ has at least two points.
Otherwise, by (c), there would be $\theta_n\downarrow m_0$ with
$\zeta_{\theta_n}=\theta_n\delta_0+(1-\theta_n)\delta_{r_n}$, and a weak limit of the form
$m_0\delta_0+(1-m_0)\delta_r$, which is not $\zeta_*$ by (b). Positive support points of
$\zeta_\theta$ are contacts (Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-variational}(e)), and by
item~\ref{item:nc-confined} they lie in $(0,K)$ and $\zeta_\theta\in\mathcal W$. A gap between
two of them would be a plateau of $\zeta_\theta$ in $(0,K)$ bounded by two contacts, at which
$\Gamma_\theta=\mathrm{id}$ and $\Gamma_\theta'\le1$ by \eqref{eq:plat-contact};
item~\ref{item:nc-positive} and the trapezoid principle exclude it
(Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-gap}(a)). So the positive support is an interval $[r_\theta,v_\theta]$ with
$r_\theta<v_\theta<K$. The first contact satisfies $q_\theta\le r_\theta$. If
$q_\theta<r_\theta$, then $(q_\theta,r_\theta)$ is a support-free interval between two
contacts, excluded in the same way; thus $q_\theta=r_\theta$. Since $\Gamma_\theta=\mathrm{id}$ on
$[q_\theta,v_\theta]$ and $\Gamma_\theta'$ is continuous, $\Gamma_\theta'(q_\theta)=1$. This
holds for $m_0<\theta<\theta_3$ with a suitable $\theta_3\in(m_0,1)$.

Let $f_3=p(\theta_3)$, which exceeds $f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ by (c). Since $p$ is nondecreasing, $p'\ge0$ and
$f_3\le p(\theta_3)+\theta_3p'(\theta_3)=\Lambda'(\theta_3)<f_1$ by the proof of (c). Let
$f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_3)$. As $p$ is nondecreasing and $\overline{\Lambda}(1)=P_{\delta_0}\ge p(s)$ for every
$s$, we have $\overline{\Lambda}(s)-sf\ge s(p(\theta_3)-f)>0$ for $s\in[\theta_3,1]$. Since
$p(s)\tof_{\mathrm{eq}}<f$ as $s\downarrow m_0$, the same quantity is negative for some
$s\in(m_0,\theta_3)$. Hence $\theta_f\in(m_0,\theta_3)$ by (c).

title: Proof
body_md:
Throughout, $m_0<\theta<\theta_3$, $q=q_\theta$, $o(1)$ refers to $\theta\downarrow m_0$, and
$U_t,V_t,W_t$ are built from $\zeta_\theta$.

\emph{Step 1: the third derivative on the left plateau.} Fix $\rho\in(0,v_*)$. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:atom-odd-structure}(b), $\zeta_*((0,\rho))>0$, and weak convergence gives
$\zeta_\theta((0,\rho))>0$ for $\theta$ close to $m_0$. Positive support points are contacts,
so $q_\theta<\rho$. Hence $q_\theta\to0$.

On $[0,q)$ the cumulative mass of $\zeta_\theta$ is exactly $\theta$, so
\eqref{eq:plat-third} holds on $(0,q)$ with $m=\theta$:
\[
 \Gamma_\theta'''=a''\mathbb{E} U^2+3aa'\mathbb{E}\bigl(V^2-2\theta U^3\bigr)
   +a^3\mathbb{E}\bigl(W^2-12\theta UV^2+6\theta^2U^4\bigr).
\]
We claim that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:atom-odd-third}
 \epsilon_\theta:=\sup_{0<t<q_\theta}\bigl|\Gamma_\theta'''(t)-D_*\bigr|\longrightarrow0 .
\end{equation}
Let $F$ be a monomial of degree at most four in $(\Phi_{xx},\Phi_{xxx},\Phi_{xxxx})$, and
write $F_\theta(t,x)$ and $F_*(t,x)$ for its values built from $\zeta_\theta$ and $\zeta_*$. For
$0<t<q$,
\[
 \bigl|\mathbb{E} F_\theta(t,X_t)-F_*(0,0)\bigr|
 \le\|F_\theta-F_*\|_\infty+\mathbb{E}\bigl|F_*(t,X_t)-F_*(t,0)\bigr|+\bigl|F_*(t,0)-F_*(0,0)\bigr| .
\]
The first term is at most $CW_1(\zeta_\theta,\zeta_*)$ by \eqref{eq:plat-jet-stability} and
the bounds \eqref{eq:plat-bounds}, and it tends to zero because
$\zeta_\theta\Rightarrow\zeta_*$. The second is at most $C(\mathbb{E} X_t^2)^{1/2}\le C\sqrt q$ by
\eqref{eq:plat-bounds} and \eqref{eq:plat-small-time}, uniformly in $\theta$. The third is
at most $Cq$ by \eqref{eq:plat-time-lip}. Finally $a,a',a''$ are continuous at zero,
$\Phi_{\zeta_*,xxx}(0,0)=0$ by parity, and $\theta\to m_0$. Therefore $\Gamma_\theta'''$
converges uniformly on $(0,q)$ to
\[
 \xi''''(0)U_*^2+3a_0\xi'''(0)\bigl(-2m_0U_*^3\bigr)
   +a_0^3\bigl(W_*^2+6m_0^2U_*^4\bigr)=D_* ,
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:atom-odd-third}. The interval $(0,q)\subset(0,K)$ is a plateau of
$\zeta_\theta$, and $\zeta_\theta\in\mathcal W$ by item~\ref{item:nc-confined}, so
item~\ref{item:nc-positive} gives $\Gamma_\theta'''\ge2$ there; letting $\theta\downarrow m_0$
in \eqref{eq:atom-odd-third} proves $D_*\ge2$.

\emph{Step 2: three identities.} By Proposition~\ref{prop:atom-odd-structure}(d), every point
of $[q,v_\theta]$ is a support point of $\zeta_\theta$, hence a contact
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-variational}(e)), so $\Gamma_\theta=\mathrm{id}$ on $[q,v_\theta]$
by~\eqref{eq:plat-contact}; and $\zeta_\theta((0,q))=0$. So
Corollary~\ref{cor:plat-first-plateau} applies to $\zeta_\theta$ with $m=\theta$ and
$D=D_*$, and its error parameter is the quantity $\epsilon_\theta$ of
\eqref{eq:atom-odd-third}. Its part~(a), with \eqref{eq:atom-at-zero}, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:atom-odd-Gpp0}
 \Gamma_\theta''(0+)=-\frac{2D_*}3\,q+O(\epsilon_\theta q).
\end{equation}
Next, $\Gamma_\theta'(0)=a_0 \bar U_\theta^2$ by \eqref{eq:atom-at-zero} and
$\Gamma_\theta'(q)=1$, and $\Gamma_\theta''$ extends continuously to $[0,q]$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-kernel}), so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:atom-odd-id2}
 1-a_0 \bar U_\theta^2=\Gamma_\theta'(q)-\Gamma_\theta'(0)
 =q\,\Gamma_\theta''(0+)+\int_0^q(q-s)\,\Gamma_\theta'''(s)\,ds
 =-\frac{D_*}6\,q^2+O(\epsilon_\theta q^2).
\end{equation}
Thus $a_0 \bar U_\theta^2=1+\frac{D_*}6q^2+o(q^2)$, which is (a). Finally,
\eqref{eq:atom-at-zero} for $\zeta_\theta$, whose atom at zero is $\theta$, reads
\begin{equation}\label{eq:atom-odd-id3}
 \Gamma_\theta''(0+)=\xi'''(0)\bar U_\theta^2-2a_0^2\theta \bar U_\theta^3 .
\end{equation}

\emph{Step 3: the onset.} By Proposition~\ref{prop:atom-odd-structure}(b),
$\xi'''(0)=2a_0^{3/2}m_0$, so \eqref{eq:atom-odd-id3} becomes
\[
 \Gamma_\theta''(0+)=2a_0^{3/2}\bar U_\theta^2\bigl(m_0-\theta\sqrt{a_0}\,\bar U_\theta\bigr)
 =-2a_0^{3/2}\bar U_\theta^2(\theta-m_0)
  -2a_0^{3/2}\bar U_\theta^2\,\theta\bigl(\sqrt{a_0}\,\bar U_\theta-1\bigr).
\]
The two leading terms $2a_0^{3/2}\bar U_\theta^2m_0$ and $2a_0^{3/2}\bar U_\theta^2\theta$ cancel
at $\theta=m_0$, and the second term on the right is of the size of
$\sqrt{a_0}\bar U_\theta-1$. This is where (a) is needed: it gives
$\sqrt{a_0}\bar U_\theta-1=O(q^2)$ and $2a_0^{3/2}\bar U_\theta^2=2\sqrt{a_0}(1+O(q^2))$.
Hence
$\Gamma_\theta''(0+)=-2\sqrt{a_0}(\theta-m_0)(1+O(q^2))+O(q^2)$. Comparing with
\eqref{eq:atom-odd-Gpp0},
\[
 2\sqrt{a_0}\,(\theta-m_0)(1+o(1))=\frac{2D_*}3\,q+o(q),
\]
and since $D_*>0$ this gives $q_\theta/(\theta-m_0)\to3\sqrt{a_0}/D_*$, the first
limit in \eqref{eq:atom-odd-onset}. In particular $q_\theta$ is of the order of
$\theta-m_0$.

\emph{Step 4: the atom at the first contact.} Part~(b) of
Corollary~\ref{cor:plat-first-plateau}, which rests on the jump formula \eqref{eq:plat-jump}
and on $\Gamma_\theta'\equiv1$ on $[q,v_\theta]$, gives
$|2a(q)^2\zeta_\theta(\{q\})\mathbb{E} U_q^3-\frac{D_*}3q|\le\frac53\epsilon_\theta q$. As in
Step~1, $a(q)^2\mathbb{E} U_q^3\toa_0^2U_*^3=\sqrt{a_0}$. Therefore
$\zeta_\theta(\{q\})=\frac{D_*}{6\sqrt{a_0}}\,q\,(1+o(1))$, and the first limit in
\eqref{eq:atom-odd-onset} gives the second.

\emph{Step 5: the envelope derivative.} By Proposition~\ref{prop:atom-odd-structure}(c) and
the definition of the obstacle,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:atom-odd-envelope}
 p'(\theta)=\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_\theta}(0)-\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_\theta}(q)=\frac12\int_0^qa(s)h(s)\,ds,
 \qquad h=\Gamma_\theta-\mathrm{id}\ \text{on }[0,q].
\end{equation}
Part~(c) of Corollary~\ref{cor:plat-first-plateau} gives
$|\int_0^qh-D_* q^4/72|\le\epsilon_\theta q^4/72$ and
$|h|\le(\frac{D_*}6+\frac56\epsilon_\theta)q^3$ on $[0,q]$. Also
$|a(s)-a_0|\le\|a'\|_\infty q$ on $[0,q]$. Splitting $a=a_0+(a-a_0)$ in
\eqref{eq:atom-odd-envelope},
\[
 p'(\theta)=\frac{a_0}2\int_0^qh+O(q^5)=\frac{a_0D_*}{144}\,q_\theta^4\,(1+o(1)).
\]
By \eqref{eq:atom-odd-onset}, $q_\theta^4=81a_0^2D_*^{-4}(\theta-m_0)^4(1+o(1))$, so
\[
 p'(\theta)=\frac{9a_0^3}{16D_*^3}\,(\theta-m_0)^4(1+o(1))=5c\,(\theta-m_0)^4(1+o(1)).
\]

\emph{Step 6: integration.} By Step 5 there is $\theta_1\in(m_0,\theta_3)$ with $|p'|\le1$
on $(m_0,\theta_1]$. For $m_0<\eta'<\theta\le\theta_1$, the function $p$ is differentiable on
$[\eta',\theta]$ with bounded derivative, hence absolutely continuous, and
$p(\theta)-p(\eta')=\int_{\eta'}^\theta p'$. Let $\eta'\downarrow m_0$; then $p(\eta')\tof_{\mathrm{eq}}$ by
Proposition~\ref{prop:atom-odd-structure}(d). Writing $p'(s)=5c(s-m_0)^4(1+r(s))$ with
$r(s)\to0$,
\[
 \bigl|p(\theta)-f_{\mathrm{eq}}-c(\theta-m_0)^5\bigr|\le c(\theta-m_0)^5\sup_{m_0<s\le\theta}|r(s)| ,
\]
which is \eqref{eq:atom-odd-p}. Since $\Lambda=\theta p$ and $\theta\to m_0>0$,
\[
 \Lambda(\theta)-\thetaf_{\mathrm{eq}}=\theta\bigl(p(\theta)-f_{\mathrm{eq}}\bigr)=m_0c(\theta-m_0)^5(1+o(1)),
\]
and
$\Lambda'(\theta)-f_{\mathrm{eq}}=(p(\theta)-f_{\mathrm{eq}})+\theta p'(\theta)
=c(\theta-m_0)^5(1+o(1))+5\theta c(\theta-m_0)^4(1+o(1))
=5m_0c(\theta-m_0)^4(1+o(1))$. This is \eqref{eq:atom-odd-Lambda}.

label: eq:atom-odd-S
title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq:atom-exact},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:atom-odd-S}
 \Sigma(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta)=-m_0\delta-S(\delta),\qquad
 S(\delta)=\sup_{0\le u\le1-m_0}\bigl\{u\delta-\widehat{\Lambda}(m_0+u)\bigr\},
\end{equation}
and by \eqref{eq:atom-odd-Lambda}, $\widehat{\Lambda}(m_0+u)=Au^5(1+r(u))$ with $A:=m_0c$ and
$r(u)\to0$ as $u\downarrow0$. For $B>0$ let
$T_B(\delta)=\sup_{u\ge0}\{u\delta-Bu^5\}=\frac45(5B)^{-1/4}\delta^{5/4}$, attained at
$u_B=(\delta/5B)^{1/4}$.

Fix $\varepsilon\in(0,\frac12)$ and choose $\eta\in(0,1-m_0)$ with $|r|\le\varepsilon$ on
$(0,\eta]$; put $c_\eta=\widehat{\Lambda}(m_0+\eta)>0$. For $u\ge\eta$, convexity of $\widehat{\Lambda}$ and
$\widehat{\Lambda}(m_0)=0$ give $\widehat{\Lambda}(m_0+u)\ge(u/\eta)c_\eta$, so $u\delta-\widehat{\Lambda}(m_0+u)<0$ when
$\delta<c_\eta/\eta$. For $u\in[0,\eta]$,
$A(1-\varepsilon)u^5\le\widehat{\Lambda}(m_0+u)\le A(1+\varepsilon)u^5$. Take $\delta$ so small that
$\delta<c_\eta/\eta$ and $u_{A(1-\varepsilon)}\le\eta$. Then also
$u_{A(1+\varepsilon)}\le\eta$, and
\[
 0<T_{A(1+\varepsilon)}(\delta)\le S(\delta)\le T_{A(1-\varepsilon)}(\delta).
\]
Since $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary, $S(\delta)=\frac45(5m_0c)^{-1/4}\delta^{5/4}(1+o(1))$,
which is \eqref{eq:atom-odd-rate}. The closed form follows from
$5m_0c=\frac{9a_0^3m_0}{16D_*^3}$ and $(16/9)^{1/4}=2/\sqrt3$.

For the dual parameter, let $f=f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta$ with $\delta$ as above. Every
$\theta=m_0+u$ with $u\ge\eta$ has
$\widehat{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta\delta\ge-m_0\delta+u(c_\eta/\eta-\delta)>-m_0\delta\ge\Sigma(f)$,
so $\theta_f<m_0+\eta$, and $\theta_f\downarrow m_0$. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:atom-odd-structure}(c), $\theta_f\in(m_0,1)$ and $\Lambda$ is
differentiable at $\theta_f$; an interior minimizer of the convex function
$\vartheta\mapsto\overline{\Lambda}(\vartheta)-\vartheta f$ satisfies $\Lambda'(\theta_f)=f$. By
\eqref{eq:atom-odd-Lambda}, $\delta=5m_0c(\theta_f-m_0)^4(1+o(1))$, which is the asymptotics
of $\theta_f$. For small $\delta$, $\theta_f\in(m_0,\theta_3)$, so $q_f=q_{\theta_f}$ is the
marginal first contact of Proposition~\ref{prop:atom-odd-structure}(d), and
Proposition~\ref{prop:atom-odd-onset}(b) gives the last two assertions.

 \alpha_*(t)=m_0+\rho_* t+o(t)\quad(t\downarrow0),\qquad \rho_*:=\frac{D_*}{2\sqrt{a_0}}

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $U_t,V_t,W_t$ be built from $\zeta_*$, and put $\mathcal U_2(t)=\mathbb{E} U_t^2$,
$\mathcal V_2(t)=\mathbb{E} V_t^2$ and $\mathcal U_3(t)=\mathbb{E} U_t^3$. For $0\le s\le t\le1$,
\begin{gather*}
 \mathcal U_2(t)-\mathcal U_2(s)=\int_s^ta\,\mathbb{E}\bigl(V_r^2-2\alpha_*(r)U_r^3\bigr)\,dr,\qquad
 \mathcal V_2(t)-\mathcal V_2(s)=\int_s^ta\,\mathbb{E}\bigl(W_r^2-6\alpha_*(r)U_rV_r^2\bigr)\,dr,\\
 \mathcal U_3(t)-\mathcal U_3(s)=\int_s^t3a\,\mathbb{E}\bigl(U_rV_r^2-\alpha_*(r)U_r^4\bigr)\,dr .
\end{gather*}
For measures with finitely many atoms these follow from It\^o's formula on each plateau,
where $dU_t=-ma U_t^2\,dt+\sqrt a\,V_t\,dB_t$ and
$dV_t=-3maU_tV_t\,dt+\sqrt a\,W_t\,dB_t$, and from continuity across the atoms; in general
they follow by approximation, using \eqref{eq:plat-jet-stability} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-coupling}, as in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:ons-equilibrium}.
In the notation \eqref{eq:plat-NS}, write $N=N_{\zeta_*}=a'\mathcal U_2+a^2\mathcal V_2$ and
$\sigma=\sigma_{\zeta_*}=2a^2\mathcal U_3$; here $\sigma>0$ because
$\mathcal U_3\ge\mathcal U_2^{3/2}>0$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:atom-odd-structure}(b) and
Lemma~\ref{lem:ons-zero-in-support}, $\Gamma_*=\mathrm{id}$ on $[0,v_*]$, so $\Gamma_*'\equiv1$ on $[0,v_*)$ and the right derivative of
$\Gamma_*'$ vanishes there. By Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-ito}(b) this right derivative is
$N(t)-\alpha_*(t)\sigma(t)$, so
\[
 \alpha_*(t)=\frac{N(t)}{\sigma(t)}\qquad(0\le t<v_*).
\]
The integrands above are right continuous at $r=0$, so $\mathcal U_2$, $\mathcal V_2$ and
$\mathcal U_3$ have right derivatives at zero. With $X_0=0$, $V_0=0$, $\alpha_*(0)=m_0$ and
$a'(0)=\xi'''(0)$,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 N(0)=a'(0)U_*^2,\qquad
 N'(0+)=a''(0)U_*^2-2a_0 a'(0)m_0U_*^3+a_0^3W_*^2,\\
 \sigma(0)=2a_0^2U_*^3,\qquad
 \sigma'(0+)=4a_0 a'(0)U_*^3-6a_0^3m_0U_*^4 .
 \end{gathered}
\]
Hence $N(0)/\sigma(0)=m_0$, and the right derivative of $\alpha_*$ at zero is
\[
 \frac{N'(0+)-m_0\sigma'(0+)}{\sigma(0)}
 =\frac{a''(0)U_*^2-6a_0 a'(0)m_0U_*^3+a_0^3(W_*^2+6m_0^2U_*^4)}
       {2a_0^2U_*^3}
 =\frac{D_*}{2a_0^2U_*^3}=\frac{D_*}{2\sqrt{a_0}} .
\]
The two consequences follow from \eqref{eq:atom-odd-onset} and \eqref{eq:atom-odd-D}.

title: Proof
body_md:
All derivatives of $\xi$ are nonnegative and nondecreasing on $[0,1]$. Since $\xi_c''\equiv1$
and $\xi_c'''=\xi_c''''\equiv0$, the $C^4$ condition gives $|a-1|<\varepsilon$,
$0\le\xi'''<\varepsilon$ and $0\le\xi''''<\varepsilon$ on $[0,1]$. This gives (i), because
$a_0>1$ and $a$ is nondecreasing. Since $\xi'''(0)=6\beta_3^2=0$,
$a'(t)=\int_0^t\xi''''\le\varepsilon t$ and $a(t)-a_0=\int_0^ta'\le\varepsilon t^2/2$,
which is (ii). For (iii), compare the series termwise: for $p\ge5$ and $0\le t\le\frac12$,
$(p-4)t^{p-5}\le(p-4)2^{5-p}\le1$, so
\[
 \xi^{(5)}(t)=\sum_{p\ge5}\beta_p^2\,p(p-1)(p-2)(p-3)(p-4)\,t^{p-5}
 \le\sum_{p\ge4}\beta_p^2\,p(p-1)(p-2)(p-3)=\xi''''(1)<\varepsilon .
\]
Then $a'(t)-\xi''''(0)t=\int_0^t\int_0^s\xi^{(5)}$ gives the second bound. For (iv),
$\xi'(q)=\int_0^qa=q\ell(q)$, and Fubini's theorem gives
$\xi''(q)-\ell(q)=\int_0^1\int_{sq}^q\xi'''(u)\,du\,ds=q\,\chi(q)$. Differentiation under the
integral gives $\ell^{(j)}(q)=\int_0^1s^j\xi^{(j+2)}(sq)\,ds$ and
$\chi^{(j)}(q)=\int_0^1v^{j+1}\xi^{(j+3)}(vq)\,dv$, and the bounds follow from (i)--(iii). The
values at zero use $\xi'''(0)=0$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:nc-class}(b), \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ holds, so $\zeta_*(\{0\})=0$ by
Proposition~\ref{prop:ons-equilibrium}(b), and at every $\theta\in(0,1)$
Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-variational}(c),(e) applies: $\zeta_\theta(\{0\})=\theta$, and $C_\theta$ is a nonempty compact
subset of $(0,1)$ that contains $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_\theta\cap(0,1]$. By item~\ref{item:nc-confined} of
the choice of constants in Section~\ref{sec:nc-reference}, $\zeta_\theta\in\mathcal W$ and
$C_\theta\subset(0,K)$. Every point of $C_\theta$ is a global, hence local, minimum point of
$\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_\theta}$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-gap}(a) gives $\zeta_\theta((u,v))>0$ whenever
$u<v$ lie in $C_\theta$.

First, $C_\theta$ is an interval. Otherwise some $t\in(q_\theta,\max C_\theta)$ is not in
$C_\theta$; then $u=\max(C_\theta\cap[q_\theta,t])$ and $v=\min(C_\theta\cap[t,1])$ satisfy
$u<t<v$ and $(u,v)\cap C_\theta=\emptyset$, so $\zeta_\theta((u,v))=0$, a contradiction. Write
$C_\theta=[q_\theta,v_\theta]$. Second, $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_\theta\cap(0,1]=C_\theta$. The positive
support is contained in $C_\theta$. If $q_\theta<v_\theta$, every interval with endpoints in
$C_\theta$ has positive mass, so every point of $(q_\theta,v_\theta)$, and by closedness every
point of $C_\theta$, is a support point. If $q_\theta=v_\theta$, the positive support is
nonempty, because $\zeta_\theta((0,1])=1-\theta>0$, and is contained in $\{q_\theta\}$. Since
$\zeta_\theta(\{0\})=\theta>0$, this proves $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_\theta=\{0\}\cup[q_\theta,v_\theta]$
and the two-atom form when $v_\theta=q_\theta$. Finally let $q_\theta<v_\theta$. Every
$t\in[q_\theta,v_\theta]\subset(0,1)$ is a minimum point of $\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_\theta}$, so
$\Gamma_\theta(t)=t$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-obstacle}(b). Since $\Gamma_\theta$ is $C^1$,
$\Gamma_\theta'(q_\theta)=1$, that is,
$\xi''(q_\theta)\mathbb{E}\Phi_{\zeta_\theta,xx}(q_\theta,X_{q_\theta})^2=1$.

label: lem:C-two-atom
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:C-two-atom}
Let $\xi(t)=\sum_{p\ge2}\beta_p^2t^p$ have radius of convergence greater than one and
$\beta_2>0$, let $\theta\in[0,1]$ and $r\in(0,1)$, and let $X$ be the diffusion
\eqref{eq:intro-diffusion} of $\zeta^{\theta,r}$. Then
\[
 \Gamma^{\theta,r}(r)=\mathfrak{T}\bigl(\xi'(r),\theta\bigr),\qquad
 (\Gamma^{\theta,r})'(r)=\xi''(r)\,\mathbb{E}\Phi_{\zeta^{\theta,r},xx}(r,X_r)^2
 =\xi''(r)\,\mathfrak{S}\bigl(\xi'(r),\theta\bigr),
\]
and the right second derivative satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C-right-second}
 (\Gamma^{\theta,r})''(r+)\le\xi'''(r)+\xi''(r)^2\bigl(10\,\Gamma^{\theta,r}(r)-2\bigr).
\end{equation}
head: environment
name: Two-atom measures

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\Phi=\Phi_{\zeta^{\theta,r}}$. On $[r,1]$ the distribution function equals one, and
$\Phi(t,x)=\log\cosh x+\frac12(\xi'(1)-\xi'(t))$ solves the Parisi equation
\eqref{eq:intro-pde} there, because $\operatorname{sech}^2+\tanh^2=1$. Hence $\Phi_x(r,\cdot)=\tanh$,
$U:=\Phi_{xx}(r,\cdot)=\operatorname{sech}^2$ and $V:=\Phi_{xxx}(r,\cdot)=-2\operatorname{sech}^2\tanh$. The measure has
no mass in $(0,r)$ and mass $\theta$ at zero, so by \eqref{eq:plat-law} the law of $X_r$ has
density proportional to $e^{\theta\Phi(r,y)}\propto\cosh^\theta y$ with respect to
$\mathcal N(0,\xi'(r))$. Since a probability density integrates to one,
$\mathbb{E} F(X_r)=\mathbb{E}_{\xi'(r),\theta}F$ for every continuous $F$ with $|F(x)|\le Ce^{|x|}$. Taking
$F=\tanh^2$ gives the first identity. The second follows from
$(\Gamma^{\theta,r})'(r)=\xi''(r)\mathbb{E} U(X_r)^2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-ito}(a)) with
$U^2=\operatorname{sech}^4$.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:plat-ito}(b), the right derivative of $(\Gamma^{\theta,r})'$ at $r$ carries
the mass $\zeta^{\theta,r}([0,r])=1$:
\[
 (\Gamma^{\theta,r})''(r+)=\xi'''(r)\,\mathbb{E} U(X_r)^2+\xi''(r)^2\,\mathbb{E}\bigl(V(X_r)^2-2U(X_r)^3\bigr).
\]
Now $U^2\le1$, $V^2=4\operatorname{sech}^4\tanh^2\le4\tanh^2$, and
$U^3=(1-\tanh^2)^3\ge1-3\tanh^2$, because $(1-y)^3-(1-3y)=y^2(3-y)\ge0$ for $y\in[0,1]$.
Since $\mathbb{E}\tanh^2X_r=\Gamma^{\theta,r}(r)$ and $\xi'''\ge0$ on $[0,1]$ (the coefficients of
$\xi$ are nonnegative), this proves \eqref{eq:C-right-second}.

label: lem:C-rs
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:C-rs}
Let $\overline C\ge1$ be the absolute constant of Lemma~\ref{lem:dat-branch}, and put
$K_{\rm rs}=\min\{\frac14,1/(2\overline C)\}$ and
$\tau_0=\min\{\frac12K_{\rm rs},1/(12\overline C^2)\}$. There is an absolute constant $C$ such
that the following holds for every $\xi\in\mathcal{K}(\frac14)$ with $\tau=a_0-1\le\tau_0$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item For each $\theta\in[0,1]$ the equation $q=\mathfrak{T}(\xi'(q),\theta)$ has exactly one solution
 $q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta$ in $(0,K_{\rm rs}]$. It satisfies $\tau/\overline C\leq^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta\le2\tau$, and
 $\theta\mapstoq^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta$ is continuously differentiable on $[0,1]$ \textup{(}one-sided at
 the endpoints\textup{)}.
\item Put $\mathfrak A(\theta)=\xi''(q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta)\,\mathfrak{S}(\xi'(q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta),\theta)$. Then
 $\mathfrak A(\theta)-1=q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta\,\mathfrak W(\theta)$ with
 $\mathfrak W(\theta)=\varpi(q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta,\theta)$; $\mathfrak W$ is strictly decreasing on
 $[0,1]$, $\mathfrak W(0)>0$ and $\mathfrak W(1)<0$. Hence there is a unique
 $\theta_c\in(0,1)$ with $\mathfrak A>1$ on $[0,\theta_c)$, $\mathfrak A(\theta_c)=1$ and
 $\mathfrak A<1$ on $(\theta_c,1]$.
\item $\bigl|\theta_c-\frac23\bigl(1+\frac14\xi''''(0)\bigr)\tau\bigr|\le C\tau^2$.
\end{thmlist}

name: The replica-symmetric branch

label: lem:C-sufficiency
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:C-sufficiency}
Let $\xi\in\mathcal{K}(\varepsilon_*)$, $\theta\in(0,1)$ and $r\in(0,2\tau]$, write
$\zeta=\zeta^{\theta,r}$ and $h(t)=\Gamma^{\theta,r}(t)-t$, and assume $h(r)=0$ and
$h'(r)\le0$. Then $h>0$ on $(0,r)$ and $h<0$ on $(r,1]$. Consequently

head: environment
name: Sufficiency of the de Almeida--Thouless condition

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\xi\in\mathcal{K}(\varepsilon_*)$, so that \ref{item:dat-C1}--\ref{item:dat-C4} hold.

\emph{Parts~(a), (b) and~(e).} By \ref{item:dat-C1}, Lemma~\ref{lem:C-rs} applies to $\xi$.
Its part~(a) gives~(a), with the absolute constant $K_{\rm rs}\in(0,\frac14]$; its part~(b)
gives~(b); and its part~(c) is \eqref{eq:nc-dat-asymptotics}, with an absolute constant $C$.

\emph{Part~(c).} Let $0<\theta<\theta_c$, so that $\mathfrak A(\theta)>1$. By
\ref{item:dat-C2}, Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-regular} applies: the positive contact set of
$\zeta_\theta$ is an interval $[q_\theta,v_\theta]\subset(0,K)$, and
$\operatorname{supp}\zeta_\theta=\{0\}\cup[q_\theta,v_\theta]$. Suppose that $v_\theta=q_\theta$, and put
$r=q_\theta$. Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-regular} then gives $\zeta_\theta=\zeta^{\theta,r}$. As in the
proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-regular}, Lemma~\ref{lem:cons-variational}(e) applies to
$\theta$, and the contact conditions \eqref{eq:cons-contact} at the first positive contact give
$\Gamma^{\theta,r}(r)=r$ and $(\Gamma^{\theta,r})'(r)\le1$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:C-two-atom} the
first condition says $r=\mathfrak{T}(\xi'(r),\theta)$. Since $0<r<K\le K_{\rm rs}$ by
\ref{item:dat-C1}, the uniqueness in~(a) gives $r=q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta$, and then the second condition
says $\mathfrak A(\theta)\le1$, a contradiction. Hence $v_\theta>q_\theta$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-regular}, $\Gamma_\theta(t)=t$ on $[q_\theta,v_\theta]$ and the first positive
contact is marginal, that is,
$\xi''(q_\theta)\mathbb{E}\Phi_{\zeta_\theta,xx}(q_\theta,X_{q_\theta})^2=\Gamma_\theta'(q_\theta)=1$;
moreover $0<q_\theta<v_\theta<K\le\frac1{20}$.

\emph{Part~(d).} Let $\theta_c\le\theta<1$, so that $\theta>0$, and put
$r=q^{\mathrm{rs}}_\theta\in(0,2\tau]$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:C-two-atom} and~(a),
$\Gamma^{\theta,r}(r)=\mathfrak{T}(\xi'(r),\theta)=r$ and
$(\Gamma^{\theta,r})'(r)=\mathfrak A(\theta)\le1$, with equality only for $\theta=\theta_c$,
by~(b). In the notation of Lemma~\ref{lem:C-sufficiency}, $h(r)=0$ and $h'(r)\le0$, so that
lemma gives $\zeta_\theta=\zeta^{\theta,r}$ with positive contact set $\{r\}$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:C-two-atom}, the Plefka quantity \eqref{eq:intro-plefka} at this contact is
\[
 1-\xi''(r)\,\mathbb{E}\Phi_{\zeta_\theta,xx}(r,X_r)^2=1-(\Gamma^{\theta,r})'(r)=1-\mathfrak A(\theta),
\]
which vanishes at $\theta=\theta_c$ and is positive for $\theta>\theta_c$, by~(b).
